item.title: Legislative Auditor Mid East Tennessee
item.description: Legislative Auditor: Mid-east Tennessee Location: Mid-east Tennessee (Putnam, Cumberland, White, Van Buren, Bledsoe, and Warren counties) Join us in our mission to make government work better. Role Snapshot This position conducts external audits for local government entities in the Mid-east Tennessee region, ensuring accountability, transparency, and effective operations across publicly funded organizations. Responsibilities may include examining and reviewing records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for state and local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Why You'll Love This Job Meaningful work that impacts communities across Tennessee Flexible schedules and a standard 37.5-hour workweek Opportunities for professional growth and development Collaborative and supportive team environment Comprehensive benefits and work-life balance What You'll Do Conduct audits of state and local governmental entities in accordance with professional auditing standards. Examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices. Evaluate financial statement presentation, internal controls, compliance, and operational efficiency and effectiveness. Produce clear, logical, and well-supported workpapers and data analyses. Communicate clearly with auditees, coworkers, elected officials, and stakeholders. Take initiative, seek continuous improvement, and contribute to a collaborative team culture. What We're Looking For Required: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Business Administration with at least 24 semester hours in accounting Ability to learn quickly, think critically, problem solve, and produce accurate work Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Clear written and verbal communication skills Ability to work tactfully with coworkers, auditees, and stakeholders Sound judgment in evaluating situations and making decisions Preferred: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license (not required but strongly encouraged for advancement) Experience in auditing, governmental accounting, or related fields Logistics Travel: For Local Government Auditors, travel is required but is generally confined to same day commutes to and from a job site. Overnight stays may be required, as necessary. Compensation: Competitive salary and benefits, including annual and sick leave, insurance plans, pension, 401(k), college fee waivers, and flexible schedules. About the Office The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury audits state and local government entities and oversees financial and administrative management of state government. We are nationally recognized for professionalism and accountability and consistently rank as a Top Workplace. Learn more at www.comptroller.tn.gov Equal Opportunity Employer We are committed to fair and equal employment opportunities and maintaining a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, religion, disability, veteran status, or any category protected by law. NOTICE This position requires a criminal background check. You may be required to provide information about your criminal history to be considered for this position. Texting TOS and Privacy Policy: Message type: informational; you will receive text messages regarding your application and potentially regarding interview scheduling. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text "STOP" to the short code. After you send the SMS message "STOP" to us, we will send you an SMS message to confirm that you have been unsubscribed. After this, you will no longer receive SMS messages from us. If you want to join again, just sign up as you did the first time and we will start sending SMS messages to you again. If you are experiencing issues with the messaging program, you can reply with the keyword HELP for more assistance, or you can get help directly at ig.askhr@cot.tn.gov . Message frequency will vary depending on the application process. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. Msg & data rates may apply. If you have any questions about your text plan or data plan, it is best to contact your wireless provider. If you have any questions regarding privacy, please read our privacy policy below. Privacy Policy: We collect your mobile number and related opt-in data for the delivery of SMS messages. Your mobile opt-in data and consent will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

item.title: Franklin County Election Canvasser
item.description: The Opportunity Down Home North Carolina (DHNC) seeks field canvassers in Franklin County to aid in our 2026 field campaigns. This year, Down Home members will endorse multiple candidates for office who align with our values and vision for a North Carolina that works for all working folks. Down Home is working to engage voters in our small towns this year to inform them about the upcoming elections, when, where, and how they can vote, and recruit more folks into our movement. Opportunities are available in the following counties: Ashe, Alamance, Cabarrus, Chatham, Franklin, Granville, Iredell, Johnson, Nash, Orange, Person, Pitt, Randolph, Rowan, Rockingham, Vance, Watauga, and Wilson. The ideal candidate is a people-person motivated to build a powerful multiracial base that wins changes for poor and working-class people in rural North Carolina. They have excellent listening skills, are team players and independent workers, and are aligned with Down Home's mission. The Work Have conversations with community members through door-to-door canvassing Participate in 4 to 6 canvasses per week Ensure that data and information collection are consistent and accurate Troubleshooting issues within the program Must be willing to work in a team-centered environment. Required Traits Excellent communication and listening skills: Can engage deeply with people they have just met. Be able to listen to community members and understand their concerns. Can build rapport quickly and is comfortable having relational conversations. Team player: Contribute to a growing and fast-paced team. Take directions well and be willing to offer feedback and suggestions to co-workers and management. Offer support to teammates and ask for help when needed. Independent worker: Be able to complete multiple canvass shifts a week. Meet deadlines and hit metric goals. Ensure that numbers are reported on time with data integrity at the top of mind. Attention to detail and be able to provide thoughtful solutions to problems that arise. Be able to work in a fast-paced environment where work areas are expected to change frequently. Mission alignment: Committed to the vision of a powerful, inclusive, rural, multiracial, working-class movement-building as a path towards liberation for all people. Is aligned with the idea that building power takes both election programs and long-term base-building and community investment. Compensation Compensation for this contract position is $22 hourly. Hours are flexible, with shifts available during the afternoon and evening. This role is not eligible for employee-sponsored benefits or healthcare. Applicants must be able and willing to travel regularly for work. How to Apply Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis if spots are available. We will still accept applications if this job description is posted on Down Home’s website (www.downhomenc.org).

item.title: Summer Associate Internship Public Policy Assistant
item.description: Description The Summer Associate Program is a 12-week internship program beginning in May 2027 and ending in August 2027. Students will work on impactful projects and meaningful work during their internship. To qualify for this position, applicants must be currently pursuing a degree from an accredited college or university and have an anticipated graduation date of December 2027 or later. As part of Navy Federal's Military Affairs & Strategic Partnerships (MA&SP) department, GRPP collaborates closely with business units across the enterprise to assess policy implications, support strategic decision-making, and represent Navy Federal's interests before policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. The Public Policy Assistant Summer Associate will support the team's policy research, reporting, and operational activities. The associate will help maintain legislative, regulatory, stakeholder engagement, and project-tracking efforts that support the team's advocacy and strategic priorities. Responsibilities may include data analysis, reporting, process improvement, policy research, and the development of materials that help inform decision-making and increase visibility into GRPP activities across the enterprise. This role will provide exposure to public policy, government relations, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional collaboration. Potential Projects Include: Support the collection, organization, and analysis of data related to legislative, regulatory, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and project activities. Assist in preparing weekly, monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc reports, executive summaries, briefing materials, and presentations for senior leadership and internal stakeholders. Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations that provide insights into policy developments, advocacy activities, stakeholder engagement, and team performance metrics. Support the tracking and management of team projects, action items, external engagements, and strategic initiatives to improve visibility and operational efficiency. Conduct research on federal and state legislative proposals, regulatory actions, and emerging public policy issues affecting credit unions, financial services, and military-affiliated communities. Perform industry benchmarking and trend analysis to support advocacy priorities and strategic planning efforts. Assist with preparing background materials, stakeholder summaries, and briefing documents for meetings with policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and internal business partners. Collaborate with business units across the enterprise to gather information and support policy-related initiatives and reporting. Complete a capstone project focused on improving GRPP's reporting, knowledge management, or operational processes, resulting in recommendations and tools that create long-term value for the team. Responsibilities Support the monitoring and tracking of legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments relevant to Navy Federal and the credit union industry. Conduct research and gather information from legislative, regulatory, industry, and internal sources to support policy analysis and advocacy efforts. Assist with maintaining records of team activities, stakeholder engagements, policy developments, and strategic initiatives. Compile, organize, and analyze data to support team reporting, metrics, and leadership updates. Prepare presentations, briefing materials, summaries, and reports for internal stakeholders and senior leadership. Support project management activities by tracking action items, milestones, and deliverables across multiple initiatives. Collaborate with business units and internal partners to collect information and support cross-functional projects. Help identify opportunities to improve team processes, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Demonstrated interest in public policy, government, financial services, advocacy, or related fields. Experience conducting research, analyzing information, or preparing reports and presentations through coursework, internships, student organizations, or other experiences. Familiarity with data analysis, reporting, data visualization, or business intelligence concepts. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience using Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint to organize information and communicate findings. Ability to synthesize complex information into concise summaries and recommendations. Experience balancing multiple projects, priorities, or extracurricular commitments. Interest in legislative affairs, regulatory issues, government relations, military affairs, consumer financial services, or the credit union industry. Demonstrated leadership through student organizations, volunteer activities, community involvement, athletics, military service, or other experiences. item.title: Legislative Affairs Coordinator
item.description: BATTERY COUNCIL INTERNATIONAL Legislative Affairs Coordinator Full-time · Washington, DC area required (work from home within the DC area) · Reports to the VP, Government Relations & Sustainability Salary range: $70,000–$90,000, plus bonus and benefits About BCI Battery Council International is the century-old trade association for the North American battery industry. We lead the industry’s federal and state advocacy on recycling, extended producer responsibility, transport, and safety, alongside our technical, data, and sustainability programs. We are a small, remote team, and we are building our state and federal advocacy capability in-house. The role This is the engine room of our advocacy program. You will track what is happening in legislatures across the country, flag what matters, and help BCI act on it. You will also assist with federal matters when state sessions quiet down in the second half of the year. It is a great role for someone early in a government-affairs career who wants real ownership and a national view of policy. What you’ll do Track fifty-state activity — monitor legislation and regulation affecting the battery industry across all states via BCI’s tracking database, and keep a current, reliable picture of what is moving. Watch the federal side — review the Federal Register daily for regulatory actions affecting the industry, follow federal legislation, and keep an eye on industry listservs. Summarize and report — turn developments into concise summaries and tracking reports, and maintain an ongoing issues-management report for the team and members. Write it up — draft articles and updates on policy issues for BCI’s digital publications and website. Support state outreach — help advance BCI’s policy priorities and coordinate with members and allied organizations. Back up federal advocacy — lend a hand on federal work as needed. What you bring A bachelor’s degree in political science, energy, public policy, related field, or equivalent experience. Roughly two to five years of experience in government affairs, legislative tracking, policy research, or a closely related field — strong internship experience considered for early-career candidates. Familiarity with how state (and ideally federal) legislative and regulatory processes work. Sharp research and writing, strong organization, and real attention to detail across a high volume of material. The self-direction to manage a broad workload well on a home-based, distributed team. Nice to have Exposure to environmental, recycling, product-stewardship, or manufacturing policy. Experience with a legislative-tracking platform (Bloomberg Government, Politico, or similar) and with coalition work. What we offer Competitive pay in the range above, plus an annual bonus. A 5% 401(k) match and medical, dental, and vision coverage. Paid time off and a work-from-home schedule based in the DC area, with occasional travel and in-person meetings. A national view of policy and genuine ownership of BCI’s state program, early in your career. Exposure to international policy and global battery-association work. How to apply Submit a resume and cover letter. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the position is open until filled. Please tell us where in the DC area you are based. Equal opportunity BCI is an equal-opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to an inclusive hiring process and will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities on request at any stage. Contact [email protected] to request accommodations. Battery Council International · batterycouncil.org · The salary range reflects the band for this role; the actual offer depends on experience and work location under BCI’s geographic pay framework.

item.title: Political Science Faculty Member
item.description: $58,722 - $70,786 USD yearly About Holyoke Community College: Holyoke Community College is housed on a multi-million-dollar, 135-acre campus, equipped with state-of-the art technology in specialized learning facilities. HCC serves over 9,000 students annually, and provides a variety of recreational and cultural activities, from sports programs to music festivals, for students and community members alike. The college's strongest assets continue to be an innovative spirit, a sincere concern for students and a commitment to strive for even greater success. These are the values which have created a tradition of excellence spanning more than six decades, and which are enabling Holyoke Community College to meet today's challenges. Mission : Educate. Inspire. Connect. Values: Kindness, Inclusion, Trust, Innovation & Collaboration Kindness, inclusion and trust are the foundation of the work that we do together. Innovation and collaboration enable us to explore and implement the ideas that will shape our future. The Critical Social Thought (CST) Department at Holyoke Community College seeks a full-time tenure-track faculty member to bring vision and innovation to Political Science courses within the department’s CST Option. We seek candidates who will bring a broad grounding in US Political Science to the department, and who can enhance our course offerings with specialized areas of expertise. Candidates with research or teaching in US National Politics, State and Local Politics, Civics, Civil Liberties, Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics are particularly encouraged to apply. Our ideal candidate will continue the department’s tradition of interdisciplinary teaching with colleagues across campus and engaging with the external community via community-based learning. As part of the college’s efforts to ensure equitable outcomes for all HCC students, candidates must bring a demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in their teaching practice, as well as a record of excellence in college-level instruction. Primary responsibilities include: teaching lecture classes on general US Political Science topics as well as electives that serve the needs of students in our program as well as other degree programs; strengthening the ongoing development of our CST academic program via assessment and curriculum development; participating in college governance, recruitment and retention efforts; and professional development. In addition to teaching experience, candidates should also demonstrate a commitment to student-centered advising, and to building partnerships that will enhance students’ opportunities for career and transfer. Such partnerships may include internal collaborations with colleagues in the CST department and in the Latinx Studies program as well as external collaborations to expand career and transfer opportunities for students who major in CST and Latinx programs. Although hybrid teaching options may be available, this position will require a substantial amount of in-person, on-campus work with students, faculty, and community partners. Teaching US Political Science lecture courses, in particular general US National as well as State and Local Politics surveys, and courses that address specific subfields in Political Science relevant to the faculty member’s expertise. Ability to teach Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics is of particular interest. Working closely with colleagues in Critical Social Thought Department and across campus, develop innovative teaching methods; expand community-engaged learning initiatives; continue a commitment to innovative, inclusive, discovery-based and critically engaged curricula; incorporate technology in the classroom; develop and implement new courses as appropriate that serve the students’ academic needs, and strengthen the ongoing development of our CST academic program. Advising students in the CST program and related majors. Meeting with and assisting students during regular office hours. Actively participating in department, division, and professional staff meetings as well as other components of college governance. Maintaining professional expertise in areas of specialization. Participating in college programs and activities. Assisting the Dean, Associate Dean, and Chair of the Critical Social Thought Department to establish and maintain existing academic partnerships with related college programs as well as expand articulation agreements with external college and university programs. Providing college service as required by the MCCC contract, including participation in shared governance committees, sub-committees, or task forces. Minimum Qualifications: Master’s degree in Political Science or closely related field, with the ability to teach standard survey courses (US National, State and Local Government, Civil Liberties) as well as specialized courses within US Political Science and across disciplines; Teaching experience in higher education, specifically as instructor of record; Demonstrated excellent teaching skills including interactive teaching, varied pedagogical strategies, and culturally responsive pedagogies; Experience using instructional technology across teaching modalities (i.e. in physical, hybrid, and online classes) to enable student success; Experience working successfully with a diverse student body, staff, and faculty; Effective communication skills and ability to work collaboratively on projects and initiatives. Equivalency Statement: We welcome and encourage applicants who do not meet the qualifications as stated above, to put in writing precisely how their background and experience have prepared them for the responsibilities of this position. It is preferred that this document be uploaded separately from the resume, cover letter, and references. Preferred Qualifications: A record of teaching excellence in Political Science at a community college or at the first year/sophomore college level; Ph. D in Political Science or closely related field; Interest in promoting and participating in interdisciplinary learning; Ability to provide leadership within an academic department that will contribute to growth, innovation, and excellence in alignment with institutional goals; Bilingual (English/Spanish). Full-Time, Tenure-Track MCCC/MTA Position: Salary Range: $58,722.00 - $70,786.00. Actual salary will be commensurate with education and experience in accordance with MCCC/MTA Collective Bargaining Agreement. Full State benefits. Funding: State. Start Date: Fall, 2027. Additional Details: Applicants must include a CV, cover letter, and syllabus in one of the following areas: US National Government, State & Local Government, or Civil Liberties. A teaching demonstration is a required part of the interview process. Disability Accommodations: Holyoke Community College is committed to the full inclusion of individuals with disabilities and will ensure the availability of reasonable accommodations. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact the Office of People and Talent at (413) 552-2554. Background Check: Employment is contingent upon the successful completion and review of a background check which will include CORI (Criminal Offender Record Information) and SORI (Sex Offender Registry Information). All candidates must have legal authorization to work in the United States. HCC is not sponsoring H1B Visa. Holyoke Community College is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, age, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity or sexual orientation in its programs and activities as required by Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and other applicable statutes and college policies. The College prohibits sexual harassment, including sexual violence. Inquiries or complaints concerning discrimination, harassment, retaliation or sexual violence shall be referred to the College’s Affirmative Action and/or Title IX Coordinator, the Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination, the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission or the United States Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights. Holyoke, Massachusetts, United States $58,722 - $70,786 USD yearly

item.title: Vp Government Affairs
item.description: Tinker Federal Credit Union’s Risk department has an immediate opening for a Vice President of Government Affairs! This is an exciting opportunity to join one of the nation’s leading credit unions! We offer competitive pay, a robust benefits package, a “smart casual dress code” and much more! We want you to work and grow at TFCU, so there will be many opportunities for professional development and growth through training and continued education. We value you at TFCU! As a Vice President of Government Affairs, you will be responsible for the following: Manages TFCU’s Government Affairs function and is accountable for developing, recommending, and executing the organization’s legislative, regulatory, and political engagement strategy. Evaluates emerging public policy developments, advises leadership regarding organizational risks and opportunities, and manages the relationships, programs, resources, and external partners necessary to advance TFCU’s approved advocacy priorities. Salary Range: This is an exempt position. The starting salary range is $161,544-$201,930; however, actual placement within the range will be determined individually based on your experience relative to organizational needs and internal salary equity. Schedule: Normally works a weekday schedule, but may be required to work evenings, holidays, or weekends. Required to travel, including overnight travel, with or without advance notice Education/Experience: You must have a bachelor's degree in government, business, public policy, political science, or a related field. At least six years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, lobbying, legislative affairs, regulatory policy, or public policy management is required, including experience managing significant programs, external partners, or cross-functional initiatives. Experience advising senior leadership and representing an organization before elected officials, regulators, or industry associations is required Certificates, Licenses, Registrations: Incumbent Bonding REQUIRED by TFCU’s chosen authority. Valid driver’s license, maintaining an acceptable Motor Vehicle Record. Registered federal lobbyist, or ability to register under the Lobbying Disclosure Act within 90 days of hire, is required. Ability and willingness to register as an Oklahoma state lobbyist is also required. Keys to success: In order to be successful as a Vice President of Government Affairs you must possess these qualifications: Ability to translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into concise organizational impact assessments and actionable recommendations. Ability to manage budgets, contracts, consultants, vendors, and multiple concurrent advocacy initiatives. Ability to exercise judgment and represent TFCU’s approved positions within established executive direction and delegated authority. Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes and lead cross-functional work without direct reporting authority. Advanced knowledge of lobbying, ethics, disclosure, campaign-finance, PAC, and related compliance requirements. Ability to develop executive and board-level briefings regarding legislative, regulatory, and political developments. Proven ability to develop and maintain strong working relationships with national and state leaders, internal and external stakeholders, and employees at all organizational levels. Ability and willingness to travel for work assignments, including out-of-state travel, which may occur as frequently as quarterly or more often depending on business needs, and to work varied hours as needed. Proficiency in financial services, business, and project management software.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: $145,000 - $155,000 USD yearly Position Summary CFR’s Government Affairs operation is focused on actively engaging members of Congress and their staff, executive branch officials, and Washington, DC-based diplomats to provide timely, relevant, and useful analysis to further inform policymaking. Through discussion and examination of the critical challenges facing the United States and the international community, the program seeks to serve as both a direct resource and convener of leading thinkers and practitioners in a nonpartisan forum. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC at least four days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Help craft and set strategy for outreach to members of Congress and congressional staff in innovative and policy relevant ways. Maintain a professional network on Capitol Hill and leverage that network to advance institutional priorities. Moderate and oversee some program events, roundtables, and briefings for policymakers and their staff. Coordinate private consultations for members of Congress and their staff to ensure CFR expertise and products are incorporated into the policymaking process. Develop and implement unique and custom outreach strategies for CFR initiatives and other bespoke institutional priorities. Invite and oversee relationships with outside experts participating in CFR programming. Develop strong working relationships with CFR fellows to promote their expertise and scholarship. Track international affairs developments on Capitol Hill. Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education and Experience 8+ years of related experience, with event planning experience required. Bachelor’s degree in international relations, government, public policy, or other related field is required; master’s degree preferred. Congressional or government relations experience required. Related Skills & Other Requirements Strong judgement, discretion, and strategic instincts to operate in high-level, dynamic, and confidential environment. Established relationships across significant segment of House or Senate environment. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills including with senior principles. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to multi-task and problem solve independently. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment both independently and on a team. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $145,000 – $155,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers an outstanding benefits package. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. Washington, District of Columbia, United States $145,000 - $155,000 USD yearly
item.dc:creator: Council on Foreign Relations

item.title: Research Associate U S Foreign Policy
item.description: $55,000 - $58,000 USD yearly Overview Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, with headquarters in New York, an office in Washington, DC, and programs nationwide. It is dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR's 5,000+ members are leaders in international affairs and foreign policy. CFR also publishes Foreign Affairs , the preeminent magazine on global issues, and provides up-to-date information about the world and U.S. foreign policy on its award-winning website, CFR.org. Position Summary CFR’s David Rockefeller Studies Program is one of the country’s largest foreign policy think tanks with a widely respected and influential research staff. The Studies Program’s aim is to advance the discussion of U.S. foreign policy and international affairs through its writing, publications, public outreach, and discussions. As part of the Studies Program, the research associate will support a variety of fellows and programs, including a senior fellow whose work focuses on international relations, foreign policy, and diplomatic history. This role encompasses both administrative and research support, with the balance between the two fluctuating based on fellow and program needs. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC, office on a hybrid basis. CFR defines hybrid status as working at least four days a week onsite, with Tuesday through Thursday considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Provide logistical and administrative support to fellows, including scheduling and calendar management, handling phone calls, and media requests, making travel arrangements, and drafting correspondence Coordinate events, including preparing invitations, making travel arrangements, corresponding with speakers, presiders, and participants, and providing logistical support for the event Conduct research and editing for articles, book chapters, and other publications Assist with budgeting, including tracking monthly income statements, monitoring grant information, potentially drafting grant reports and proposals, creating and updating Excel spreadsheets, and preparing vouchers for reimbursement Assist fellows with social media outreach, including website maintenance and posting and/or using social media platforms, as needed Support other fellows and departments, upon request Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required Minimum Qualifications Experience and Education Bachelor’s degree in a related field such as political science, history, or international relations or other related fields. Demonstrated interest in foreign policy studies, diplomatic history, or related fields Master’s degree preferred, but not required One or more years of related administrative and/or internship experience preferred Related Skills & Other Requirements Excellent research, writing, editing, and communication skills Strong organizational and time management skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with others Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and manage sensitive information with discretion. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other digital productivity tools, with strong online research and information-management skills Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $55,000 – $58,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. Washington, District of Columbia, United States $55,000 - $58,000 USD yearly

item.title: Public Policy Coordinator Program And Data Support
item.description: Description Pay Range - $50,939.20 - $55,016.00 (Median Pay $52,510,00) I. Purpose & Summary of Position: The Texas Council on Family Violence is the only 501(c)(3) nonprofit coalition in Texas dedicated solely to creating safer communities and freedom from family violence. With a state-wide reach and direct local impact, TCFV, with the collective strength of more than 1000 members, shapes public policy, equips service providers, and initiates strategic prevention efforts. Using TCFV’s strategic plan as a guide, the Public Policy Coordinator, Program and Data Support is responsible for strengthening and expanding the capacity of family violence programs and community partners working to create system change in support of survivors of family violence. The Public Policy Coordinator , Program and Data Support works on the Program Policy Focus Area of the Policy Team within TCFV, reporting to the Public Policy Manager (Programmatic Focus Area) and/or the Director of Public Policy. The Public Policy Coordinator will focus on supporting the agency and programs by focusing on the following areas of data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety. They will also provide support, training, and technical assistance to agencies and professionals that directly advocate for survivors of family violence, including state and federal laws around service provision to survivors of family violence. II. Priority functions / Accountabilities: A. Training Development and Coordination – 15% Coordinate, develop and offer trainings on issues related to the areas of data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety for a wide variety of audiences. Create, develop and update written materials and protocols for use by survivors, family violence programs, and allied professionals, with particular emphasis on building knowledge and skills related to areas of data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety . Utilize effective, current, innovative methods to strengthen and expand the capacity of family violence service providers. B. Technical Assistance and Consultation – 35% Provide technical assistance to advocates, family violence programs, and other entities with a focus on data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety . Support relevant TCFV listservs and respond to relevant email accounts to support program staff across the state via training and technical assistance. Ensures that calls and requests for technical assistance are responded to in a supportive, timely manner. C. Systems Advocacy Efforts– 35% Assist in TCFV’s Allocations committee processes with a focus on leading data and analytics. Support evaluation efforts related to the Texas State Plan. Assist policy team in a variety of data analysis and analytics as requested. Develop and maintain expertise on state and federal laws pertaining to confidentiality and privilege for survivors of family violence. Research, track, and provide recommendations about bills during legislative session, including TCFV’s priorities and other proposals that would impact family violence survivors and the allies who serve them. Other projects and responsibilities may be added and/or changed at the discretion of the Managers and Directors. D. Administrative- 15% Ensures timely and accurate reporting of grant activities, including contributing information for the agency’s funding applications. Ensures timely and accurate submission of evaluations, reports, and other required or requested documentation. Actively participate in team efforts to deepen our practices of relationship building, learning, and leadership development. Leads policy team efforts around Tableau. Qualifications III. Minimum Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Sought: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below represent the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Required: Texas residency required. This role is a hybrid remote job and requires in-office responsibilities, in Austin, on a periodic basis. If not directly located in Austin, successful applicants must maintain an ability and availability to attend in-person team activities, necessary Policy, or TCFV-wide activities, and attend in-person meetings and other responsibilities, as requested by the Policy Manager or Policy Directors. Hybrid staff are also expected to travel and attend in person activities associated with their job descriptions and duties. Outside of these expectations, hybrid staff work remotely within the state of Texas. Experience incorporating the perspectives of multiple communities, including BIPOC survivors, advocates, and stakeholders in the consideration of impacts and outcomes of a decision-making process. Experience in data science, data analytics, or other data analysis. Strong team building and leadership skills to effectively manage Coalition activities through vision, strategic planning, and expertise. Self-driven to work independently with minimal supervision and use disciplined time management skills. Thorough knowledge of domestic violence issues and the circumstances faced by those experiencing it. Critical analytical skills to understand the political, social, financial, and external issues affecting service providers; to foresee and interpret trends and dynamics changing needs of TCFV constituents; and to develop process and resources to respond effectively and in a timely manner. Communication skills suitable for presentation and written publication, for internal and external distribution. Self-driven to manage time and complete multiple activities and grant deliverables within deadlines. Working experience with Microsoft Office applications and can adeptly navigate new software and technology. Ability to work collaboratively in a team, providing support and constructive feedback in interpersonal interaction with staff, board, and members. Must be proactive, communicative, responsive, creative, flexible, to accomplish agency and program goals; and possess mission of service attitude with a strong commitment to and knowledge of constituent service and relations. Ability to work within a team to offer support and collaborate on team projects. Ability to maintain strict confidentiality of employee, donor, funder, survivor, and case information. Preferred: Bachelor’s Degree. We will consider a combination of education and related experience. (Equivalency formula: two years of experience is equal to one year of education.) Bi-lingual English/Spanish language a plus as is any bi-lingual / bi-cultural lived experience. Experience providing direct services to individuals affected by domestic violence preferred. IV. Working Conditions and Environment/Physical Demands: Ability to communicate and converse in English. Travel up to 25% during non-legislative session times. Ability to frequently tolerate prolonged stationary positions and frequently move about a large public building. Ability to engage in frequent public contact. Professional attire may be required for most public-facing work. Ability to work in or from a remote location or from a home-based office. Must possess the emotional and physical stamina to deal with a variety of high-pressure situations, such as: responding to urgent legislative issues, handling difficult internal and external interactions, and effectively working long and, at times, odd hours which could exceed 40 hours or include weekends as necessary. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and minimum level of work being performed. They are not intended to be construed as exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required for the position. The employee will be required to perform any other job-related duties as required by the job objectives, the CEO and mission and philosophy of TCFV.

item.title: Policy And Legislative Affairs Coordinator
item.description: Position: Policy and Legislative Affairs Coordinator Classification: Full-time, Exempt Reports to: Director, Special Projects Company: Texans Together Location: Houston, TX Position Description: The Policy and Legislative Affairs Coordinator serves as the organization's lead resource for legislative affairs, policy analysis, advocacy strategy, and government relations. This position monitors legislative and regulatory developments, analyzes their impact on organizational priorities, and provides recommendations to executive leadership regarding advocacy efforts and implementation strategies. Working closely with the Director of Special Projects, the Coordinator will help develop and execute legislative engagement strategies, build relationships with policymakers and stakeholders, coordinate advocacy activities, and support organizational readiness for policy and regulatory changes. Primary Responsibilities: Monitor legislation, regulatory activity, and policy developments at the local, state, and federal levels. Track bills and legislative initiatives relevant to the organization's mission and strategic priorities. Analyze proposed legislation and assess potential impacts on operations, programs, and stakeholders. Develop policy summaries, legislative reports, issue briefs, and executive-level recommendations. Provide strategic guidance regarding emerging policy issues. Assist in the development and implementation of the organization's advocacy agenda and legislative priorities. Execute advocacy strategies and activities aligned with organizational goals. Prepare policy positions, talking points, briefing documents, and stakeholder communications. Recommend advocacy approaches and engagement opportunities based on legislative developments. Coordinate organizational responses to policy proposals and legislative initiatives. Support the cultivation and maintenance of relationships with members of the Texas Legislature, legislative staff, state agencies, and key stakeholders. Support leadership engagement with elected officials and policy influencers. Coordinate legislative meetings, site visits, presentations, and informational briefings. Represent the organization at legislative hearings, stakeholder meetings, conferences, and public forums. Serve as a liaison between the organization and governmental entities. Support legislative engagement efforts during legislative sessions and interim periods. Track committee hearings, legislative deadlines, policy proposals, and stakeholder activities. Identify opportunities for strategic engagement and advocacy. Prepare leadership for legislative meetings, testimony, and policy discussions. Lead policy-focused projects and strategic initiatives. Research emerging trends, best practices, and policy innovations relevant to child welfare and community-based care. Develop reports, presentations, dashboards, and briefing materials for executive leadership and board members. Required Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Social Work, Communications, or a related field. Minimum two (2) years’ experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, advocacy, child welfare, public administration, communications, or a related field. Experience working with the Texas Legislature, legislative offices, state agencies, or governmental entities. Experience in child welfare, community-based care, human services, education, healthcare, or nonprofit advocacy. Preferred Qualifications: Master’s degree in Public Policy, Public Administration, Law, Social Work, or a related field preferred. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Knowledge of Texas legislative processes and policymaking. Strong writing and communication skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into concise summaries. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to independently manage multiple projects and competing priorities. Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities. Ability to translate strategic direction into actionable plans and measurable outcomes. Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills. Ability to influence and coordinate work across teams without formal authority. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment. Sound judgment, initiative, and a willingness to take ownership of projects and results. Work Conditions: Environment: Office Work Schedule: Monday – Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Travel: Occasional (Must have reliable transportation, valid Texas Driver License and current Auto Insurance) DePelchin is Proud to be an Equal Opportunity Workplace. DePelchin is committed to selecting and employing the best and most qualified person available for each job opening without unlawful discrimination of any kind. Additionally, DePelchin is committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), marital or parental status, veteran status, religion, national origin, age, disability, family medical history, genetic information, or political affiliation.

item.title: Multimedia Coordinator Outreach Government Affairs
item.description: About Houston-Galveston Area Council The Houston-Galveston Area Council is one of the largest regional planning commissions in the country with a diverse service area of 13 counties and more than 7 million people. We are the pulse of our region addressing issues that cross city limits and county lines every single day. We make decisions that affect our transportation system, ensure the safety and well-being of our seniors, connect people to jobs, help families recover from natural disasters, preserve water quality for our children, and so much more. We work to make the region a great place to live, work, and thrive. What will I be doing? The Multimedia Coordinator is a strategic communicator who will connect H-GAC’s programs, priorities, and regional impact with the people and organizations the agency serves. As part of the Outreach & Government Affairs team, this position will create clear, compelling, and visually engaging communications for residents, member governments, elected officials, community partners, media, and other stakeholders. The coordinator will support strategic communications, graphic design, digital marketing, social media, media relations, and intergovernmental relations. This position will also monitor governmental developments, assess their relevance to H-GAC, and help align communications activities with organizational strategy. The successful candidate will be an excellent writer and strong graphic designer with sound judgment, audience awareness, and an interest in the governmental environment in which H-GAC operates. Strategic Communications & Content Development Help develop public affairs and communications strategies that advance H-GAC’s mission, programs, and regional priorities. Work with leadership and program staff to identify audiences, messages, communications needs, and appropriate outreach channels. Write and edit content for websites, newsletters, reports, presentations, social media, talking points, and outreach materials. Translate technical, governmental, and policy information into clear, audience-focused content. Maintain editorial calendars, communications standards, and project workflows while ensuring materials are accurate and consistent. Graphic Design & Multimedia Communications Create polished print and digital materials, including reports, infographics, presentations, newsletters, advertisements, event materials, and social media graphics. Transform regional data, policies, and technical subjects into accessible and visually engaging stories. Apply strong design judgment in typography, layout, imagery, branding, and information hierarchy. Maintain brand consistency, develop reusable templates, and prepare files for print and digital production. Coordinate with creative vendors and support photography, video, and other multimedia projects as needed. Digital Marketing & Social Media Plan and create digital content that builds awareness of H-GAC programs, services, events, and regional initiatives. Develop copy, graphics, short-form video, and multimedia content for social media, websites, email, newsletters, and digital campaigns. Manage content calendars and coordinate approvals, publishing, and monitoring. Monitor online conversations and news for communications opportunities or reputational concerns. Use analytics and digital best practices to improve audience reach and engagement. Project Coordination Manage multiple communications and public affairs projects from concept through delivery. Coordinate schedules, requirements, reviews, approvals, and final production. Support public meetings, conferences, board-related activities, community events, and outreach campaigns. Explore emerging communications tools and responsible uses of artificial intelligence to improve quality and efficiency. Key Qualifications Excellent writing, editing, visual communication, and verbal presentation skills. Strong graphic design capabilities and a portfolio demonstrating expertise in layout, typography, branding, information design, and digital content. Ability to interpret governmental, policy, and technical information for different audiences. Understanding of how communications, government relations, media relations, and stakeholder engagement support organizational strategy. Proficiency with Adobe Creative Cloud, particularly InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop. Experience developing content for print, websites, email, social media, and presentations. Strong project-management skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Sound judgment and the ability to work effectively with executives, elected officials, government staff, media, vendors, and community partners. Commitment to accessible communications, nonpartisan public service, and regional cooperation. Do you have… Bachelor’s degree in an applicable academic discipline or related field of study 3 years of experience working with local government, nonprofit programs, school, or in job-related duties Preferred 3+ years of progressively responsible experience in public affairs, strategic communications, government relations, or public-sector communications. Experience working for a government, regional organization, public agency, nonprofit, association, news organization, legislative office, or public-sector consulting firm. Experience communicating with elected officials, government staff, media, and community stakeholders. Knowledge of the Houston-Galveston region and issues affecting local governments. Experience monitoring governmental activity and connecting developments to organizational strategy. Familiarity with media relations, digital advertising, photography, video, data visualization, or web content. Knowledge of the Texas Open Meetings Act, public-information practices, or public-sector accessibility requirements. Working knowledge of Spanish or experience developing multilingual materials. Salary range: $70,000.00 - $77,000.00 All employees of H-GAC are required to reside within the agency’s region of service to support our commitment to excellence in service of our region. H-GAC is an equal opportunity/ADA employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, or protected veteran status.

item.title: Deputy Director Elections
item.description: Summary The Deputy Director of Elections supports the Elections Director in overseeing the daily operations and long-range planning of the Elections Department. This position works closely with all areas of the department and its vendors to ensure continuity of operations and the successful administration of elections throughout Delaware County. The Deputy Director provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and coordination to support elections that are secure, accurate, transparent, and accessible to Delaware County voters. Essential Duties Support the Elections Director in overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Elections Department. Assist with long-range and strategic planning for election operations. Plan, coordinate, and direct election activities involving more than 2,000 full-time, temporary, and Election Day workers. Support election operations serving approximately 330,000 voters during each election. Coordinate activities across all areas of the Elections Department to ensure continuity of operations. Work closely with departmental staff, County departments, outside vendors, and other stakeholders. Assist with ballot system preparation and testing. Support poll worker recruitment, training, and coordination. Assist with voter registration activities and election-related voter services. Support ballot processing, audits, and election results reporting. Assist with campaign finance activities and other election administration responsibilities. Develop and maintain procedures that support secure, accurate, and transparent election processes. Identify operational needs and assist with implementing improvements to departmental processes. Provide leadership and guidance to staff to ensure deadlines, regulatory requirements, and departmental goals are met. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications High school diploma or equivalent required. Bachelor’s degree preferred. Experience should include a combination of responsibilities in at least two or more of the following areas: Ballot system preparation and testing Poll worker training Voter registration Ballot processing and audits Election results reporting Campaign finance Other related election administration functions Additional Information Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Ability to clearly plan and direct election operations. Ability to work effectively with department staff and vendors. Strong organizational and communication skills. Ability to manage multiple responsibilities related to election operations.

item.title: Senior Federal Lobbyist
item.description: American Association of University Professors Political Department Senior Federal Lobbyist – Hybrid position based in Washington, D.C. The American Association of University Professors (AAUP), a fast-growing union of higher education workers, is pleased to announce a professional position for a Senior Federal Lobbyist, to be filled as soon as possible. Our goals are to build AAUP member power in order to defend the higher ed sector against increasing attacks and lead a fight for fair wages, job security, academic freedom, an end to student debt, and expanded access to postsecondary education. The Senior Federal Lobbyist leads the American Association of University Professors' (AAUP), an affiliate of the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), AFL-CIO, federal advocacy agenda, serving as the primary liaison to Capitol Hill, executive agencies, and national advocacy coalitions. Reporting directly to the Political Director, this person will develop and execute legislative and regulatory initiatives to champion higher education as a public good, safeguard academic freedom, protect shared governance and faculty tenure, advance labor and collective bargaining rights, and secure robust federal funding for higher education and scientific research. The ideal candidate combines sharp political acumen with exceptional attention to detail, innovative out-of-the-box thinking, and outstanding interpersonal skills. As a key team player within the Political & Legislative Affairs department, the lobbyist will collaborate across teams and affiliate organizations to translate complex policy into high-impact advocacy strategies. The AAUP is committed to a diverse workforce and strives to achieve a workplace environment respectful of the many cultures of our own employees and the higher education workers we represent, including a significant number of African-American, Asian-American/Pacific Islander, and Latinx employees, as well as LGBTQl-identified employees, and those who have immigrated from various countries. The AAUP values the benefits that diversity brings to the faculty profession and the labor movement. We seek applicants whose experience and perspective will contribute to strong representation of our diverse members. Duties and Responsibilities The position will include the following responsibilities: Federal Advocacy & Legislative Strategy Capitol Hill Engagement: Serve as the principal registered lobbyist for the AAUP before Congress, maintaining active, collaborative, and bipartisan relationships with key committees (e.g., Senate HELP, House Education & the Workforce, Appropriations) and leadership offices. Executive Branch & Agency Liaison: Monitor and influence federal rulemaking and regulatory policy within the U.S. Department of Education, National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), Department of Labor (DOL), NSF, NIH, and the White House. Policy Monitoring & Analysis: Rigorously track federal legislation, executive orders, and agency guidance. Perform thorough, detailed policy analyses on issue areas affecting higher education, academic freedom, civil rights, labor rights, and research funding. Creative Strategy: Bring innovative, out-of-the-box strategies to legislative campaign planning, identifying non-traditional avenues and message framing to advance AAUP priorities in challenging political environments. Policy Writing & Precision Communications Detail-Oriented Deliverables: Draft and meticulously edit high-priority advocacy materials, including legislative briefs, congressional testimony, sign-on letters, administrative comments, and background memos for AAUP leadership where accuracy and precision are paramount. Member Updates: Translate complex legislative developments into clear, accessible, and actionable updates for AAUP state conferences, campus chapters, and national membership. Coalition Leadership & Collaborative Partnerships Coalition Engagement: Represent the AAUP in national coalitions alongside higher education associations, labor unions (such as our affiliate, the AFT), civil rights groups, and scientific advocacy networks. Joint Campaigns: Build strong consensus and lead collaborative campaigns on shared federal priorities, including Title IV/Pell Grants, student loan reform, research funding, and defending public higher education against political interference. Member Mobilization, Event Coordination & Internal Collaboration Annual Capitol Hill Fly-In & Lobby Day: With the assistance of cross-departmental staff and legislative team members, lead the strategic planning, messaging, precision scheduling, and execution of AAUP's annual fly-in and lobby day on Capitol Hill. Team-Oriented Integration: Serve as a proactive team player within the Political & Legislative Affairs department, working closely with the Political Director, state policy leadership, and grassroots team to align federal policy goals with member mobilization. Ethics & Compliance: Meticulously maintain compliance records to ensure 100% adherence to the Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA), federal ethics rules, and required reporting standards. Qualifications Professional Experience: 5–10 years of progressive experience in federal government relations, congressional staff roles (e.g., Legislative Director, Senior Committee Staff, Counsel), higher education policy, or labor advocacy. Uncompromising Attention to Detail: Exceptional precision in policy analysis, statutory language review, advocacy writing, compliance reporting, and event schedule management. Interpersonal Excellence & Teamwork: Proven track record as a collaborative team player with strong relationship-building skills across diverse political, labor, academic, and coalition stakeholders. Innovative Problem Solving: Ability to think out of the box to navigate complex legislative landscapes, craft compelling narratives, and develop creative advocacy tactics. Legislative & Budget Expertise: Deep working knowledge of federal legislative processes, statutory reauthorizations (e.g., Higher Education Act), federal budget/appropriations cycles, and administrative rulemaking. Event Leadership: Proven capability to coordinate and run large-scale advocacy events, fly-ins, or member lobbying days on Capitol Hill with high organizational precision. Mission Alignment: Deep commitment to the principles of academic freedom, shared governance, tenure, equity and civil rights in education, and collective bargaining rights. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Law, or related field required; Master’s, J.D., or Ph.D. preferred. This job description is not designed or intended to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Activities, duties, and responsibilities may change, or new ones may be assigned during the course of employment.

item.description: At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers. When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the microphone and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 6,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing. Director, Public Policy Why We Have This Role As the Director of Policy, you will serve as the primary expert monitoring, interpreting, and responding to the evolving healthcare policy landscape. You will lead strategic efforts to identify regulatory trends, analyze reporting requirements (including CAHPS, quality, safety, and value-based payment models), and evaluate their impact on product strategy and client operations. Serving as the company liaison to key government and industry bodies—such as CMS, NQF, and AHRQ—you will develop corporate positions, draft public comment letters, and advocate on behalf of Press Ganey and our healthcare clients. If you are a high-level policy expert with executive presence and a passion for shaping healthcare strategy, this role offers significant influence. How You’ll Find Success Regulatory Landscape Mastery: Expertly analyzes and interprets developments in CAHPS, quality reporting, and value-based payment programs to inform executive strategy. Strategic Stakeholder Advocacy: Establishes and nurtures key relationships with CMS, NQF, AHRQ, and health policy stakeholder groups to advocate for business and client interests. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partners closely with Product Management, Sales, Marketing, and Operations to signal strategic opportunities and guide product enhancements. Executive Communication & Thought Leadership: Delivers high-impact policy updates to C-suite client executives and represents the company as a key speaker at industry events. Policy Team Leadership: Directs, coaches, and manages the public policy team while overseeing annual department budgeting and strategic goal alignment. How You’ll Grow Drive company-wide strategy at the intersection of healthcare technology, regulatory compliance, and public policy. Elevate your professional standing as a prominent health policy thought leader across national conferences, client summits, and industry panels. Deepen direct working relationships with federal policy officials and key regulatory governing bodies. Scale and mentor a high-performing public policy research and regulatory data team. Things You’ll Do Monitor & Interpret Policy: Track developments across the health policy landscape to inform product, marketing, and operational strategy. Lead Government Liaisons: Act as the primary organizational liaison to CMS, NQF, AHRQ, and related governmental or public policy entities. Develop Corporate Positions: Draft, review, and submit official comment letters and position statements for rulemaking and requests for information (RFIs). Author & Present Policy Content: Produce regulatory updates for clients and present policy trends at client meetings and industry events. Direct Public Policy Team: Manage Policy Analysts and Senior Regulatory Data Analysts, guiding research projects, annual performance goals, and department budgets. What We’re Looking For On Your Resume 10+ years of experience in the health policy arena, regulatory affairs, or a related healthcare industry role. Demonstrated experience developing corporate position statements and drafting official comment letters for rulemaking. Bachelor’s Degree in Health Policy, Public Health, Business, or related field required (Master’s Degree preferred). Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with proven executive presence. Ability to navigate a matrixed corporate environment and lead direct reports effectively. What You Should Know About This Team Strategic Core: We sit within Product Management and Enterprise Strategy to directly influence our product vision and business roadmap. Advocacy & Impact: We proactively represent healthcare organizations to safeguard business interests and advance quality reporting standards. Thought Leadership Focus: We serve as the trusted regulatory voice for both internal leadership teams and external health system leaders. Travel Expectation: This role involves approximately 25% travel for client meetings, regulatory sessions, and industry events. Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits Comprehensive Health & Wellness Coverage: Industry-leading medical, dental, and vision packages for employees and dependents. Executive Leadership Development: Opportunities for high-visibility leadership, professional association involvement, and career growth. Generous Paid Time Off: Comprehensive paid vacation, sick leave, and paid company holiday schedule. 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan: Competitive company matching contributions to support your long-term financial health. The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: Our hybrid work model is elegantly simple: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. For the rest of the week, work where you want, owning the integration of work and life . #hybrid Qualtrics is an equal opportunity employer meaning that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic. ​​​​​​​Applicants in the United States of America have rights under Federal Employment Laws: Family & Medical Leave Act , Equal Opportunity Employment , Employee Polygraph Protection Act Qualtrics is committed to the inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Qualtrics will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please let your Qualtrics contact/recruiter know. Not finding a role that’s the right fit for now? Qualtrics Insiders is the one-stop shop for all things Qualtrics Life. Sign up for exclusive access to content created with you in mind and get the scoop on what we have going on at Qualtrics - upcoming events, behind the scenes stories from the team, interview tips, hot jobs, and more. No spam - we promise! You'll hear from us two times a month max with fresh, totally tailored info - so be sure to stay connected as you explore your best role and company fit. A sign-on bonus and restricted stock units may be included in an employment offer. Full-time employees are eligible for medical, dental, vision, life and disability, 401(k) with match, paid time off, a wellness reimbursement, and mental health benefits. item.title: Director Federal Government Affairs
item.description: - Director, Federal Government Affairs PMI US, the maker of ZYN and IQOS, Washington, D.C., US PMI US’s Federal Government Affairs team is seeking a Director of Federal Government Affairs in Washington, D.C. We’re looking for an entrepreneurial, intellectually curious and results-driven professional who demonstrates initiative, creativity and a strong work ethic. Reporting to the Head of Federal Government Affairs, you will collaborate with the U.S. External Affairs team and global colleagues to advance the company’s policy agenda. Your day to day: Develop and maintain relationships with Members of Congress and staff, Executive Branch agencies and officials, and other key stakeholders. Develop and lead advocacy campaigns supporting domestic policy objectives. Serve as an in-house specialist on the U.S. Senate, advising management on policy risks, opportunities and strategies. Provide legislative analysis and develop policy statements, position papers, letters and legislative summaries. Lead legislative efforts in Congress, particularly the Senate, to advance health policy dialogue surrounding tobacco harm reduction. Who we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 10–15 years of experience within the Federal Government, Capitol Hill, private sector, business associations, think tanks or public interest organizations. Professional experience in health care policy. Strong bipartisan relationships and ability to work across the political spectrum. Excellent interpersonal, networking, strategic-thinking and communication skills. Legal authorization to work in the U.S. Preferred Qualifications: Experience and relationships with congressional leadership and/or Senate HELP, Finance or Appropriations committees. Demonstrated leadership and a track record of legislative success. Ability to succeed in a fast-paced team environment while working independently. Annual Base Salary Range: $202,400–$253,000 What we offer: Competitive base salary and annual bonus based on position level. Medical, dental and vision coverage. 401(k) with company match. Wellness and commuter benefits, pet insurance and generous PTO. Smart Work, our hybrid working model. An inclusive, diverse culture with opportunities to develop your skills and career within a global business. The opportunity to contribute to our smoke-free future. PMI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. For more information, visit PMI US and PMI Science.
