item.title: Icba Government Relations Vice President Congressional Relations
item.description: The Vice President, Congressional Relations is responsible for advocating ICBA’s legislative policy positions before the Congress (both House and Senate), financial regulatory agencies, and the Executive Branch. This role also assists and informs ICBA members on congressional activities and with policymaker interaction. Additional responsibilities include communicating association policies to members, other financial groups, and the media. This position is open to applicants in the Washington, DC area. What You’ll Do Maintain continuous contact with members of Congress, their personal office staff and key committee staff. Orchestrate grassroots/grass tops lobbying efforts to motivate members and influence Congress. Attend PAC events, both in-town and out-of-town. Assist association members visiting Congressional offices and agencies. Develop, draft and negotiate bill language and/or amendments. Cover and report on Congressional hearings and legislative markups. Work with association members to formulate association positions. Assist in developing strategies for lobbying Congress in coordination with legislative and regulatory teams. Assist with drafting congressional testimony, letters, position papers, regulatory comments, and articles. Help thoroughly prepare association members testifying before Congress and regulatory agencies. Prepare for, attend and report on association committee meetings and other events. Respond in a timely manner to banker and press inquiries. Establish and maintain relationship with other lobbyists, trade associations and coalitions. Work with state banking associations on Federal legislation Represent association at industry conferences, coalition meetings and other gatherings Areas of legislative responsibility: Monitor and influence legislative and regulatory developments in assigned areas. Analyze legislation in assigned areas for impact upon community banks and their customers. Assist other members of the congressional and regulatory teams on priority lobbying issues. What You Bring Minimum BA degree: law or public policy degree preferred Minimum seven (7) years of related government relations or trade association experience, including working knowledge of banking and financial services issues; Congressional experience preferred Strong written, analytical and oral communication skills Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to interface well with members of Congress, Hill staff, member bankers and ICBA staff colleagues Able to work well both independently and as a member of a team Ability for travel 10% We recognize that candidates may not meet every qualification listed. If your background and experience are close to what we’re seeking, we encourage you to apply. Benefits of Working at ICBA Generous and competitive benefits package 401(k) savings plan offering 100% employer match of up to 6% of annual earnings. Hybrid work environment, monthly work from home stipends, and flexible work hours Fitness discounts, telemedicine, on-demand therapy, and work-life balance tools Tuition reimbursement and allowances for professional development Frequent company social events Friendly and inclusive workplace culture The target annual salary range for this role is currently $125,000 – 175,000 based on a regular, full-time schedule. The amount of compensation offered will be determined by several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications, location, market data and internal equity. ICBA is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. ICBA does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA)’s guiding mission is to create and promote environments where community banks flourish. We are: • Dedicated advocates providing community bankers, policymakers and the public with authoritative insights and resources to support and strengthen community banking. • Knowledgeable, applying their expertise to offer personalized service that addresses the distinct challenges and opportunities facing community banks. • Community-centered, driving meaningful change that strengthens community banks and the communities they serve. We turn commitment into action and deliver real results. ICBA’s workplace culture is built on our core values: • Caring -We support and prioritize your well-being and professional growth. • Connected - We foster strong relationships that create meaningful impact. • Collaboration – We are team-oriented and results driven where diverse perspectives are valued, and innovative ideas are encouraged to achieve our common goals. Join ICBA and further your career while making a lasting impact

item.title: Government Affairs Intern
item.description: A bout the Position: The National Association of Counties (NACo) is offering a paid internship within the Government Affairs department. This internship provides a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in federal advocacy, policy analysis and county government practices. This internship will run from mid-January 2027 to mid-May 2027 , with start and end dates subject to the availability of the candidate. Candidates must be available to provide on-site assistance to the Government Affairs team at NACo’s 2027 Legislative Conference from February 19 – 23 in Washington, D.C. As part of NACo’s Government Affairs team, you will gain significant exposure to the federal legislative process, explore advocacy strategies and make valuable connections with government officials, Congressional staff and other legislative professionals. NACo is a friendly, fast-paced work environment with a bipartisan, mission-driven team. An ideal candidate will thrive in a strategic, nonpartisan political environment designed to advance the policies and priorities of our members. Candidates should have a strong understanding of and interest in the U.S. political system, including local and regional government and its nexus with federal programs and regulations. Key Responsibilities: Researching and analyzing impacts of legislation and regulations Authoring advocacy updates on regulatory and legislative actions Learning and utilizing software and computer systems utilized by the Government Affairs department Organizing materials, such as agendas, briefing documents and attendee packets, for conference sessions and meetings Supporting NACo Government Affairs team at in-person meetings and conferences Other duties as assigned Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s degree and are at least a sophomore in good standing, or have earned a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university Excellent oral and written communications skills Ability to meet deadlines and work well under pressure Knowledge of and interest in local government policies and practices Prior internship experience a plus, particularly in government affairs, on Capitol Hill or for a state or local government Hours/Salary: Expected to work 10-15 hours per week. This internship pays $18.40 per hour. Application Procedures: Please send a cover letter and indicate your availability (approximate number of hours per week available to work and approximate start and end dates). Applications are processed on a rolling basis until all available positions are filled, so applying early is encouraged. Location and Travel: The internship is based in our NACo’s Washington, D.C. office and will be primarily in person.

item.title: Associate Government Affairs
item.description: Who We Are: Raben is a public policy, strategic communications and organizational consulting firm. Our talented and passionate team champions diversity, equity, and justice as core values that ignite our mission for impactful change in corporate, nonprofit, government, and foundation work. Our changemakers work to solve real-world problems and inspire lasting changes through our four service offerings: strategic communications, government affairs, issue campaigns, and culture, strategy, & organizational design. We have been fueled by insightful strategy, creative tactics, and plain old hustle for over 20 years. We are people of color, women, immigrants, disabled, and LGBTQ. Spend time with us and you will quickly learn we value smarts, creativity, and audaciousness in just about all we do… and a sense of humor is a contractual must. Learn more at raben.co. What We Seek: We seek an AssociateAssociate to join our Government Affairs practice in our Washington, DC office to support Raben client teams and engagements. Associates have hands-on expertise, contextual knowledge, strong critical thinking abilities, the desire to develop and the tactical skills to advance the strategic mission and vision of Raben and further the development and success of our Government Affairs practice in providing excellent client services and engaging prospective clients. Our successful candidate will have a high degree of initiative, personal resilience, attention to detail, intellectual engagement in the subject-matter at hand, and a concierge-like approach to client services. This position is located in our DC office and follows a hybrid schedule with at least two days per week in office. We offer schedule flexibility, while prioritizing a consistent and meaningful in-office presence to support collaboration and team engagement. Responsibilities: Serve as a tactician on designated teams, conducting legislative and policy research, drafting memos and reports, monitoring legislation, monitoring and summarizing legislative hearings, and conducting outreach to Hill offices for scheduling, information gathering and coordination. Ensure timely, responsive client service delivery, including tracking internal deliverables, responding to client requests, capturing notes and action items in team meetings, and proactive troubleshooting. Assist in the planning, coordination, and staffing of meetings, convenings, conference calls, panels, Lobby Days, etc., including – venue logistics, registrations, marketing and outreach, attendee and speaker communications, on-site support, vendor management, etc. Contribute to the organizational goals of the firm’s Government Affairs and Policy Counsel practice group. Other duties as assigned. Requirements Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required; work, internship, or volunteer experience on the Hill is a plus. Strong proficiency with internet research, Microsoft Word, Sharepoint, Excel and PowerPoint required; professional experience with social media applications and web content management systems a plus. A collaborative and relationship-building mindset. Must be able to proactively identify potential challenges/conflicts and communicate with team members with a problem-solving approach. Strong writing, layout and editing skills; experience with desktop publishing tools. Strong oral and written communication skills are a non-negotiable requirement. Candidates must have the demonstrable ability to quickly produce clear, compelling written collateral and communicate professionally and diplomatically with a wide range of staff, clients, partners and stakeholders. Ability to thrive and manage shifting priorities under tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Demonstrable project and time management skills across multiple assignments with many moving parts. Prior event coordination experience preferred. Application Instructions: To apply, please submit an application and resume via our online job portal. At this time, we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship. If you need accommodation during the recruitment process, please email your needs to careers@raben.co . Salary Range and Benefits: Our salary for this role is $55,000 per year. In addition to a great degree of autonomy in work and projects, our colleagues enjoy a suite of benefits such as health, dental, and vision insurance, unlimited PTO, flexibility in schedule, a rich professional development curriculum, a 3% 401K match, yearly employer FSA contribution, work from home flexibility, and many more. Raben finds it quite natural to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, aspiring to live the values of equity in everything we do. Salary Description $55,000 annually

item.title: Coordinator Government Affairs
item.description: Apply here - https://secure.builtapp.com/rila/jobs/fd89422c RILA is growing! At the Retail Industry Leaders Association (RILA) , we convene decision-makers, advocate for the retail industry, and promote operational excellence and innovation. Our aim is bold but simple: to elevate a dynamic industry by transforming the environment in which retailers operate. We are a dynamic, collaborative, team-oriented trade association in Washington, DC. Our employees are passionate about customer service and supporting our members and each other, and we are adding to the team! What we are looking for: Position Summary: The Coordinator, Government Affairs is an entry‑level position supporting the work of RILA’s Public Affairs department. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Government Affairs, this role assists with the day‑to‑day execution of member‑facing activities, policy tracking and research, and communications that advance RILA's broader public policy priorities. This position plays a key role in logistics, content development, member engagement, and internal coordination to support the department’s initiatives. It is well suited for a motivated early‑career government affairs professional with strong communication, organizational, and analytical skills. Position Responsibilities: Project Coordination & Administration: Serve as an internal project coordinator by tracking timelines, documenting progress, and aligning deliverables with relevant team members. Provide administrative and coordination support to the SVP, GA and the broader Public Affairs team as needed. Identify opportunities to improve internal processes, tools, and resource delivery. Policy Research & Content Development: Conduct policy research and prepare briefing materials, reports, talking points, and background documents. Draft and support delivery of written member communications, including newsletters, issue briefs, research summaries, meeting notes, and internal memos. Member Engagement & Meeting Support: Assist with coordination of virtual and in‑person member committee meetings, legislative fly‑ins, and conference calls. Schedule meetings with policymakers and assist with outreach to coalition partners. Systems & Information Management: Maintain and update databases and digital assets (e.g., Salesforce), including committee rosters, registration links, and public‑facing and member web content. Success Metrics & Performance Indicators: Timely and accurate coordination of meetings, communications, and deliverables. Member satisfaction with responsiveness and support. Quality, clarity, and accuracy of written materials and research outputs. Consistent and accurate maintenance of internal databases and public‑facing content. Ability to manage multiple responsibilities with attention to detail and follow‑through. Core Competencies: Project and Task Coordination. Written Communication and Editing. Stakeholder Service Orientation. Research and Information Synthesis. Database and Digital Content Management. Professional Growth Opportunities: This role provides opportunities for growth through increased responsibility in program coordination, public policy engagement, issue‑area expertise, and member communications. The Coordinator will gain exposure to national issues impacting the retail industry and build foundational experience working with corporate executives, government affairs professionals, policymakers, and external partners. What you will get from us: At RILA, you will find solid people. We do our best to learn and grow each day, driven by a passion for building leaders and cultivating an inclusive and collaborative culture. We promise that the work you do will matter and will have an impact on the vast retail industry and the communities our retailers serve. You will have an opportunity to grow professionally and develop new skills and we will challenge and support you in your professional journey. Consider becoming part of the RILA team - check out our RILA Careers page here and some RILA reviews here. Compensation & Benefits: $53,000 starting annual salary with overtime and bonus opportunities. Flexible and hybrid office environment (3 days in office). Affordable Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage (FSA/HSA options available). Employer-sponsored Life Insurance, STD, and LTD Coverage. 401(K)/Roth 401(K) Retirement Plan with employer match. Unlimited Paid Time Off + 12 Federal holiday closures. Professional development opportunities. Team outings/gatherings. *** RILA is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Application Instructions: Please submit a resume and statement of interest to https://secure.builtapp.com/rila/jobs/fd89422c explaining your interest in the role and how your experience aligns. Thanks!

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: Everytown for Gun Safety is seeking an experienced Director of Government Affairs to lead federal lobbying and advocacy efforts on Capitol Hill and with the Administration. We're looking for someone who knows how Washington works, has strong relationships with policymakers and congressional staff, and can turn legislative strategy into action. This is an opportunity for an experienced Hill staffer or federal lobbyist to put their relationships, political instincts, and expertise to work advancing gun violence prevention policies. As a senior member of the Government Affairs team, the Director will help shape and execute federal legislative strategy, engage key decision-makers, and advance the organization's priorities in Congress and across the Administration. This position will be based at our Washington, DC office, and will adhere to a hybrid work schedule. WE TRUST YOU TO: Federal Lobbying & Legislative Strategy • Lead federal lobbying and advocacy efforts before Congress and the Administration. • Develop and execute legislative strategies to advance the organization's federal gun violence prevention priorities. • Build and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, Administration officials, and key stakeholders. • Monitor legislative and political developments, identify opportunities, and advise leadership on strategy and engagement. • Represent Everytown in congressional meetings, legislative briefings, coalition meetings, and other external engagements. • Lead advocacy efforts during key legislative moments, including hearings, markups, floor votes, and other congressional activity. Advocacy & Coordination • Work with policy, political, communications, and research teams to align federal advocacy strategy and messaging. • Collaborate with national coalitions and advocacy partners to advance shared legislative priorities. • Develop briefing materials, talking points, and strategic recommendations to support federal lobbying efforts. QUALIFICATIONS: We're looking for someone with strong political instincts, an established network, and a commitment to preventing gun violence. The ideal candidate knows how to navigate Capitol Hill, build effective relationships, and move legislative priorities forward from day one. • Significant experience working on Capitol Hill, in federal lobbying, government affairs, or political advocacy. • Established relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, and key federal stakeholders. • Deep understanding of Congress, the legislative process, and the federal political landscape. • Proven ability to develop and execute legislative strategies, navigate political challenges, and deliver results. • Strong communication skills, political judgment, and the ability to work effectively with policymakers and coalition partners. • A genuine commitment to gun violence prevention and Everytown's mission. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS The salary range for this position is $135,000 to $145,000 per year, depending on experience. Everytown offers a generous benefits package, including medical, vision, and dental insurance, paid time off, 401(k) matching, education assistance, and more. ABOUT THE HIRING PROCESS We are accepting applications on a rolling basis and will review applications as they are received. To be considered, applicants must submit both a cover letter and an updated resume. ** Applications missing either document will not be reviewed. DIVERSE WORKFORCE AND OPEN CULTURE Candidates who identify as members of historically underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply to Everytown. A diverse workforce and open culture are at the heart of our organization and vital to our success. Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. You can learn about the framework that guides our work by viewing Everytown's Organizations Values ABOUT EVERYTOWN FOR GUN SAFETY Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund (“Everytown for Gun Safety”) is the largest gun violence prevention organization in the country, with nearly 11 million supporters and more than 700,000 donors, including moms, mayors, survivors, students, and everyday Americans fighting for common-sense gun safety measures that can help save lives. Learn more at www.everytown.org and follow us @Everytown.

item.title: Elections Pm And Consultant Onsite
item.description: Job Title: Elections PM and Consultant (Onsite) Location: Jackson, MS Duration: 12 Months Job Description: The Client is seeking a qualified contractor with 10 years or Greater of relevant experience to provide elections oriented project management, elections systems and support technical coordination, and county consultation and support services for the Statewide Elections Management System (SEMS). This position will be responsible for overseeing all SEMS development activities, coordinating and managing the third-party development vendor, monitoring project progress, and ensuring that development activities, enhancements, and deliverables align with agency requirements and operational needs. The contractor will also serve as a primary liaison between the agency, county election officials, and the development vendor, including documenting, communicating, tracking, and escalating system issues or enhancement requests submitted by the agency or counties and coordinating with the vendor to ensure timely and effective resolution. The contractor will provide consultation and assistance to county election officials regarding SEMS functionality, utilization, troubleshooting, and related inquiries. Responsibilities: Responsibilities will also include assisting with the development, coordination, and delivery of training to counties concerning SEMS operations, system features, and other relevant or applicable election procedures and processes, utilizing agency-approved guidance and materials. The contractor shall not independently provide elections-related policy, procedural, or legal interpretations or advice to counties. When such matters arise, the contractor may serve as an intermediary by referring inquiries to appropriate authorized agency personnel or other official sources and communicating the guidance received. Total compensated hours shall not exceed 1,040 hours per calendar year, regardless of the agreed-upon weekly schedule or work arrangement. Education Level: Bachelor's or Higher Required Skills/Experience: The candidate must have relevant experience in software application project management, third-party vendor coordination, and technical issue resolution. Preferred qualifications include experience with election management systems, governmental information systems, or comparable enterprise applications. Candidates should possess strong organizational, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to coordinate software development activities, document and track technical issues through resolution, and communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Experience providing system consultation, user support, and training to government personnel or other end users is highly desirable. Familiarity with Mississippi election administration, Mississippi county election processes and procedures, and the Statewide Elections Management System (SEMS) is required. Preferred/Not Required: Preferred qualifications include familiarity with application security best practices, including secure software development, vulnerability management, access controls, data protection, and identification and remediation of security risks. Additional preferred experience includes software development lifecycle (SDLC) methodologies, quality assurance, user acceptance testing (UAT), database management, systems integration, and software change and release management. Experience with the Statewide Elections Management System (SEMS) or comparable election management applications is preferred, along with familiarity with Mississippi election administration, county election operations, and applicable election procedures. item.title: 2027 Summer Internship Public Policy Government Relations
item.description: When you’re the best, we’re the best. We instill an environment where employees feel engaged, satisfied and able to contribute their unique skills and talents while living and working as their authentic selves . We provide extensive opportunities for personal and professional development, building both employee competence and organizational capability to fuel exceptional performance through an inclusive environment both now and in the future. Vizient Intern Program Overview: This program is designed to foster a beneficial relationship and provide growth opportunities for Vizient, our employees, and collegiate students. Since 2000, our summer intern program has provided college undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students with practical experience that exposes them to multiple aspects of a career field and the healthcare industry. This full-time, paid intern program offers an opportunity to accelerate academic learning, apply classroom knowledge, and introduce students to a professional setting. Interns are assigned a supervisor to mentor/develop their business skills, as well as monitor their work experiences. Interns are integral members of the company’s team, setting goals, working toward deadlines, and actively participating in community service projects. The program requires the intern to commit to 10 weeks of participation in all formal training, mentoring, on-the-job learning, and opportunities to interact with senior leaders. Program starts June 1, 2027, and ends August 6, 2027 Pay rate: $25 per hour. About the team and role Vizient's Office of Public Policy and Government Relations in Washington, DC serves as an advocate and liaison on policy and legislative issues that affect the diverse healthcare organizations we serve. With a strategic, balanced and forward-thinking approach, our team of bipartisan professionals regularly delves into emerging legislative and regulatory issues, conducts research on healthcare policies and coordinates appropriate responses. Vizient is seeking a dedicated and passionate intern to support key government relations and public policy projects in the summer of 2027. What You’ll Do Serve as an indispensable partner to the Public Policy & Government Relations team. Assist staff in developing and executing legislative and regulatory advocacy strategies; provide research on key policy priorities. Represent Vizient at Congressional hearings and briefings by partner organizations, think tanks, federal agencies, and academic institutions; attend meetings with government officials. Support the development of advocacy communications collateral and other policy-related communications, including grassroots engagement. Support the development of educational materials and assist in drafting regulatory summaries and comment letters. Participate in health sector advocacy group meetings to learn about shared policy priorities. Other responsibilities may include administrative office support; updating public policy web pages; preparing policy memos and PowerPoint slides; and supporting political engagement and reporting. What You’ll Learn We provide the tools and training necessary to succeed, as well as provide intentional development opportunities such as: Exposure to senior leadership to discuss advocacy strategy, research projects and milestones. Networking opportunities with cross-functional teams to learn about various areas within the organization. Networking opportunities and exposure to external stakeholders, including government officials and partner organizations in the healthcare sector. Value added skills development in advocacy strategy, government relations, policy research and analysis, writing, communications and project management. Personalized strengths coaching. Participation in company meetings and key culture events. Intern-led community impact project and team building activities outside of work. Qualifications Enrolled in a four-year accredited college or university and in favorable academic standing. Must have completed sophomore year as an undergraduate prior to the start of the internship or recently completed your degree. Knowledge of or demonstrated interest in politics and/or policy, including legislative and regulatory process at the federal, state, or local level (specific interest in health policy is preferred). Demonstrated ability to conduct public policy, legislative, regulatory, or healthcare research and analysis. Strong written communication skills, including the ability to prepare concise policy memos, summaries, briefing materials, or other professional communications. Ability to analyze, synthesize, and communicate complex information and apply problem-solving skills. Strong interpersonal skills for interacting across the team and with internal Vizient business partners and external stakeholders. Strong project coordination and organizational skills, including the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines. Previous experience with local, state or federal government entities, advocacy or policy organizations and/or healthcare organizations is preferred but not required. This position will be based in Vizient’s Washington, DC office, with an in-office work schedule Monday-Thursday; Fridays are work from home days. Equal Opportunity Employer: Females/Minorities/Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities The Company is committed to equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, color, gender identity, ethnicity, age, national origin, sexual orientation, disability status, veteran status or any other category protected by applicable law.

item.title: Senior Analyst Legislative
item.description: Company Overview Pantheon Data (a Kenific Holding company) is a private, small business based in the Washington, DC, area. Pantheon Data was founded in 2011, initially providing acquisition and supply chain management services to the US Coast Guard. Our service offerings have grown in the past ten years, including infrastructure resiliency, contact center operations, information technology, software engineering, program management, strategic communications, engineering, and cybersecurity. We have also grown our customer base to include commercial clients. The company has used this experience to expand our service offerings to other agencies within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the Department of Defense (DoD), and other Federal Civilian Agencies. Position Overview We are seeking a Senior Analyst, Legislative to serve as the client's front door for incoming audit and review requests. Audit requests arrive from the Defense Audit Office, the DoD Inspector General, the Naval Audit Service, the Government Accountability Office, and comparable review bodies. Each audit has its own scope, its own set of the right people to answer it, and its own clock. Without a single point of intake, requests scatter , deadlines surface late, and the same question can draw different answers from different offices. This role is the single point where those requests come in and the single place where their status is known. You receive the request, read it closely enough to understand what is being asked, route it to the right point of contact , and then stay with it through to closure. You hold the tracker, you run the recurring status, and you are the person who can answer "where does that one stand" without going to look. The judgment is the job. Some requests you own and close. Some need to be in front of a senior leader the same day for input, review, and submission . Knowing which is which, and being right about it, is what this role requires . The work is administrative and analytical rather than financial. You are not performing or auditing financial statements. You are making sure the right people see the right request in time to answer it well. Responsibilities Receive and route Serve as the initial point of receipt for audit, review, and data call requests directed to the client organization. Analyze incoming request , identify what is being asked, and determine the offices and action officers who can answe r . Route request s to the correct point of contact with a clear statement of what is needed and by when. Acknowledge receipt to the requesting body and establish the point of contact relationship early. Identify requests that overlap with earlier or ongoing responses and connect them, enabling consistent answers from the organization. Track to completion Maintain a single authoritative tracker covering every open request: requesting body, scope, assigned office, interim milestones, due date, and current status . Manage multiple independent timelines simultaneously. Each request carries its own clock, and most don't align. Drive interim milestones rather than due dates. Build back from the deadline and check in against the plan, not the calendar. Follow each request through submission, follow-on questions, and formal closure. Produce recurring status reporting for senior leadership and be able to answer the status of any open item on request. Exercise judgment Distinguish requests you can own and those that need senior attention, and act on that distinction without being told. Elevate early, with a recommendation attached. Bring the issue, the options, and your recommendation on sensitive and high-stake audits . Recognize sensitivity in an incoming request , such as scope creep, an unusual data ask, a line of inquiry with broader implications , and flag it to leadership before the response is built. Identify where a request is unclear or overly broad, and work with the requesting body to scope it before the organization spends effort on the wrong answer. Analyze and improve Review draft responses for completeness, internal consistency, and responsiveness to what was asked. Read across requests over time to identify recurring themes, repeat findings, and areas drawing sustained attention. Build the intake process, tracker, templates, and operating rhythm that make a reliable process that will allow easy status updates . Maintain a retrievable record of prior responses so the organization can answer repeat question s in hours rather than weeks. Required Skills and Experience Bachelor's degree and a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant professional experience; or a bachelor's degree in a field related to this work and a minimum of sixteen (16) years of relevant professional experience. Background in legislative or congressional analysis, policy implementation and review, or other formal inquiry response work. Demonstrated experience coordinating responses to formal external taskers, data calls, audits, inspections, or congressional inquiries within a government or defense organization. Demonstrated ability to manage concurrent items on independent timelines without losing track of any of them. E xperience exercising judgment on audits, including when to escalate, reassign, reject, and submit materials. Strong reading comprehension for formal correspondence: the ability to determine precisely what is being asked and what is not. C oncise written communication suitable for senior military and civilian leadership. Demonstrated ability to work across organizational boundaries and to get responses from people who do not report to you. Discretion in handling sensitive and controlled unclassified information. Proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Word, Excel, SharePoint, and Teams. Ability to work effectively remotely in cross-functional teams. Ability to meet deadlines and produce quality work. Preferred Skills and Experience Direct experience supporting audits or reviews conducted by the DoD Inspector General, the Naval Audit Service, the Government Accountability Office, or a service audit agency. Familiarity with the audit lifecycle: entrance conference, fieldwork, notice of findings and recommendations, draft report comment , exist conference, and corrective action tracking. Experience developing or tracking corrective action plans and milestones through closure. Working knowledge of NAVSEA, the Navy, and the Department of War . Experience using ETMS2. Experience supporting senior military or civilian executives in a high-tempo environment. Experience building a tracking or case management process from scratch. Active Secret clearance is strongly preferred. Clearance Requirements Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements. Secret Clearance is required for continued employment. Must maintain a favorable background investigation at the Secret level for the duration of the assignment. Must execute a non-disclosure agreement within 15 days of hire. Work Location: Washington, D.C. ( Washington Navy Yard) Our company prioritizes the benefits of flexibility and collaboration, whether that happens in person or remotely. If the position is remote or hybrid, you may periodically work from a Pantheon Data office location or client site. If this position is assigned to a Pantheon Data office location or client site, you'll work with colleagues and clients in person, as needed for specific client requirements. Compensation The salary range for this position is $100,000 - $113,000. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range. Benefits Overview We are always looking for good people! Pantheon Data is committed to providing its employees with competitive salaries and benefits in order to increase employee satisfaction and productivity. In addition to our benefits, we also offer SmartBenefits through the Washington Metro Area Transportation Authority, where you specify an amount of your pre-tax wages be paid directly to your SmarTrip account. In some cases, tuition assistance may be available for continuing education expenses and certifications related to their position. Additional details may be found at https://pantheon-data.com/careers/ Pantheon Data Important Information All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law. As part of the application process, you are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to our Talent Team at Recruiting@pantheon-data.com or by phone (571) 363-4020. This company uses E-Verify to confirm each employee's work authorization. For more information, click here E-Verify Participation Poster

This role will monitor legislative and regulatory developments, track government funding opportunities, prepare briefing materials, and assist with grant and funding applications. The ideal candidate is a strong researcher and communicator who can translate complex policy issues into actionable business insights while supporting engagement with government stakeholders. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Monitor federal legislation, agency actions, and policy developments impacting critical minerals, domestic manufacturing, and supply chain security. item.title: Director Of Advocacy And Government Affairs Hybrid
item.description: Position Summary NFHA’s Director of Advocacy and Government Affairs leads the implementation of legislative advocacy campaigns and government relations initiatives that advance fair housing and fair lending. Reporting to the Vice President of Public Policy and Senior Counsel for Fair Lending, who works with the Executive Vice President to establish advocacy strategy and priorities. The Director translates NFHA’s approved policy agenda into coordinated action, manages relationships with government officials, coalition partners, and industry and recommends implementation approaches. The Director leads the planning, execution, and evaluation of NFHA’s legislative advocacy; develops and coordinates policy analysis and advocacy communications; and manages related project resources and reporting. The position exercises independent judgement in day-to-day implementation within approved plans, budgets, policy positions, and delegated authority. Essential Job Functions Education, Event Coordination, and Training Lead the planning, implementation, coordination, execution, and evaluation of NFHA’s advocacy events, such as Board Capitol Hill days, within the established advocacy strategy and objectives. Present at conferences and community events as assigned. Contribute to policy-related content at member trainings and conferences. Advocacy Campaigns, Implementation, and Coalition Engagement Provide input on advocacy priorities and lead implementation of approved legislative advocacy campaigns under the direction of senior leadership. Develop field advocacy strategies for approval, and lead their implementation. Provide technical assistance on policy and advocacy to external partners. Engage with NFHA’s coalition partners and industry on Hill priorities and coordinate coalition activities regarding the Hill. Represent NFHA in the Fair Housing and Fair Lending Task Force of the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights and other relevant coalitions. Build partnerships to advance fair housing and lending policy. Support the Executive Vice President and Vice President of Public Policy and Sr. Counsel for Fair Lending in managing the Governmental Affairs Advisory Committee. Policy Analysis and Government Affairs Draft testimony and written comments to governmental bodies, as directed. Analyze bills for rapid response for policy and legislative developments. Draft policy messaging materials, talking points, and reports. Draft policy briefs and contribute to publications. Lead Capitol Hill meetings; coordinate meeting preparation and follow-up, and support the VP in working on Administrative priorities in support of NFHA’s advocacy efforts. Draft comments on proposed federal regulations and coordinate review and submission activities. Logistics and Administration Participate in departmental planning and program development. Prepare required lobbying and disclosure reports and review supporting submissions for accuracy and completeness; coordinate final review and filing with the VP and designated legal or compliance advisors. General Responsibilities Other related duties as assigned. Qualifications and Competencies Bachelor's degree in political science, public policy, law, sociology, or related field required, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. At least 5 years of progressively responsible experience in advocacy, government affairs, public policy, legislative work, or a closely related field, including demonstrated experience leading implementation of advocacy initiatives or complex policy-related projects. Prior Director-level experience and direct staff supervision are not required. Background in civil rights, housing, lending, or related policy fields required Working knowledge of congressional process, federal legislative advocacy, Executive Branch processes, and agency rulemaking. Working knowledge of congressional appropriations and budgeting processes, including the ability to identify relevant funding proposals and explain their implications for NFHA’s advocacy priorities. Understanding of how legislative and regulatory development affects advocacy planning and implementation Familiarity with federal lobbying disclosure requirements and ability to identify matters requiring legal or compliance guidance. Relevant certifications in nonprofit management, advocacy or civil rights law are a plus. Ability to travel and represent NFHA at conferences and other events; up to 20%. Ability to work in-person at the NFHA office a minimum of 2 days/week. Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this role is $105,700 - $110,700 annually. Salary is commensurate with experience. item.title: Associate Political Director
item.description: Position Title: Associate Political Director Reports to: National Political Director Start Date: Immediately Location: Washington, DC (in person) Hours: Full Time, Exempt Position J Street's political program supports a rapidly growing national network of pro-Israel, pro-peace, pro-democracy advocates and donors who work to elect federal candidates that share our values and vision. JStreetPAC is the nation's largest pro-Israel political action committee, distributing millions of dollars each cycle to endorsed candidates. This individual will play a key role in the Political team's fundraising operations and donor engagement, as well as cultivating relationships with campaigns, candidates, and members of Congress. The ideal candidate is a self-starting, entrepreneurial thinker with keen political instincts, strong relationship management skills, and a track record of setting and hitting ambitious fundraising goals. 2-3 cycles of experience working on political campaigns, on the Hill, and/or for advocacy or political fundraising organizations is preferred for this role. About J Street J Street organizes pro-Israel, pro-peace, pro-democracy Americans to promote US policies that align with Jewish and democratic values, that help secure the State of Israel as a just, democratic homeland for the Jewish people, and that advance freedom, safety and self-determination for the Palestinian people. J Street focuses its work in three main areas: (1) Advocating and demonstrating support for pro-Israel, pro-peace, pro-democracy policies in Congress, the media and the Jewish community; (2) Endorsing and raising money for federal candidates who share J Street's agenda; and (3) Educating the public and raising awareness of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the two-state solution. Our Core Values At J Street, everything we do is grounded in three core values that guide how we work, collaborate, and show up for our mission. Impactful — We act with intention. We measure success not just by what we do, but by the progress we make and the change we help bring about. Adaptable — We treat every challenge as an invitation to think creatively, reframe the problem, and find a better path forward. Aligned — We are united by shared principles and an unwavering commitment to our mission. Our strength comes from believing in what we're building together Specific Responsibilities Political Fundraising & Donor Engagement Steward our high- and medium-dollar political fundraising programs Manage JStreetPAC's national events calendar and own the national conduit fundraising portfolio. Maintain trackers of political fundraising and giving progress in spreadsheets and Salesforce, keeping goal-to-actual data current for leadership. Political Program Support Foster and grow relationships with fundraisers, staffers, and partners across the political ecosystem to advance J Street's political work and reputation. Grow J Street’s political communication program Serve as a go-to resource for internal and external stakeholders on J Street's political and PAC work. Contribute to the organization's strategic political planning as a member of the public affairs team. Support the National Political Director and VP of Political and Digital Strategy on other key political priorities possibly to include J Street presence at the Democratic National Convention, other presidential engagement, and independent expenditure work Candidate Engagement Support day-to-day management of the endorsement process Create opportunities for J Street leadership to engage with endorsed candidates, including meetings and fundraising events during candidate travel. Required and Desired Skills and Characteristics 2-3 cycles of political, campaign, advocacy, or fundraising experience Strong familiarity with the motivations and dynamics that drive federal campaigns and political fundraising Proven ability to manage multiple projects and donor relationships with precision and attention to detail Strong relationship-building and communication skills, including with major donors and political stakeholders Comfortable working collaboratively across teams in a fast-paced political environment Experience managing spreadsheets (Google Sheets/Excel) and Salesforce or a comparable CRM required Formal education requirements are less important than relevant hands-on experience Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this full-time exempt position is $77,000-$87,000 The final salary offer will be determined after reviewing relevant factors, including but not limited to skill sets; relevant experience; internal equity; and other business and organizational needs. Our comprehensive benefits package includes: Unlimited personal time off Sick leave Generous parental and family paid leave (up to 12 weeks) Paid time off on many federal and Jewish holidays Health and dental and vision insurance Company-paid life insurance A 401k program with a competitive employer match and unmatched contributions Commuter benefits A Flexible Spending Account Health Savings Account with an employer contribution Professional Development Funding Six Week Paid Sabbatical J Street recognizes a staff bargaining unit affiliated with IFPTE Local 70, a union for non-profit workers. This position is included in J Street’s bargaining unit and is covered under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. Physical Requirements There are no extraordinary physical requirements for the essential functions of this role. J Street will make reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job tasks. Minimal travel may be requested and can be discussed if it presents a barrier to applying. To Apply Please submit: Resume Short statement of interest Contact information for three references Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the position will be filled as quickly as possible. Equal Opportunity Employment Applications are being accepted now and the position will be filled as quickly as possible. At J Street we value an inclusive, welcoming, and diverse workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to understanding and valuing each other's perspectives at all levels of the organization thereby creating a culture that allows us to better serve our employees, and the communities we work with. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law. This policy applies with regard to all aspects of one's employment and fellowship, including hiring, transfer, promotion, compensation, eligibility for benefits, and termination. J Street is an Equal Opportunity Employer

item.description: Coordinator, Operations & Outreach (SCCJS and Political Science) About Western Kentucky University: Western Kentucky University (WKU) is a student-centered, applied-research institution committed to providing its students with a transformative academic and social experience and to elevating its surrounding communities. Founded in 1906, WKU is the third largest public four-year institution in the Commonwealth of Kentucky with approximately 16,293 students and nearly 2,612 faculty and staff employees. Western Kentucky University is committed to empowering its campus community. At the heart of our mission, we seek to provide holistic education and employment experiences that prepare students, faculty, and staff to become effective scholars, contributors, and leaders in our ever-evolving communities. Located 65 miles north of Nashville, TN, and just over 100 miles south of Louisville, KY, WKU's main campus is in Bowling Green, KY - a city with approximately 70,000 residents. Our population is ethnically diverse, with more than 85 languages spoken in and around Bowling Green, and people from 35 nationalities call our community home. Western Kentucky University seeks to attract talented faculty and staff who are inspired individually to contribute to WKU's strategic plans and ongoing success. We offer comprehensive wellness and health benefits to employees and their families, including domestic partners and other qualified dependents and take pride in providing a workplace culture that supports balancing the responsibilities of work and family life. Paid-time off for holidays, vacation and sick leave, and a tuition discount program for employees and dependents are also provided. Learn more about WKU and Bowling Green at wku.edu/about . Job Description: The Potter College of Arts & Letters is accepting applications for an Operations & Outreach Coordinator to support the Society, Culture, Crime, and Justice Studies and Political Science Departments and will continue in that role within the newly formed School of Social Sciences beginning July 1, 2027. This position will work closely with academic leadership and faculty to coordinate day-to-day operations. This role requires initiative, attention to detail, and sound judgment in managing a range of administrative responsibilities. Duties include: Assist with coordination for recruiting, retention, and outreach events. Assist with coordination of marketing and promotional activities for academic programs. Schedule departmental tours for potential students. Oversee Faculty Load and Compensation process to ensure timely and accurate payment to all full-time and part-time faculty. Prepare departmental course scheduling in Banner. Support Graduate Assistantships by ensuring departmental budget accuracy, assisting with graduate assistantship forms, creating EPAFs and managing the onboarding process. Support the management of building, including classrooms, offices, common areas, and assisting on facilities projects. Ensure proper function of office and classroom equipment. Provide administrative support to department chairs and complete other special projects as needed. Communicate clearly and professionally both internally and externally from departments. Cross-train duties to provide departmental and college support when necessary. Supervise student workers to include hiring, onboarding, scheduling, approving timesheets and overseeing duties. Update departmental website and social media with new events and information. Other duties as assigned. Requirements: Bachelor's degree Additional Information: Hourly Rate: $19.49 Kentucky state law requires all public institutions of postsecondary education to conduct pre-employment criminal background checks to determine suitability for employment. Western Kentucky University (WKU) is committed to a policy and practice of providing equal employment and educational opportunities to all individuals. In accordance with Title VI and VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Revised 1992, and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, no form of discrimination or harassment will be tolerated at WKU on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, national origin, creed, religion, political belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, marital status, age, uniformed services, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, or physical or mental disability in admission to career and technical education programs and/or activities, or employment practices. item.title: Head Of Government Affairs
item.description: Founded in 2022 by Joey Levy and Jake Paul, Betr has built the world's first real-money gaming super app. The Betr super app currently consists of Picks, Predictions, Social Sportsbook, Social Casino, and Arcade, with Rips and additional products coming soon. Betr has one million paying users and is one of the fastest-growing companies in the industry, as well as the world's most-followed real-money gaming brand on social media. About the Role Betr is looking for a driven, entrepreneurial Head of Government Affairs to shape and execute our public policy strategy. Our business spans fantasy sports, social sportsbook and casino, skill games, prediction markets, and digital rips. We need someone who can stay ahead of developments across these categories, protect our existing products, and help create opportunities for growth. Reporting to the General Counsel and working closely with executive leadership, you will turn political intelligence into clear recommendations and action. You will set priorities, build relationships, manage outside lobbyists, and recommend where we invest our advocacy resources. This is a hands-on role for someone eager to take ownership, move quickly, and deliver results with limited oversight. Location: Strong preference for candidates based in Miami, Florida, or willing to relocate. Exceptional candidates elsewhere in the United States may be considered. Regular domestic travel is required for government meetings, legislative sessions, conferences, and other engagements. What You'll Do: Own our policy strategy. Develop and execute a coordinated state and federal government affairs strategy across our product categories. Stay ahead of developments. Track legislation, rulemaking, enforcement trends, and political shifts affecting our products. Maintain an actionable view of priority jurisdictions, key decision-makers, deadlines, and next steps. Build relationships and represent Betr. Develop credible relationships with legislators, governors’ offices, attorneys general and their staff, regulators, and other policymakers. Represent Betr at meetings, hearings, conferences, and industry events. Manage lobbyists and the advocacy budget. Select, direct, and hold outside lobbyists and consultants accountable. Set objectives, evaluate performance, coordinate messaging, and recommend how to allocate spending across jurisdictions and initiatives. Build coalitions and make our case . Work with trade associations, peers, and other stakeholders to advance shared priorities. Develop policy briefs, talking points, testimony, and proposed legislative language with internal teams and outside advisers. Keep leadership informed and drive execution . Provide concise updates on material developments, recommended actions, and progress. Partner with internal teams to align advocacy with business goals and carry initiatives through to completion. What We're Looking For 7+ years of relevant experience in government affairs, public policy, lobbying, legislative or executive branch roles, or political campaigns, with demonstrated responsibility for strategy and execution. Strong understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes, sound political judgment, and a track record of building relationships across party lines. Experience managing outside lobbyists or consultants, prioritizing across jurisdictions, and making effective use of a government affairs budget. A self-starter with urgency, initiative, and persistence. You spot issues, propose a plan, and follow through without waiting for detailed direction. Excellent writing and communication skills, including the ability to translate complex policy issues into clear business implications and practical recommendations. Strong organization, discretion, and judgment, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-moving business. Law degrees and legal experience are welcome but not required. We value substantive expertise, political instincts, and demonstrated results. Betr provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression. We deeply understand the value of bringing together a team with different perspectives, educational backgrounds, and life experiences. We encourage people from underrepresented backgrounds to apply Thank you for your interest in Betr. We look forward to reviewing your application. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

item.title: Vice President Government Affairs
item.description: Role Specific Information Job Description *This role can be based at either Kohl’s Corporate Headquarters in Menomonee Falls, WI, or in Washington, DC, with travel as needed. About the Role As Vice President, Government Affairs, you will act as the company’s political strategist and architect of our legislative and regulatory agenda. You will also ensure our commercial interests are prioritized within major industry bodies like the National Retail Federation (NRF) and the Retail Industry Leaders Association (RILA). What You’ll Do Execute a multi-year roadmap to address legislative threats and opportunities (e.g., AI, pricing, interchange fees, organized retail crime, data privacy, and trade tariffs) Act as the principal liaison to NRF, RILA and other key trade associations. Secure and maintain leadership positions to ensure the company’s specific voice drives broader industry mandates Provide leadership with real-time briefings on political shifts that could impact business, operational freedom, or global supply chain stability Maintain a deep and continuous partnership with the Legal and Risk Departments to ensure legislative advocacy is fully integrated with the company's broader legal strategy and risk appetite Ensure positions do not create legal exposure or contradict defense strategies in areas like antitrust or consumer protection Collaborate with the Compliance team to translate new statutes into actionable internal controls and provide early visibility into the rulemaking phase of legislation Partner with Human Resources to influence labor relations, wage and hour policy (FLSA), and emerging regulatory issues affecting the associate experience, such as workplace safety standards, predictive scheduling, and employee privacy Partner on "Extended Producer Responsibility" (EPR) and supply chain transparency (e.g., UFLPA) Translate regulatory changes into operational impacts for distribution centers and last-mile delivery Align advocacy efforts with brand "purpose" to mitigate reputational risk Additional tasks may be assigned What Skills You Have 10+ years in government relations, preferably with significant tenure in-house at a Fortune 500 retailer or as a senior strategist within a major retail trade association Deep understanding of the global retail ecosystem, including stores, supply chain, technology and risk management Proven ability to know when to lead a solo advocacy charge and when to leverage a trade association Ability to navigate conflicting internal priorities to find a unified corporate voice Preferred Master’s in Public Policy Deep understanding of how federal, state, and local regulations directly affect our business and the daily work and safety of our associates at both the store and supply chain levels Essential Functions The requirements listed below are representative of functions you will be required to perform, however you may be required to perform additional functions. Kohl’s may revise this job description from time to time. To perform this job successfully, you must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions, absent undue hardship. Ability to perform the accountabilities listed in the “What You’ll Do” Section Ability to maintain prompt and regular attendance as set by the company Ability to work at least 8 hours per day, occasionally longer when necessary to meet business needs, 5 days per week Ability to comply with dress code requirements Ability to learn and comply with all company policies, procedures, standards and guidelines Ability to give direction and receive, understand and proactively respond to direction from leadership and other company personnel Ability to work as part of a team and interact effectively and appropriately with others Ability to maintain composure and work in a fast paced environment while accomplishing multiple tasks within established timeframes Ability to satisfactorily complete company training programs Perform work in accordance with the Physical/Cognitive Requirements section Physical/Cognitive Requirements Ability to use a personal computer for tasks such as communicating, preparing reports, etc. Ability to plan, prioritize and monitor activities across business units Ability to complete or oversee the completion of assigned projects in a timely manner Ability to comply with health and safety standards

item.title: Public Policy Manager
item.description: Description Job Purpose The Public Policy Manager advances MHAMD’s behavioral health policy agenda through research, legislative advocacy, community engagement, and project management of priority initiatives. Reporting to the Chief Public Policy Officer, the Manager translates policy goals into actionable plans, delivers substantive policy work, and ensures timely execution across the team and its partners. Duties and Responsibilities Manage Maryland legislative-session activities, including bill tracking, hearing schedules, action alerts, testimony coordination, and follow-up. Represent MHAMD before the Maryland General Assembly, and serve on key coalitions, various external committees and workgroups as assigned. Prepare testimony, policy briefs, fact sheets, talking points, correspondence, and other advocacy materials. Manage efforts to facilitate and increase citizen action through rallies and public events, social media, advocacy campaigns, and other community engagement strategies Establish and maintain Public Policy teamwork plans; assign actions and set deadlines, track tasks, operationalize shared documentation, and establish practical reporting processes. Improve team workflows and use of digital tools. Coordinate meetings and cross-functional work with external coalitions, MHAMD staff and board committees, and other stakeholders; ensure decisions are carried through. Maintain the project plan, milestones, assignments, dependencies, records, and reporting deadlines for the newly awarded Maryland Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) apprenticeship planning grant. Complete assigned RHTP project deliverables and coordinate partner contributions, reporting, and financial documentation. Build expertise in workforce development and help position the apprenticeship initiative for implementation, partnerships, and continued funding. Requirements Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in public policy, government affairs, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience; master’s degree preferred. Experience researching and analyzing legislation, regulations, or public programs and producing clear policy briefs, testimony, or recommendations. Familiarity with Maryland legislative and political processes desired. Working knowledge of behavioral health or related health and human services policy, with demonstrated interest in advancing behavioral health policy. Familiarity with workforce development a plus. Experience independently managing projects with multiple workstreams, interdependent milestones, external partners, and measurable deliverables. Experience building and using project plans, action logs, reporting systems, and digital collaboration tools such as Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, and Excel. General Conditions Standard work schedule is Monday through Friday, with additional evening or weekend hours during the Maryland legislative session and for occasional events. Position requires substantial computer-based work and participation in meetings, hearings, and events. Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable law. Travel Requirement Travel within Maryland, including to Annapolis during the legislative session, and occasional out-of-state travel as required. Travel expenses reimbursed in accordance with MHAMD policy Benefits Full time, exempt, hybrid and benefits. Benefits include PTO, sick, and holidays, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability, 403(b) retirement plan, medical, dental and vision insurance, and health savings account. Salary $80,000 - $95,000 annually, commensurate with experience.

item.title: Political Reporter
item.description: Job Title: State Politics Reporter Georges Media Group, the largest media organization in Louisiana, seeks an enterprising reporter for one of the best journalism beats in the Deep South: Louisiana politics and government. Georges Media, a locally owned company with a track record of growth, oversees The Times-Picayune, The Advocate, The Shreveport-Bossier Advocate and The Acadiana Advocate. Our media brands have received five Pulitzer Prizes. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: We’re looking for someone who can cover the halls of power in and around Baton Rouge, a city whose politics are as delicious as its Cajun and Creole cuisine. You'd round out a team of talented journalists who cover the governor, the legislature, and various state agencies. You’d write about new laws, political campaigns, and factions warring for influence over policy changes that impact thousands of Louisianans. The ideal candidate will be a team player who is as committed to covering the people affected by state politics as they are to covering the big political players. You should bring curiosity, passion and creativity to the role, and have a history of breaking news and developing complex enterprise. We are a seven-day, home-delivered newspaper with a growing digital subscriber base. We are fiercely committed to our mission: to create impactful journalism that is indispensable to readers. Our news coverage, produced in four distinct markets, aims to hold the powerful accountable, unite our communities and celebrate Louisiana. We are also an equal-opportunity employer, committed to recruiting, maintaining and developing a diverse workforce while providing unique opportunities and career paths for our employees. List of preferred qualifications aside, we invite applicants of all backgrounds and experience levels to apply. This position offers a competitive salary and benefits package that includes medical, vision and dental insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, paid parental leave and 401K plan. Preferred qualifications: - At least three years reporting experience (state or local political reporting experience a bonus) - Strong writing and grammar skills - Curiosity about the topics you cover, dedication to the journalism you produce, and empathy for the audience you serve

item.title: District Legislative Aide District 33
item.description: General Summary The Office of State Senator Jonathan Martin is now accepting applications for a District Legislative Aide based in Tallahassee, Florida. This is work assisting a Senator with a variety of administrative and public relations matters requiring a thorough understanding of the policies, procedures, and operating practices of the Florida Legislature. An employee in a position allocated to this class performs duties of limited variety and complexity. Work involves the performance of various routine and non-routine tasks following clearly defined standardized practices. Results are reviewed upon completion for judgment, completeness, and accomplishment of objectives within deadlines. Financial Disclosure: Pursuant to sections 112.3144 and 112.3145, F.S., this position is required to electronically file a Form 1 – Statement of Financial Interests with the Florida Commission on Ethics within 30 days of hire. Examples of Work Performed Manages or assists in managing a district office and supervises other staff in all functions performed by district office. Serves as a liaison for constituents. Responds to inquiries by seeking solutions to problems or assisting in communication with appropriate agency. Performs research to gather and assemble information for drafting of bills, speeches, or special reports. Attends various local functions and meetings with supervisor to gather information, or on behalf of the supervisor, as a representative of the staff. Prepares and distributes press releases and other public information data. Supervises maintenance of district office files including selection of newspaper articles and other source materials for files. Manages district office expense account. Formulates replies to correspondence in draft or final form depending on the complexity of the issue. Advises supervisor of issues and projects in the district that require involvement to better serve the district. Reviews all correspondence, reports, and legislative proposals for accuracy and quality of content. May perform extensive background research on a bill in working it through the committee process.
