item.title: Associate Professor Of Political Science Oklahoma Baptist University
item.description: Associate Professor of Political Science - Oklahoma Baptist University OBU Mission Statement OBU transforms lives by equipping students to pursue academic excellence, integrate faith with all areas of knowledge, engage a diverse world, and live worthy of the high calling of God in Christ. Expectations for all Employees Oklahoma Baptist University achieves its mission through a shared commitment to the following expectations. All employees must embrace these expectations and model them in their behavior. Demonstrate commitment to the essentials of the Christian faith. Commit to the mission and vision of Oklahoma Baptist University. Treat people with dignity and respect. Build relationships on honesty, integrity, and trust. Strive for excellence through teamwork, leadership, and a strong work ethic. Manage human and financial resources wisely and efficiently. Purpose: Oklahoma Baptist University invites applications and nominations for a tenure-track position in Political Science, beginning August 2027. The successful candidate will teach American National Government, Introduction to Political Science, and upper-level courses in areas such as Congress, the courts, and the U.S. presidency. Other courses may be taught or developed according to the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs, subject to approval. A Ph.D. in Political Science is strongly preferred by the time of appointment; advanced ABD candidates will be considered. Strong candidates will demonstrate excellence or strong promise in undergraduate teaching, student mentoring, and contributing to a rigorous liberal arts education within a Christian university context. The standard teaching load is 24 credit hours per academic year. Responsibilities also include advising Political Science majors and minors, participating in departmental, university, and professional service, and assisting with recruitment through meetings with prospective students and families. The successful candidate will teach, advise, and serve in a manner consistent with Oklahoma Baptist University’s Christian mission and will thoughtfully integrate Christian faith with Political Science. The department especially welcomes candidates whose teaching and scholarship demonstrate respect for constitutional democracy, religious liberty, civil discourse, careful institutional analysis, and serious engagement with the Christian tradition. Applicants should submit a letter of interest addressing their qualifications, teaching interests, and fit with Oklahoma Baptist University’s Christian mission. Additional materials should include a curriculum vitae, statement of teaching philosophy, statement of Christian faith, graduate transcripts, and a list of references. Review begins immediately and continues until filled. Essential Functions: · Teach introductory and upper-level undergraduate Political Science courses. · Serve as an advisor to Political Science majors and minors. · Keep accurate class records and submit reports and grades. · Work regularly with faculty members from other disciplines. · Keep regular office hours for advising students. · Be an active member in a local evangelical church. Other Duties: · Maintain an active program of professional development. · Assist in recruiting students to the Political Science program. · Serve on university committees and take an active part in shaping the work of the division. · Support and guide students in research and practica. Required Qualifications: · Must be able to teach multiple Political Science courses, including ones covering the major branches of the government. · Possess and demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, communication skills, and pedagogy. · Be able to conduct a college classroom to maximize the student learning experience. · Be able to adjust teaching methods to meeting student needs. · Be able to work effectively with college students in either individual advisement, as well as small and large class environments. · Be able to relate to colleagues in the OBU community as well as be a representative to the professional community beyond OBU. · Be proficient in office technology, office software (including various Microsoft tools), and classroom presentation software. Education: · Required : PhD in Political Science (advanced ABD considered). · Preferred : Completed PhD in Political Science. Experience: · Preferred: Experience teaching undergraduates in a Christian, liberal arts environment. Special Requirements: · Must be a member of a local evangelical* Christian church. *Evangelical is a broad term referring to segment within Christianity which maintains the authority of the Bible and the belief in salvation by faith in Jesus alone. OBU Benefits Summary: OBU understands that our employees are our most valuable assets when fulfilling our mission. We strive to offer an extensive array of benefits and opportunities for employees to choose from. Full-time employees benefit from the generous OBU provision of premium contributions for nationwide family-friendly Health and Dental coverages along with free life insurance that includes accidental death and dismemberment equal to an employee’s base salary. OBU provides access to optional employee-paid ancillary benefits like vision, hospitalization, critical illness, accident, additional employee-paid family life insurance coverages, and education benefits at OBU and other institutions of higher education. There is generous paid time off that includes annual granted vacation time, accrued sick leave, six annual holidays, and week-long breaks for Thanksgiving and Christmas that include energy conservation days. For all employees working at least half-time, there is an employer matching opportunity for retirement investments in a 403(b)(9) plan administered by Guide Stone. There are numerous other perks and opportunities for OBU employees including FREE family membership to the OBU Recreation and Wellness Center or RAWC, Global outreach university mission trips, cafeteria discounts, and parking privileges to name a few.

item.description: Job Description WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY? The Senior Director, Strategic Execution and Business Operations, serves as the SVP's chief of staff and strategic right hand, ensuring alignment between departmental initiatives and organizational strategy while proactively managing risk and organizational effectiveness. The role acts as a trusted extension of the SVP, representing their priorities and perspective across the Global Affairs and Public Policy function and enterprise partners. Leading a small and evolving team, the Senior Director translates organizational strategy into executable plans, connects GA & PP initiatives to broader business objectives, maintains visibility into emerging risks, and drives disciplined operations and accountability. The role operates as a strategic advisor and trusted partner who challenges organizational assumptions, holds teams accountable without direct authority, and ensures the department operates with the rigor and excellence expected of a high-performing organization. WHAT WILL YOU DO? Strategic Partnership and Executive Support (30%) Act as the SVP's trusted extension, providing independent perspective, analysis, and recommendations on complex issues Prepare the SVP for key decisions and ensure alignment across the GA & PP leadership team Anticipate needs and proactively identify emerging gaps, risks, or issues before escalation Challenge organizational assumptions constructively and bring solutions, not just problems, to leadership discussions Strategy Execution and Portfolio Management (25%) Maintain clear visibility of how GA & PP initiatives ladder to broader RBC strategic objectives; flag misalignment and support reprioritization Translate organizational strategy into executable operational and enablement plans with measurable outcomes Manage the portfolio view, monitor program performance, and ensure focus on value delivery and business outcomes Develop, manage, and monitor the departmental budget and resource allocation; track spend against forecasts, manage variances, and ensure efficient resource utilization across the team and initiatives Oversee workforce planning, resources, and third-party arrangements Risk and Issue Management (20%) Build and maintain visibility into operational, delivery, regulatory, and reputational risks across the GA & PP portfolio Establish early warning mechanisms and drive timely escalation and resolution before issues become crises Hold teams accountable to risk mitigation commitments and ensure rigorous, frequent risk discussions Track commitments and organizational follow-through on decisions and timelines Operating Rhythm and Accountability (15%) Own the governance and decision-making cadence that keeps the department functioning: leadership meetings, planning cycles, reporting, forums Establish clear decision rights and accountability frameworks Track organizational commitments and hold teams accountable to agreed-upon deliverables and timelines Ensure efficient governance processes that add clarity to decision-making Communications and Organizational Effectiveness (10%) Prepare executive-ready materials including strategy narratives, business reviews, and decision memos that distill complexity into actionable insights Develop and deliver employee engagement and learning initiatives that build team capability, cohesion, and culture Oversee communication quality assurance and consistency with organizational priorities Support organizational design and talent development as the team grows WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED? Must have: University degree in business, policy, strategy, communications, or related discipline, or equivalent experience Minimum of 10–12 years of progressive experience in financial services, or corporate strategy/operations Demonstrated experience in a chief of staff, right-hand advisor, or trusted strategic partner role to senior leadership Demonstrated experience operating in a matrixed, complex, and highly regulated environment Nice-to-have : Strong track record managing risk and driving accountability across a complex portfolio of initiatives and work Proven ability to develop and execute strategy while maintaining operational performance and managing multiple priorities Excellent judgment and discretion; comfortable operating with visibility into sensitive, high-stakes information Demonstrated ability to influence senior executives and mobilize stakeholders across organizational boundaries without direct authority Experience in program management, portfolio management, or strategic initiative oversight Strong financial management and resource planning experience Excellent executive communication skills; comfortable distilling complexity into actionable insights for senior leaders What’s in it for you? item.title: Research Associate Economic Policy
item.description: Full-time Description The Cato Institute is seeking a Research Associate to join a team of researchers working on economic policy. The Research Associate will be responsible for supporting the R. Evan Scharf Chair for the Public Understanding of Economics in his research, communications, and administrative arenas. This position will help produce original policy analysis in multiple formats, including policy analyses, briefing papers, blog posts, and op-eds. The Research Associate will be an integral part of the team’s workflow, helping with new research, data analysis, econometrics, drafting and editing, and fact checking. The Research Associate will also support the team’s podcast production on The Economics of It , prepare scholars for live events, and undertake certain administrative tasks. They will have the opportunity to co-author certain pieces with other members of the team and will be encouraged to be a self-starter and remain on the lookout for good research ideas, timely news hooks, and new ways to promote Cato scholars’ work. This role is available through our two-year Research Associate program, where you’ll have the opportunity to learn from senior staff and featured guest lecturers across academia and the business community. With ample opportunities to attend these educational sessions, network with peers and scholars, and gain mentorship from some of the nation’s foremost public policy scholars, you’ll be well prepared to excel as a leader in policy, academia, government, business, and beyond. The Research Associate is a full-time, exempt position and will primarily report to the R. Evan Scharf Chair for the Public Understanding of Economics. This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC. The projected salary range for this role is $53,000 to $62,000 per year. Compensation is based on the successful candidate's educational background, experience, and skills. About Cato The Cato Institute is a public policy research organization—a think tank—dedicated to the principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace. Its scholars and analysts conduct independent, nonpartisan research on a wide range of policy issues. Founded in 1977, Cato owes its name to Cato’s Letters, a series of essays published in 18th-century England that presented a vision of a society free from excessive government power. Those essays inspired the architects of the American Revolution. And the simple, timeless principles of that revolution — individual liberty, limited government, and free markets – turn out to be even more powerful in today’s world of global markets and unprecedented access to information than Jefferson or Madison could have imagined. Social and economic freedom is not just the best policy for a free people, it is the indispensable framework for the future. Cato Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Responsibilities Support the research of senior members of the economic studies team, including through literature reviews, summaries of new academic and working papers, and collating original datasets. Collect, clean, and analyze economic and/or polling data and produce charts and data visualizations for publication. Edit and fact-check drafts of blog posts, op-eds, policy analyses, and books, verifying figures, quotations, and sources before publication. Support the team’s economics podcast and video content by researching guests, drafting interview questions and briefing notes, editing transcripts, and tracking audience metrics. Prepare scholars for events, media appearances, and live interviews by compiling supporting data and anticipating audience questions. Monitor new economic data releases, research, and news for timely hooks for the team’s work. Support the administrative and organizational needs of the economic studies team. Occasionally co-author policy analyses, working papers, peer-reviewed academic papers, blog posts, and other empirical work with members of the economic studies team. Requirements Education/ Experience A degree in economics, statistics, political science, or data science is required. Proficiency with Excel required; experience with econometrics via either Python, R, or Stata. Evidence of good writing skills. Skills Strong organizational skills, including the ability to work on multiple tasks both independently and as part of a collaborative team on a time-sensitive basis Strong writing and editing skills preferred. Experience and comfort in finding, cleaning, and analyzing economic data from sources such as BLS, BEA, the Census Bureau, and the Federal Reserve. Ability to explain economic research clearly to non-specialist audiences, in writing and for podcast, video, and event formats. Willingness to learn new tools, including data automation and AI-assisted research tools. Commitment to accuracy. Ability and willingness to challenge and question ideas. Interest in libertarianism. Familiarity with basic macroeconomic and microeconomic concepts. To Apply Please submit the following materials in one PDF file: CV/Resume. Cover letter optional. Two writing samples (research reports, working papers, peer-reviewed articles, dissertations, data memos, blog posts, etc.). Benefits Cato offers the following benefits: Health, dental, and vision coverage Retirement contributions Generous paid leave Professional development support Hybrid work schedule Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. This position does not offer visa sponsorship.

item.title: Voter Registration Clerk Elections
item.description: Description The Voter Registration Clerk performs clerical work assisting in preparations for elections and voter registration. Work involves registering voters and maintaining voter registration records. Employee is responsible for utilizing computer-driven data entry equipment to prepare and modify files, and for answering telephones and assisting the general public, including receiving payment for fees. Must be able to travel when necessary for county business. Examples of Duties Serves as Deputy Registrar and is responsible for duties associated with voter registration and election-related activities including registering new voters' name, residence, and party affiliations. Determines voter eligibility by checking records including DPS, State, and felony records and the voter registration system. Files registration applications and records data into computer files; printing and issuing voter registration cards. Maintains voter registration rolls, changing addresses of voters as notified, and deleting names of deceased persons or those no longer residing in county. Resolves Task Summary as assigned on TEAM, including Cancelled Application Maintenance, Possible Deceased, Possible Duplicate, Possible Felon, DPS Applications, Web Application, Address Confirmation, Duplicate Application Status, and Correspondence. Sets up and prints voter registration certificates in-house. Researches in voter registration system and other systems and records to determine voter eligibility for Election Day. Provides telephone support to early voting clerks and election judges for equipment problems and voter information questions/issues. Performs assigned clerical work such as document processing and/or record keeping in the daily operations of the department. Handles requests for information that may not be provided in a standardized format. Executes reports in voter registration system to produce reports and/or CDs for sale requests, and resolves issues in TEAM (Texas Election Administration Management). Regular and punctual attendance is required. Performs other related duties as required. Minimum Qualifications High school diploma or G.E.D and minimum one year of experience in a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and related experience required. Possession of a valid driver's license. Must be able to obtain a State of Texas driver's license within 90 days. item.title: Legislative Director Ohio Columbus
item.description: Americans for Prosperity (AFP) is the premier grassroots organization focused on advocating solutions to the country’s greatest challenges. We recognize that tens of millions of Americans are frustrated with the extreme partisanship in government that keeps common-sense reforms from being passed, and instead seek to stand with policy leaders who are committed to finding a better way. Americans for Prosperity is part of the Stand Together philanthropic community. As Legislative Director for AFP-Ohio, you'll lead our work at the Ohio Statehouse, serving as our state government affairs lead and lobbyist. You'll track and shape legislation, build trusted relationships with lawmakers and coalition partners, and use AFP's grassroots strength to move policy forward. How You Will Contribute Develop an annual legislative agenda that aligns with AFP's policy priorities and Ohio's opportunities. Track and analyze bills in the Ohio General Assembly, take support, oppose, or watch positions, keep the state team informed, and issue key vote alerts and testimony on priority bills. Build and maintain relationships with legislators, legislative staff, administration officials, and coalition partners in Columbus and across the state. Convene and lead coalitions at the Statehouse, including regular partner calls and clear task assignments, and lead campaigns on priority issues such as energy, K-12 education, and local government reform. Create your own path to wins by using coalitions, research, studies, and targeted campaigns to move legislation. Partner with grassroots, communications, and political teams to turn AFP's activist network into legislative impact. Develop and promote Ohio's biennial legislative scorecard. Work with AFP's national policy and government affairs teams, and flag emerging opportunities and threats. What You Will Bring Experience in legislative affairs, lobbying, public policy, or working in a legislative office. Strong working knowledge of how legislation moves, and Ohio's legislative process. Established relationships with legislators, staff, and coalition partners in Columbus. Strong written and verbal communication skills, and comfort testifying and representing an organization publicly. Ability to travel regularly within Ohio and a valid driver's license. Enthusiasm to contribute to Stand Together's vision and principled approach to solving problems, and a commitment to stewarding our culture , which champions values including transformation and innovation, entrepreneurialism, humility, and respect. Standout Candidates Will Bring Relationships with elected officials, community leaders, and organizations outside of Columbus. A proactive, entrepreneurial mindset: you take ownership and move work forward without heavy direction. Understanding of grassroots advocacy and how to use grassroots tactics to achieve legislative goals. What We Offer Competitive benefits: Enjoy a 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting, flexible time off, comprehensive health and dental plans, plus wellness and mental health support through Peloton and Talkspace. A meaningful career: Join a passionate community of over 1,400 employees dedicated to improving lives and driving innovative solutions to complex social challenges. Commitment to growth: Thrive in a non-hierarchical environment that empowers employees to discover, develop and apply their unique talents. Competitive compensation: Our approach rewards the value you create through competitive salaries and bonus opportunities, allowing you to share in the success you help drive. $70,000 - $100,000 a year For this role, the anticipated base salary range is $70,000–$100,000 per year. This role may also be eligible for additional bonus compensation designed to align total compensation with an employee’s overall contribution to the organization. Our Principles-Based Management™ (PBM) compensation philosophy is grounded in an individualized approach that rewards the long-term value each person creates for the organization. Compensation decisions are informed by a variety of factors, including relevant experience, capabilities, demonstrated skills, role responsibilities, and expected contribution. Consistent with this approach, base salary may vary within or outside of the anticipated range based on these considerations. Our Values: Working for an organization within the Stand Together philanthropic community is different from many other places. The culture is deeply rooted in Principle Based Management® (PBM®), a framework guided by the principles that drive human progress, such as dignity, openness, and bottom-up empowerment. PBM® empowers employees to be entrepreneurial, to innovate, and to continually drive transformation. We believe diversity fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. That is why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and strive to treat all employees and applicants with honesty, dignity, and respect. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

item.title: U S Public Policy Director
item.description: Who is USP? The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. Brief Job Overview The U.S. Public Policy Director is responsible for developing USP’s positions on priority U.S. regulatory and public policy matters that impact the quality of medicines, dietary supplements, and food, as well as broader public health priorities, and for leading the development of the evidence-based content that supports USP’s advocacy. The Director anticipates emerging regulatory and policy trends, leads the development of evidence-based policy content, shapes USP’s responses to policy and regulatory proposals, and develops policy and thought leadership materials that support USP’s mission and advocacy objectives. The Director ensures that USP’s scientific expertise and public health mission inform regulatory and public policy discussions, while translating external policy developments into strategic insights that support organizational priorities and decision-making. The role serves as a strategic adviser to USP leadership on emerging policy risks and opportunities and helps set and advance USP’s U.S. public policy agenda and is accountable for the quality and impact of USP’s policy content and strategy. This position requires extensive, senior-level experience in policy development and implementation within the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the Department of Health and Human Services, or another comparable federal department or agency, gained through direct government service or sustained substantive engagement. The successful candidate will bring the credibility and judgment to engage effectively with senior government officials, policymakers, industry leaders, academic partners, patient and public health organizations, and other key stakeholders. This position reports to the Vice President, U.S. Government and Regulatory Affairs and works closely with colleagues across Global External Affairs and the broader USP organization. How will YOU create impact here at USP? As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. The U.S. Public Policy Director has the following responsibilities: Policy Strategy and Content Development Develop USP’s public policy positions and advocacy priorities, and lead the process for developing, reviewing, and finalizing them. Lead the development and authorship of the policy analysis, recommendations, and written materials (for example, regulatory comments, white papers, and journal articles) to support engagement with government stakeholders and direct the work of external consultants who contribute to them. Lead USP’s internal process for aligning scientific, legal, regulatory, communications, and program leaders on policy positions and clearing them for external release. Identify and lead opportunities for USP to advance its mission through policy and regulatory engagement. Support the Vice President and USP’s government affairs team in external engagement by providing policy content, briefing materials, and technical expertise, and participate in coalitions and stakeholder meetings as appropriate. Monitoring and Regulatory Intelligence Lead USP’s monitoring and assessment of policy and regulatory developments relevant to USP’s mission and strategic priorities and determine which developments require a USP response. Provide strategic insights and recommendations to inform leadership decision-making and organizational planning. Advise the Vice President and USP’s senior leadership on emerging policy risks, opportunities, and priorities, and recommend how USP should position itself. Lead internal efforts to anticipate emerging policy issues and develop USP’s policy and advocacy strategies. Internal Collaboration and Leadership Lead cross-functional working groups and organization-wide efforts related to policy development and regulatory engagement. Present policy analyses and recommendations to senior and executive leaders and internal governance bodies. Lead the U.S. public policy work plan and priorities, including policy projects and policy work of external consultants and subject-matter experts, and ensure delivery against agreed objectives. Establish and track measures of the impact of USP’s policy work (for example, positions adopted, comments cited by agencies, and stakeholder alignment). Who is USP Looking For? The successful candidate will have a demonstrated understanding of our mission, commitment to excellence through inclusive and equitable behaviors and practices, ability to quickly build credibility with stakeholders, along with the below competencies and experience Minimum of ten years of progressively responsible experience in regulatory policy, regulatory affairs, public policy, or a related field, including at least five years in a senior or leadership role. Advanced degree preferred; equivalent experience may be considered. Demonstrated knowledge of the U.S. regulatory and public policy environment relevant to USP’s mission. Experience analyzing complex policy, regulatory, or scientific issues and developing policy positions, recommendations, and related written materials. Demonstrated success influencing policy development through evidence-based policy content that advances a clear point of view. Substantial expertise in one or more policy areas relevant to USP’s mission and strategic priorities. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives in a matrixed environment. Experience developing and implementing public policy, regulatory policy, or advocacy strategies. Experience leading projects and managing external consultants or subject-matter experts, with or without direct reports. Excellent communication, relationship management, facilitation, and consensus-building skills. Experience advising executive leadership, with sound judgment and the ability to influence senior leaders and external stakeholders. Ability to set priorities, manage competing demands, and deliver results in a dynamic environment. Additional Desired Preferences Experience working within a regulatory authority, standards-development organization, public health organization, life sciences company, or trade or professional association. Established relationships within relevant regulatory, policy, or public health stakeholder communities and experience working with government institutions or policymakers. Familiarity with global regulatory and policy trends and their implications for USP's mission and objectives. Familiarity with state policy or legislative processes. Supervisory Responsibilities None, this is an individual contributor role. Benefits USP provides the benefits to protect yourself and your family today and tomorrow. From company-paid time off and comprehensive healthcare options to retirement savings, you can have peace of mind that your personal and financial well-being is protected. Compensation Base Salary Range: USD $151,802.00 – $212,585.00 annually. Target Annual Bonus: % Varies based on level of role. Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate’s skill set, experience, qualifications, equity, and other job-related reasons. Third-Party Recruiters: USP does not accept unsolicited resumes from 3rd party recruitment agencies and is not responsible for fees from recruiters or other agencies except under specific written agreement with USP. Note: As part of the recruitment process, USP's Global Talent Acquisition team may contact candidates through a variety of communication channels, including Microsoft Teams, telephone, email, and WhatsApp (voice calls and text messages). These communications may be used to schedule interviews, provide updates on application status, discuss career opportunities, and answer questions about employment with USP. item.title: Elections Specialist
item.description: Description JOB SUMMARY This position provides specialized administrative support for county elections and voter registration functions. MAJOR DUTIES Provides support for voter registration functions; distributes voter registration information and candidate information; processes voter registrations and changes to voter status due to change of address, move out of area, or felony convictions. Serves as primary point of contact for poll workers; coordinates the recruitment and review of poll worker applicants; schedules and facilities poll worker training; schedules and facilitates Election Day poll worker activities; facilitates poll worker employment Provides administrative support for the Director and other staff; types, edits, and proofreads correspondence. Answers telephone and greets visitors; provides information and assistance; directs callers and visitors to appropriate staff. Processes documentation related to department payroll processes; reviews timesheets for accuracy and completeness; prepares payroll worksheets and reports and forwards for payment for poll workers. Processes incoming and outgoing mail. Maintains department files and records. Monitors inventory of department supplies and forms; purchases office supplies as needed. Performs related duties. KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED BY THE POSITION Knowledge of state and federal election laws. Knowledge of state and federal voter registration laws. Knowledge of county and department policies and procedures. Knowledge of department and county payroll policies and procedures. Knowledge of computers and job-related software programs. Skill in the provision of training to poll workers. Skill in the maintenance of files and records. Skill in oral and written communication. Skill in the provision of customer services. SUPERVISORY CONTROLS The Assistant Director of Elections assigns work through general instructions. The supervisor spot-checks completed work for compliance with procedures, accuracy, and the nature and propriety of the final results. GUIDELINES Guidelines include state and federal election laws, State Election Board rules, and board and county policies and procedures. These guidelines are generally clear and specific but may require some interpretation in application. COMPLEXITY/SCOPE OF WORK The work consists of related specialized duties. Strict timelines and regulations contribute to the complexity of the position. The purpose of this position is to provide specialized administrative support for county elections and voter registration functions. Successful performance contributes to the efficiency and effectiveness of election processes and compliance with all state and federal regulations. CONTACTS Contacts are typically with co-workers, other county employees, vendors, voters, members of the news media, and the general public. Contacts are typically to give or exchange information, resolve problems, and provide services. PHYSICAL DEMANDS/ WORK ENVIRONMENT The work is typically performed while sitting at a desk or table or while intermittently sitting, standing, or stooping. The employee occasionally lifts light and heavy objects. The work is typically performed in an office. SUPERVISORY AND MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITY This position assists in coordinating the work of seasonal, part-time poll workers. Qualifications Knowledge and level of competency commonly associated with completion of specialized training in the field of work, in addition to a high school diploma. Sufficient experience to understand the basic principles relevant to the major duties of the position, usually associated with the completion of an apprenticeship/internship or having had a similar position for one to two years. Possession of Georgia Registrar Officials certification. Benefits: Bi-weekly payroll 12 hours of PTO per month 12 paid Holidays Employee Assistance Program No-Cost Employee Health Clinic Health Care Plan, Life Insurance, and Long-term Disability Deferred Compensation, Voluntary Benefits Retirement - Defined Contribution Plan

item.title: Senior Manager Communications Global Public Policy
item.description: Job Title: Senior Manager, Communications, Global Public Policy Job Location: Washington, D.C. Salary: $148,000 - $185,000 per year Although we’re small, we’re mighty and influence and impact society at large positively. At SEMI, we offer opportunities to connect and interact with world leaders, industry legends, and rising stars. We help our members develop public and private policies to strengthen global supply chains and promote business growth and prosperity. Learn and grow professionally through career opportunities such as rotational assignments. Contribute by influencing and impacting an industry that is the foundation for innovation and positive change in areas like environmental sustainability, thought leadership, and workforce development. We take pride in offering work-life balance so you can live your personal and professional life to the fullest. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome all to apply Position Summary The Senior Manager, Communications, Global Public Policy will plan and execute communications, content and media relations strategies that elevate SEMI’s public policy and advocacy work, with primary focus on U.S. policy priorities and targeted support for global initiatives. Based in Washington, D.C., this role works closely with the Public Policy & Advocacy (PP&A) team while serving as part of Corporate Marketing. The Senior Manager will identify communications needs early, develop promotional plans, create high-quality content for corporate channels, and work with SEMI’s Corporate PR agency to support media strategy, press engagement, spokesperson preparation and visibility for SEMI policy priorities. This is a full-time, exempt position reporting to the VP, Global Public Policy & Advocacy and based in Washington, D.C. THE ROLE: Based in Washington, D.C., this role works closely with the Public Policy & Advocacy (PP&A) team while serving as part of Corporate Marketing. The Senior Manager will identify communications needs early, develop promotional plans, create high-quality content for corporate channels, and work with SEMI’s Corporate PR agency to support media strategy, press engagement, spokesperson preparation and visibility for SEMI policy priorities. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES: Communications Strategy & Planning · Develop integrated communications plans supporting PP&A priorities, programs, events, webinars, podcasts, member engagement and advocacy initiatives. · Participate in PP&A planning meetings to anticipate needs, identify communications opportunities and align messaging with policy priorities. · Translate complex policy, regulatory, supply chain, workforce, sustainability and technology topics into clear, balanced communications for government, industry and media audiences. Content Development & Promotion · Create content (i.e., written, visual, audio) for SEMI.org, newsletters, email campaigns, member communications, blogs, social media, podcasts, presentations, talking points, briefings, fact sheets and event materials. · Manage the monthly PP&A report, partnering with PP&A on content and Corporate Marketing on design, distribution and promotion. · Develop messaging that communicates SEMI’s policy priorities, advocacy impact and member value while maintaining a country- and company-neutral association voice. · Support executive communications, remarks, quotes, statements and briefing materials for SEMI leaders involved in policy and advocacy. · Monitor policy developments, hearings, agency actions and industry issues to identify timely communications opportunities and produce summaries for internal or external use. Media Relations · Work with SEMI’s Corporate PR agency to develop media strategies, storylines, press materials and outreach plans. · Support proactive and reactive engagement with trade, policy, business and technology press, including releases, statements, pitches, talking points and background materials. · Prepare PP&A spokespeople with message briefs, Q&A documents and issue backgrounders. · Track press coverage and communications metrics for PP&A campaigns and report results to stakeholders. Public Affairs Support · Support communications and promotion for SEMI policy events, webinars, briefings, member meetings, coalitions and policymaker engagements. · Lead marketing for the annual SEMI Washington Fly-In, including messaging, digital campaigns, website content, event materials, stakeholder communications and post-event visibility. · Track priority policy issues, legislation, regulatory actions, hearings and federal activities relevant to SEMI members. · Coordinate with PP&A staff to ensure materials are accurate, timely, reviewed and aligned with advocacy objectives. Cross-Functional Partnership · Serve as Corporate Marketing’s primary communications partner for PP&A, collaborating with Corporate Marketing, Program and Regional teams. · Support global advocacy communications, including the SEMI International Policy Summit. · Manage timelines, approvals, content calendars and stakeholder reviews for PP&A deliverables. · Build trusted relationships with internal teams, member companies, policy stakeholders and external communications partners. What Success Looks Like · SEMI’s PP&A priorities are communicated clearly and proactively through corporate channels in a member-driven, country- and company-neutral voice. · PP&A stakeholders view this role as a trusted Corporate Marketing partner who anticipates needs and turns policy activity into timely, high-value content. · Media engagement and thought leadership raise awareness of SEMI’s U.S. public policy work and global advocacy initiatives. Working at SEMI · Working at SEMI means joining a mission-driven global organization at the center of the electronics manufacturing and design ecosystem. Our employees collaborate across regions, functions, and industry communities to advance innovation, strengthen the workforce, support sustainability, and help our members solve shared challenges. Qualifications & Experience Required · Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, marketing, public policy, political science or related field. · 7+ years of experience in communications, public affairs, media relations, marketing communications or public policy communications. · Excellent writing, editing, proofreading and message-development skills, with the ability to synthesize complex policy and technical content for diverse audiences. · Experience developing communications plans, managing multiple projects, coordinating cross-functional deliverables and producing high-quality content under deadline. · Strong understanding of media relations, digital communications, email marketing, website content, social media and content marketing best practices. Preferred · Experience working in government communications as a press secretary, communications director, or similar role, and a strong understanding of how to develop and execute communications strategies in a fast-paced policy environment. · Experience with a trade association, government affairs organization, public affairs agency, technology company, or in a policy-focused communications role. · Experience in Washington, D.C. policy, advocacy or media environments and a strong understanding of the legislative and executive branch policy-making processes. · Exposure to semiconductor, technology, advanced manufacturing, supply chain or trade policy issues. · Experience working with PR agencies and supporting executive-level media engagement. · Basic visual content development skills for digital, social, presentation and event materials. · Willingness to travel periodically to SEMI Headquarters and events. ABOUT SEMI SEMI® is the global industry association connecting over 4,000 companies and 1.5 million professionals worldwide across the semiconductor and electronics design and manufacturing supply chain. We accelerate member collaboration on solutions to top industry challenges through Advocacy, Workforce Development, Sustainability, Supply Chain Management and other programs. Our SEMICON® expositions and events, technology coalitions, standards and market intelligence help advance our members’ business growth and innovations in design, devices, equipment, materials, services and software, enabling smarter, faster, more secure electronics. Visit www.semi.org , contact a regional office, and connect with SEMI on LinkedIn and X to learn more.

item.title: Director Public Policy Advocacy
item.description: Job Title: Director, Public Policy & Advocacy Location: Washington, D.C. Reports to: Vice President of Global Public Policy & Advocacy Salary: $185,000- $232,300 Department: Global Advocacy This position is open to candidates residing in U.S. states where the organization is currently authorized to employ individuals. Eligible work locations will be confirmed during the hiring process. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and maintain ongoing work authorization throughout employment without the need for current or future employer sponsorship. INTRODUCTION OF SEMI Although we’re small, we’re mighty and influence and impact society at large positively. At SEMI, we offer opportunities to connect and interact with world leaders, industry legends, and rising stars. We help our members develop public and private policies to strengthen global supply chains and promote business growth and prosperity. Learn and grow professionally through career opportunities such as rotational assignments. Contribute by influencing and impacting an industry that is the foundation for innovation and positive change in areas like environmental sustainability, thought leadership, and workforce development. We take pride in offering work-life balance so you can live your personal and professional life to the fullest. THE ROLE: The Director of Public Policy and Advocacy drives the development and implementation of strategies designed to advance SEMI members’ public policy objectives through strategic partnerships with government and other industry groups. This position will work with policymakers, member companies, and other industry representatives to ensure U.S. public policies support innovation and growth in the microelectronics/semiconductor industry and throughout the complex and differentiated value chain. This position will focus on leading advocacy campaigns related to the microelectronics/semiconductor industry that are central to U.S. innovation policy and international competitiveness, which may include some or all of the following: incentives, trade and export control matters, supply chain policies and workforce development. This is a full-time, exempt position that reports directly to the Vice President of Global Public Policy & Advocacy and is based in SEMI Washington, DC office . CORE RESPONSIBILITIES : Represent the public policy priorities of members to U.S. lawmakers, administration officials, and their staff: Work with government officials to facilitate understanding of a diverse, global, high-tech industry. Represent the association in coalition work with other industries to obtain shared desired outcomes. Directly participate in discussions to advance SEMI’s advocacy efforts, including but not limited to presentations, public testimonies, roundtable discussions, interviews, policymaker/lawmaker meetings, industry association meetings, etc. (development of material, prep, and participation). Provide management, training, motivation of employees as the Advocacy teams grows providing assessment of employee performance and helpful feedback and training opportunities. Develop and execute strategies required to advance SEMI’s U.S. policy priorities: Manage activities along timelines required to meet overall SEMI objectives and goals. Lead/facilitate internal teams and external collaborations as necessary to successfully develop and implement policy proposals and lobbying strategies. Work closely with other SEMI staff members, member company representatives, external stakeholders, and subject matter experts. Ensure association participation in government forums and industry group meetings. Manage programs to benefit member organizations: Oversee the planning, execution, and evaluation of programs, advisory committee or working groups under your purview. Ensure programs deliver measurable value to the association’s members. Collaborate with internal departments to align efforts and resources. Manage internal and external communications: Advise member executives and other employees on implications of pending public policy, draft policy papers, and supporting communications (including but not limited to internal communications, SEMI website updates, blog postings, articles, press releases, op-eds, testimony, talking points, meetings etc.) Develop presentations and report on activities to ensure thorough communications. Support the development/execution of communication and marketing strategies; work with and provide input/material to the SEMI Communications team. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: You have successfully advanced SEMI’s public policy objectives by effectively promoting the industry’s global interests, keeping member companies informed, and aligning policy makers with the industry’s positions. All activities reflect the highest degree of integrity and are aligned with SEMI vision and goals. You have successfully facilitated an efficient and effective two-way communication process to engage members. CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS : Strong verbal and written communication skills Strong problem-solving skills Strong organizational skills: ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and able to react to shifting priorities to meet business needs. Cooperative, flexible, team-oriented attitude Self-starter with strong, proactive work ethic and the ability to meet deadlines and commitments. Willingness to learn new tasks and a positive, service-oriented attitude. Be willing and able to travel both domestically and abroad. KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE : Bachelor’s Degree in public policy, political science, or similar fields; advanced degree a plus 9+ years of government or private sector public policy experience Familiarity with the issues affecting the semiconductor industry. Experience with developing and executing successful efforts to affect U.S. legislation/regulation and internal/external communication plans. Lobbying experience (must be willing/able to register as a lobbyist, as required) THE IDEAL CANDIDATE : The ideal candidate will be a self-starter with policy experience related to federal research programs and appropriations, excellent communication and writing skills and a demonstrated ability to work independently, think broadly, and develop strategic approaches to problem solving. ABOUT SEMI SEMI® is the global industry association connecting over 4,000 companies and 1.5 million professionals worldwide across the semiconductor and electronics design and manufacturing supply chain. We accelerate member collaboration on solutions to top industry challenges through Advocacy, Workforce Development, Sustainability, Supply Chain Management and other programs. Our SEMICON® expositions and events, technology coalitions, standards and market intelligence help advance our members’ business growth and innovations in design, devices, equipment, materials, services and software, enabling smarter, faster, more secure electronics. Visit www.semi.org , contact a regional office, and connect with SEMI on LinkedIn and X to learn more.

item.title: Congressional Engagement Associate
item.description: ABOUT US The Aspen Institute is a global nonprofit organization whose purpose is to ignite human potential to build understanding and create new possibilities for a better world. Founded in 1949, the Institute drives change through dialogue, leadership, and action to help solve society’s greatest challenges. It is headquartered in Washington, DC, and has a campus in Aspen, Colorado, as well as an international network of partners. CONGRESSIONAL PROGRAM The Aspen Institute Congressional Program is a nonpartisan neutral convener of world-renowned policy experts and bipartisan, bicameral groups of Members of Congress and their staff, focused on the pressing public policy issues of our time. Through our educational programs, Members of Congress and their staff work with policy experts to discuss, civilly debate, and develop policy solutions in private, off-the-record sessions conducted in the United States Capitol and all over the world. ABOUT THIS ROLE The Congressional Engagement Associate will work with the whole team to provide highly valued programming to Members of Congress and senior congressional staff members. The Congressional Engagement Associate will specifically be part of the Congressional Engagement team within the Aspen Institute Congressional Program, which includes the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement, the Program Associate, and interns. The Congressional Engagement Associate will support the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement with outreach to congressional offices, track legislation and impact from our educational conferences’ attendees, work closely with the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement on the programming, logistics, and execution of our Capitol Hill events, and complete other tasks as needed. The Congressional Engagement Associate may also get the opportunity to travel with the team to international destinations during our conferences. This is a term limited position set to last one year (January 2027 - January 2028). This full-time position has a salary range of $60,000 - $75,000. This position reports directly to the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement. WHAT YOU WILL DO Support Associate Director of Congressional Engagement with tasks assigned related to recruitment of Members of Congress or congressional staff for our conferences, such as crafting targeted invites or updating our congressional contacts. Attend and support the programming, logistics, and execution of the Program’s congressional breakfast series and congressional staff lunch series, with a particular focus on the congressional staff lunch series. This position will play a large role in the planning and execution of our senior congressional staff events focused on global health and development, artificial intelligence, energy security, and more. Track legislation, impact, and other actions proposed by Members of Congress and congressional staff who attend our conferences and Capitol Hill events. Regularly update Associate Director of Congressional Engagement on legislation that is tracked. Support Associate Director of Congressional Engagement and Finance and Grants Manager with tracking attendee data from our programs. Track post-conference surveys and outcomes for Members of Congress and report progress to the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement. Assist the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement with the Program’s outreach plans, including promotional events, to Members of Congress and congressional staff to promote our member breakfasts, senior staff lunches, and conferences. The Congressional Engagement Associate may get the opportunity to travel with the Program’s team to our domestic and international conferences. Conduct policy writing as needed. Complete other tasks as assigned. WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO THRIVE Minimum 3-5 years of relevant experience. Recent Capitol Hill experience or public policy experience is highly recommended. This position requires knowledge of the function and make-up of the U.S. Congress and the ability to engage with people of all political perspectives. Ability to be a team player who can also work independently. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, and familiarity with or easily trained in Salesforce. SurveyMonkey, iContact, Canva, and Leadership Connect experience is not required, but is a plus. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION The Aspen Institute offers a generous benefits package including health, dental, vision, and prescription benefits, retirement benefits, and paid leave. The Aspen Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all District and federal laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or protected veteran or disabled status and will not be discriminated against. The Aspen Institute welcomes individuals with disabilities to participate in its programs, including the interview process. If you would like to request accommodations or have questions about accessibility, please email hrsupport@aspeninstitute.org or call 202-736-2127 in advance of your visit. Requests for ASL or CART services should be made at least two weeks in advance when possible. We will make every effort to fulfill requests, subject to availability.

item.title: Supervisory Attorney Advisor Associate General Counsel For External And Legislative Affairs
item.description: Summary The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) is seeking an experienced attorney to serve as the agency's primary legal advisor on matters relating to requests for information and documents from key external stakeholders, including Congress or the Government Accountability Office (GAO) in connection with their respective oversight responsibilities. Duties Working closely with the General Counsel, the Associate General Counsel for External and Legislative Affairs will guide the agency's responses to oversight requests while navigating the agency's legal duties and its strategic goals and objectives. The position requires a capable legal strategist with exceptional judgment, preferably with past experience with congressional oversight, legislative affairs, and GAO. As Associate General Counsel for External and Legislative Affairs, you will: Serve as a key member of the General Counsel's senior management team and interact directly with high-level officials in connection with congressional and GAO requests; Spearhead the agency's responses to formal and informal congressional and GAO requests by preparing or reviewing correspondence, negotiating compliance with demands for documentary material, and providing advice on any complex legal issues that may arise; Conduct or assist with briefings of congressional staff, and prepare or assist in the preparation of testimony for congressional hearings; Closely monitor and advise senior agency officials of developments in Congress and associated oversight requests; Work with the agency's Office of Congressional Relations and Office of Public Affairs to develop communication plans in connection with congressional oversight; and Assist with other aspects of OGC's work, including by rendering advice on questions of law or policy and assisting with pending litigation, especially in cases that overlap with the subject of an oversight request. Requirements Conditions of employment U.S. citizenship requirement must be met by the closing date of this vacancy. This position is subject to a background investigation. Males born after December 31, 1959 must register with Selective Service. Possess a J.D. or LL.B. degree from an accredited law school. Member in good standing of the Bar of a state or territory - US, PR, DC. The position may be subject to completion of a two-year trial period. Trial periods are an extension of the hiring process. This position is not in the bargaining unit. If selected for this position, the agency will evaluate your fitness and whether continuation of employment advances the public interest before extending your appointment beyond the two-year trial period Financial Disclosure may be required. You may be subject to a one-year supervisory probationary period. Qualifications Minimum Requirements Applicants must have attained the first professional law degree (LL.B. or J.D.) from an accredited law school and be an active member in good standing of the bar of a state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, or a U.S. territory. Applicants must demonstrate excellent writing skills and be able to work effectively with other people, exercise sound judgment, and exhibit a strong interest in the work of the agency. Additional Requirements GS-15 Positions For attorney appointments: active member of the bar in good standing and 60 months of legal experience after graduation from law school. Note: Legal and nonlegal experience gained in the Federal Government before completing law school does not satisfy post law school experience. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Education This position has an education requirement. You must submit a copy of your transcripts. Unofficial transcripts will be accepted in the application package; however, official transcripts will be required prior to receiving an official offer. If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, visit: https://www.ed.gov/about/initiatives/international-affairs/recognition-of-foreign-qualifications Additional information This position is in the Excepted Service (Schedule A). Individuals applying for this announcement are required to complete and submit an online application and all supporting documentation through the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) application system, USAJOBS. Traditional rating and ranking procedures do not apply. Only experience and education obtained by the closing date of this announcement will be considered. Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. Opens in a new window Learn more about federal benefits . Review our benefits Eligibility for benefits depends on the type of position you hold and whether your position is full-time, part-time or intermittent. Contact the hiring agency for more information on the specific benefits offered.

item.title: Intern Congressional Program
item.description: ABOUT US The Aspen Institute is a global nonprofit organization whose purpose is to ignite human potential to build understanding and create new possibilities for a better world. Founded in 1949, the Institute drives change through dialogue, leadership, and action to help solve society’s greatest challenges. It is headquartered in Washington, DC, and has a campus in Aspen, Colorado, as well as an international network of partners. CONGRESSIONAL PROGRAM The Aspen Institute Congressional Program is a nonpartisan neutral convener of world-renowned policy experts and bipartisan, bicameral groups of Members of Congress and their staff, focused on the pressing public policy issues of our time. Through our educational programs, Members of Congress and their staff work with policy experts to discuss, civilly debate, and develop policy solutions in private, off-the-record sessions conducted in the United States Capitol and all over the world. ABOUT THIS ROLE The Congressional Program Intern will work with the whole team to provide highly valued programming to Members of Congress and senior congressional staff members. The Intern will assist with crafting policy briefing books for our conferences and will conduct other policy writing as needed, will collaborate closely with other team members to develop logistics for our domestic and international events for Members of Congress and congressional staff, and complete other tasks as needed. The Intern will get the opportunity to attend our regular breakfast series with Members of Congress and lunch series with senior congressional staff. This internship has a 6-month term, with an hourly rate of $20 and expectation to work up to 20 hours per week. The Intern will report directly to the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement. WHAT YOU WILL LEARN The Aspen Institute Congressional Program Intern will develop invaluable skills in verbal communication and writing, particularly with and for a bipartisan audience of members of Congress. The Intern will also learn congressional research skills (legislation tracking, creating targeted invite lists dependent on policy interest, and more), events planning and execution skills, and teamwork within an integrated program. The Intern will also be given the opportunity to apply skills gained in the classroom by writing memos for our team and outside audiences and will learn more about our organization’s programs, operating procedures, and concepts. The Intern will be given the unique opportunity to network and connect with Members of Congress, their congressional staff, and world-renowned policy experts. The Intern will also have the opportunity to connect with seasoned professionals who will support them as they explore career options within organizations like the Aspen Institute. WHAT YOU WILL DO Attend the Program’s congressional breakfast series and congressional staff lunch series if class schedule allows. Help Congressional Engagement Associate with tracking legislation or other actions proposed by Members of Congress and senior staff who attend our conferences and breakfasts. Interns and Congressional Engagement Associate will directly update the Associate Director of Congressional Engagement on legislation that is tracked. Assist Senior Conference Manager with logistics and operations for our member and staff conferences as needed. Assist Funds and Grants Manager with grant tracking as needed. Support Program Associate with briefing book preparation for our conferences which will be read by Members of Congress and world-renowned policy experts. Support the Congressional Engagement team with the Program’s outreach plans, including promotional events, to Members of Congress and congressional staff to promote our member breakfasts, senior staff lunches, and conferences. Conduct policy writing as needed. Complete other tasks as assigned. WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO THRIVE Must be currently enrolled in an undergraduate program at an accredited college or university in the Washington, DC area. Focus on public policy is a plus. This position requires some knowledge of the U.S. Congress and ability to engage with people of all political perspectives. Ability to be a team player who can also work independently. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel. SurveyMonkey, iContact, Canva, Leadership Connect, and Salesforce experience (or easily trained in) is not required, but a plus. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION The Aspen Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all District and federal laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or protected veteran or disabled status and will not be discriminated against. If you would like to request a reasonable accommodation regarding the accessibility of our website, a modification or adjustment of the job application or interview process due to a disability, contact HRSupport@aspeninstitute.org or call (202) 736-5800.
item.dc:creator: The Aspen Institute

item.title: Director Of Government Affairs
item.description: Washington,D.C. | Hybrid (Minimum 2 days a week in office) | Minimum Salary: $150,000, Maximum Salary: $170,000 The Century Foundation (TCF), a progressive, independent think tank, seeks a Director of Government Affairs with deep experience working in Congress to craft and execute our congressional affairs and partnership engagement strategies, and leverage TCF’s research and thought leadership for policy impact. The Director of Government Affairs will serve as an advisor, strategist, and connector to TCF’s executive leadership and policy experts, ensuring that TCF’s research and analysis reaches policy makers, their staff, and opinion leaders positioned to drive change. They will develop TCF’s government affairs strategy and goals, and execute on all aspects of Hill and partnership engagement, from building relationships on Capitol Hill on behalf of team members, to briefing TCF experts on developments on the Hill, to generating original and action-oriented communications materials to support the organization’s mission to improve working families’ lives and build an economy that works for everyone. The Government Affairs Director will also work to strategically place TCF, the executive leadership, and all policy experts at the center of major policy conversations in and outside Washington, D.C. This is an ideal position for an individual with established relationships with members and staff on relevant committees, and key players at peer organizations, a keen sense for how issues are likely to land with policy makers, and the ability to work across teams to help distill complex policy research and ideas into relevant, bite-sized information packaged for policy makers and key influencers. This position reports to the Chief of External Affairs and Special Initiatives, but will work across the policy and external affairs groups. This is a full-time position based in our Washington, D.C. office. About TCF's Values One in three Americans are skipping meals and medication to save money. Half are draining their savings to cover everyday expenses. Meanwhile, the richest 1 percent now hold nearly as much wealth as the bottom 90 percent. Powerful corporations jack up prices with impunity while billionaires write the tax code to their own benefit. When families can’t afford the basics and believe government only works for the wealthy, democracy itself becomes fragile. History shows where this leads: strongman politics, widening inequality, and the erosion of basic rights and norms. TCF is addressing the crisis facing working families and our democracy by fighting for policies that restore power to workers, families, and consumers and tangibly improve Americans’ daily lives. We’re using every tool at our disposal—from research and data analysis to policy development, polling, and messaging research to strong partnerships with movement and advocacy groups—to reshape markets and build an economy that actually works for working people. Responsibilities Update and execute on a comprehensive government affairs strategy to advance The Century Foundation's federal and state policy agenda across education, labor, health care, and the economy. Cultivate and strengthen relationships with key congressional and government contacts, including staff and members, to drive meaningful legislative action. Brief the TCF team on Hill and administration news and developments, and advise in real time on effective congressional engagement strategies. Generate high-impact written materials, including talking points, emails, and policy summaries, informed by The Century Foundation's research, to educate and equip policy makers and their staff. Organize, lead, and participate in effective and timely briefings, meetings, and events on Capitol Hill to advance TCF’s legislative priorities. Brief TCF experts on developments on the Hill, and in the administration relevant to our work and identify opportunities for impact. Manage and mentor team members on a project basis to advance TCF’s government affairs goals. From time to time, support state or local level lobbying efforts on a case-by-case basis. Manage TCF’s tracking and compliance systems and maintain accurate and timely 501c3 lobbying reporting. Map and maintain external organization relationships relevant to economic, labor, healthcare, and education policy, among other areas. Qualifications At least 10 years of experience working on or with Capitol Hill to effect public policy change, ideally with multiple years of experience working in a Hill office. Deep understanding of congressional and administrative policymaking and procedures. A robust network of contacts in congressional offices and on relevant committees including, but not limited to: Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP); House Education and the Workforce; Senate Finance; House Energy and Commerce; Senate Budget; and House/Senate Appropriations. Experience leading government affairs at a 501c3 non-profit preferred, with knowledge of lobbying compliance. Excellent communication skills, including experience producing policy briefings and fact sheets, as well as persuasive messaging tailored to specific target audiences. Strong analytical and organizational skills, keen attention to detail, and willingness to learn new skills or techniques. Dedication to building a stronger, more equitable, and more inclusive society. A commitment to progressive values and interest in TCF’s research agenda. Compensation and Benefits TCF offers a competitive compensation package, with a salary range determined by years of experience, skills, and abilities. Each candidate’s placement within the range will be based on these factors while ensuring alignment with our commitment to equitable internal pay practices. TCF is a unionized workplace and is represented by the Communications Workers of America (CWA1180). This position is not in the bargaining unit. This is a hybrid work position to be based in Washington, D.C. TCF’s benefits include health, dental. vision, and life insurance, and an employer-funded health reimbursement account (HRA). This benefit package is in addition to generous vacation, sick and personal days, an employer matching 403(b) plan, and up to fourteen weeks family medical leave. The salary range for this position is $150,000–170,000. Please apply with a resume, cover letter, and two writing examples (three to five pages maximum) via BambooHR. No inquiries by third-party vendors and no phone calls, please. If you have any issues accessing the hiring portal, please reach out with questions to hr@tcf.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The deadline for submission of application materials is December 7, 2026. The Century Foundation is committed to diversity and building an inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds. Everyone is encouraged to apply, including women, LGBTQIA people, people of color, and people with disabilities. Applicants must be eligible to work in the United States. About TCF The Century Foundation is a progressive, independent think tank that conducts research, develops solutions, and drives policy change to make people’s lives better. We pursue economic, racial, gender, and disability equity in education, healthcare, and work, and promote U.S. foreign policy that fosters international cooperation, peace, and security. TCF has offices in New York City and Washington, D.C. You can learn more at tcf.org.
