item.title: Public Policy Manager
item.description: Government affairs plays a strategic role at Istari, advancing the company's federal strategy, securing funding, supporting business development, and building relationships across Congress, federal agencies, and industry. Reporting to the Director of Government and External Affairs and working closely with executive leadership, the Policy Analyst will own key policy issues, conduct independent research, and develop strategies that advance Istari's priorities. This role requires strong analytical judgment, initiative, and the ability to translate complex policy developments into strategic opportunities at the intersection of national security, emerging technology, and federal policy. Core Responsibilities Manage key policy portfolios, independently monitoring developments, assessing implications, and recommending strategic actions. Lead research and analysis of federal legislation, appropriations, authorizations, executive branch initiatives, and regulatory developments. Develop policy positions, legislative proposals, and engagement strategies aligned with Istari's business and technology objectives. Identify federal funding opportunities, emerging government priorities, and policy initiatives that support business development and market expansion. Analyze congressional and agency priorities, federal budgets, and defense programs to identify opportunities and risks. Lead specific government affairs initiatives, managing research, stakeholder engagement, and execution from start to finish. Build and maintain relationships with congressional offices, federal agencies, industry organizations, and strategic partners. Produce substantive policy analyses, position papers, and strategic recommendations to inform leadership decisions. Represent Istari at congressional meetings, agency engagements, conferences, and industry events. Collaborate with business development, product, and engineering teams to connect policy priorities with customer needs and company strategy. Coordinate strategic engagements and cross-functional initiatives, ensuring accountability and follow-through. Required Qualifications 3–5 years of experience in public policy, government affairs, congressional offices, federal agencies, lobbying, or a related field. Bachelor's degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Government, International Affairs, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience). Strong understanding of Congress, the Executive Branch, federal budgeting, and the policymaking process. Demonstrated ability to independently research complex policy issues, assess implications, and develop actionable recommendations. Excellent analytical, written, and verbal communication skills. Experience managing policy initiatives, legislative priorities, or research portfolios with limited oversight. Strong judgment, initiative, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities independently. Experience engaging with congressional staff, federal officials, senior executives, and external stakeholders. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace; CRM experience preferred. Interest or experience in aerospace, defense, national security, artificial intelligence, or emerging technologies. Willingness to travel up to 25%. Preferred Experience Experience in a congressional office, federal agency, think tank, government affairs firm, or in-house policy team. Familiarity with federal appropriations, authorizations, defense budgeting, and acquisition policy. Experience developing legislative proposals, policy recommendations, or government engagement strategies. Experience connecting policy developments to business development opportunities and organizational strategy. About Istari Digital Istari is a digital engineering software company building open, scalable infrastructure for engineering data. Our platform lets customers simply and securely integrate engineering models across disciplines, organizations, and security levels — whether they're designing prototypes, performing virtual testing, or training AI and autonomy for complex systems. Focus is rewarded. Finish is remembered. Facts are friendly. Even when they are not fun. Fellowship is fundamental. Make others successful. $80,000 - $100,000 a year The anticipated compensation range for this position may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, location, and business needs. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

item.title: Legislative Affairs Manager
item.description: Sierra Space Careers: At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth. Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond. Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space. We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team. About the Role The Legislative Affairs Manager is a key member of the Government Relations team. The role conducts advanced research, analyzes data, and develops strategies to influence public policy and legislative action. The manager brings extensive experience in government operations, policy analysis, and public affairs. The role focuses on the U.S. Federal budget process and on legislative activity related to the Department of Defense (DoD) and NASA. The manager also represents Sierra Space at industry events, in government meetings, and with customer audiences. In that capacity, the manager acts as a credible, knowledgeable voice for the company with external stakeholders. The Legislative Affairs Manager conducts advanced research on the legislative, regulatory, and policy issues that affect the organization. The manager monitors and analyzes federal government activity, including legislation, regulations, and budget processes, with particular attention to DoD and NASA programs. The manager tracks and reports on key legislative and regulatory developments. The manager also prepares detailed reports, briefs, and presentations that give the Government Relations team clear, actionable insight. Building on this analysis, the manager develops and implements advocacy strategies and campaigns. The manager keeps current knowledge of how decision-making authority is structured within legislative and National Security organizations. This knowledge helps the team direct its efforts to the right people and offices. This role represents Sierra Space at industry events, government meetings, and customer engagements. The manager supports the company's work with government officials, agencies, and other stakeholders. Internally, the manager handles multiple tasks and competing deadlines and delivers assignments on time. The manager also leads and mentors junior members of the Government Relations team, helping build their skills and strengthen the team's overall capability. About You Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission. We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum Qualifications: Requires a Bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree or Masters +3 years of experience). Typically 5+ years of related experience, including time as staff on Capitol Hill or within U.S. government agencies and/or National Security organizations. Demonstrated experience analyzing and influencing the U.S. federal budgeting process. Ability to represent Sierra Space externally at industry events, government meetings, and/or with customer audiences. Strong project and process management skills. Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines. Excellent communication and organizational skills. Preferred Qualifications: Previous work experience in government relations, public policy, or a related field. Familiarity with legislative tracking tools and databases. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Experience in the aerospace and defense industry. Knowledge of key issues and trends in aerospace and defense policy. Understanding of the procurement processes and funding mechanisms within DoD and NASA. Experience with advocacy and lobbying efforts related to aerospace and defense. Proficiency in using data analysis tools and software relevant to government relations. Compensation : Pay Range: $101,680.00 - $139,810.00 Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness. Elevate Your Career At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations. We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more. Sierra Space is an industry-leading space and defense technology company providing satellites, spacecraft, and enabling mission systems and components. We deliver mission-proven technologies to our customers that safeguard our nation, protect space-based assets and enable space exploration. Application Deadline: This role will remain posted until a qualified pool of candidates is identified. Please note: Sierra Space does not accept unsolicited resumes from contract agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to our website or to Sierra Space team members not through our approved vendor list or Talent Acquisition will be considered property of Sierra Space, and we will not be obligated to pay any referral fees. Sierra Space Corporation is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need special assistance or a reasonable accommodation related to applying for employment with Sierra Space or at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us .

item.title: Congressional Liaison Representative
item.description: Summary Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below to view Eligibilities being considered and other IMPORTANT information. The primary purpose of the position is to serve as a Congressional Liaison Representative who is responsible for planning and scheduling Congressional engagements for the Department of the Air Force Senate Office and House Office in the Directorate of Legislative Liaison. Duties Represents the Secretary of the Air Force in liaison activities with Members of Congress and their staff members concerning all aspects of DAF operations. Participates in planning, organizing, and executing duties related to DAF liaison with the United States Congress. Serves as the primary focal point for scheduling, reporting, monitoring, and coordinating courtesy calls, program briefings, and other meetings between the SECAF, USECAF, CSAF, VCSAF, CSO, VCSO, all DAF commanders, Joint Commanders, and other DAF leadership with Members of the Senate and House, their staffs and committees. As a Congressional Liaison Representative, provides executive support to the Division Chief of the Senate and House Liaison offices and acts as a liaison from the LLS/LLH Division Chief to the Director and Deputy Director of the Legislative Liaison and other organizational personnel to include DAF House and Senate liaison staff as required to accomplish administrative functions. Represents the organization and maintains a continuous liaison with other DAF offices, Office of the Secretary of Defense, Joint Staff, other Services, Congressional Members and Congressional staff members to ensure informed decision making by senior DAF leadership. Represents SAF/LLS/LLH with a variety of organizations. Requirements Conditions of employment U.S. Citizenship Required Males must be registered for Selective Service, see www.sss.gov If authorized, PCS will be paid IAW JTR and AF Regulations. If receiving an authorized PCS, you may be subject to completing/signing a CONUS agreement. More information on PCS requirements, may be found at: https://afciviliancareers.com/regulatory/ This position is subject to provisions of the DoD Priority Placement Program Disclosure of Political Appointments Depending on the type of position (competitive/excepted) you are selected for, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period OR 2-year trial period. Upon completion of your probationary/trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest. The incumbent must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret Clearance. The employee may be required to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evenings, weekends, and/or holidays. May travel by military or commercial air to conferences, meetings, or other functions away from the duty site. Qualifications In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-11, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience include: 1) coordinating protocol activities and procedures applicable to Congressional Members and other distinguished visitors; 2) applying analytical and research processes to establish options and propose courses of action; 3) responding to official requests for information or complaints received from the members of Congress and their staffs. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Thorough knowledge of the Air Force mission, organization (Air Staff and Secretariat functions as well as general Air Force command structure), and congressional game plan to facilitate rapid and accurate responses to congressional inquiries and other congressional requests. General knowledge of congressional procedures and expert knowledge of congressional organization and associated committee structure for authorizing the defense budget. Thorough knowledge of diplomatic, official, and social protocol policies and procedures to facilitate distinguished visitor visits to Capitol Hill and other official events/functions. Ability to define and identify the various forms and procedures that constitute proper protocol. Knowledge of protocol procedures including specifics of distinguished visitor and Congressional travel. Excellent written and oral communications skills are required due to the high visibility and sensitive work accomplished by this office. Ability to elicit information from others and present findings in a logical sequence. Insight, judgment, and diplomacy are critical skills necessary for establishing and maintaining an effective relationship with DoD and Congressional contacts. Ability to organize and coordinate multiple tasks and assure timely completion. Ability to collaborate effectively across organizations. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Education This job does not have an education qualification requirement. item.title: Government Relations Defense Appropriations Lobbyist
item.description: Date Posted: 2026-11-17 Country: United States of America Location: US-VA-ARLINGTON-108 ~ 1100 Wilson Blvd ~ ROSSLYN HQ Position Role Type: Onsite U.S. Citizen, U.S. Person, or Immigration Status Requirements: Active and transferable U.S. government issued security clearance is required prior to start date.​ U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance​ Security Clearance Type: DoD Clearance: Top Secret Security Clearance Status: Active and existing security clearance required on day 1 At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense. RTX is looking for a talented Government Relations, Defense Appropriations Lobbyist to join our Global Government Relations team in Arlington, VA! This position will lead a Military Service account-focused federal government relations lobbying portfolio for all three RTX businesses (Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon). This lobbyist will foster relationships with the U.S. government and internal RTX business leaders while raising the RTX profile. This lobbyist will develop overall RTX government relations strategies, with an emphasis on the assigned Military Service portfolio across all three business areas, as well as promote and oversee RTX legislative priorities to the Appropriations Committees of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. What You Will Do: Lead Military Service-related Appropriations government relations efforts throughout the U.S. by identifying and supporting policymaking and funding opportunities that advance the objectives and successful execution of all related RTX programs. Develop and implement a comprehensive government relations strategy with respect to the portfolio to successfully achieve RTX legislative priorities particularly related to (but not limited to) additional funding from the Appropriations Committees of the House of Representatives and the Senate. Advise the Presidents of the three RTX business units and other senior business leaders on all federal legislative matters that may affect the successful execution and funding of their programs. Develop and maintain relationships with key U.S. government customers/officials to identify opportunities of aligned interest, shape requirements, and influence laws and regulations in support of all RTX related products and services. Collaborate with the Appropriations Team Lead to enhance RTX’s presence in Washington, D.C. with respect to assigned programs to create a national platform on which these programs’ positions, requirements, and priorities can be articulated. Provide insight, guidance, and support to RTX program managers, their direct reports, the Senior Vice President for Global Government Relations, and other key company leaders on program standing on budgetary, legislative, and regulatory matters being considered by Members of Congress, their staffs, and the Appropriations Committees of the House of Representatives and the Senate. Coordinate and integrate Appropriations legislative affairs activities with all other lobbying activities across Global Government Relations. Build and maintain strong relationships with internal business functions and work proactively to keep them well-informed about political, legislative, and regulatory developments impacting their programs. Coordinate internally with the Appropriations Team Lead and the Manager of RTXPAC to develop a strategy and attend events in support of the company’s political action committee. Represent RTX interests on Capitol Hill at hearings, help prepare company leaders for Hill testimony when required, and provide briefings to Members of Congress, their staff, and key congressional committee professional staff on RTX programs. Qualifications You Must Have: Typically requires a University Degree and minimum 14 years prior relevant experience or an Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 12 years of experience. Active Top Secret Security Clearance. Demonstrated knowledge of defense legislative processes and associated funding mechanisms such as the annual appropriations bills and the National Defense Authorization Act. Demonstrated proficiency and understanding of U.S. military concepts, programs, and terminology. Previous experience working on Capitol Hill, particularly on the annual appropriations bills. Demonstrated capacity to operate independently across a highly matrixed organization, with strong research, writing, and communication skills. What We Offer: Some of our competitive benefits package includes: Medical, dental, and vision insurance Three weeks of vacation for newly hired employees Generous 401(k) plan that includes employer matching funds and separate employer retirement contribution, including a Lifetime Income Strategy option Tuition reimbursement program Student Loan Repayment Program Life insurance and disability coverage Optional coverages you can buy pet insurance, home and auto insurance, additional life and accident insurance, critical illness insurance, group legal, ID theft protection Birth, adoption, parental leave benefits Ovia Health, fertility, and family planning Adoption Assistance Autism Benefit Employee Assistance Plan, including up to 10 free counseling sessions Healthy You Incentives, wellness rewards program Doctor on Demand, virtual doctor visits Bright Horizons, child and elder care services Teladoc Medical Experts, second opinion program This position may be eligible for relocation. And more! Learn More & Apply Now! *Please ensure the role type (defined below) is appropriate for your needs before applying to this role. Onsite: Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products. Location: Arlington, VA As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote. The salary range for this role is 204,800 USD - 389,200 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills. Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance. This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply. RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window. RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act. item.title: Legislative And Public Communications Manager
item.description: Summary The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the principal legislative liaison and public communication (L&PC) manager providing sound/timely L&PC advice/guidance to the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force (Installations, Environment & Logistics), the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary, the four Deputy Assistant Secretaries for Installations, Environment, Energy and Logistics, other Headquarters Air Force leaders, and advisory/strategy groups, on a broad portfolio of issues. Duties Plans, organizes and oversees the activities of the Congressional Liaison/Public Communications requirement. Acts as the senior congressional advisor for Assistant Secretary (Installations, Environment, & Logistics), Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary and the four DASs, providing in-depth analysis, technical expertise and advice on the development or interpretation of congressional budget cycle legislation, executive orders, guidelines, and policies derived from Congress. Manage SAF/IE congressional/public affairs information processes. Incumbent serves as a representative for the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force (Installations, Environment & Logistics) during meetings with congressional staffers, OSD, other military services and federal and state government agencies and community groups. Incumbent attends meetings, seminars, and workshops to remain proficient on developments within the installations, environment, logistics, and energy fields. Requirements Conditions of employment U.S. Citizenship Required Males must be registered for Selective Service, see www.sss.gov If authorized, PCS will be paid IAW JTR and AF Regulations. If receiving an authorized PCS, you may be subject to completing/signing a CONUS agreement. More information on PCS requirements, may be found at: https://afciviliancareers.com/regulatory/ This position is subject to provisions of the DoD Priority Placement Program Disclosure of Political Appointments Advance in hire may be authorized if there is demonstrable proof provided on your resume Leave accrual may be authorized upon request Depending on the type of position (competitive/excepted) you are selected for, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period OR 2-year trial period. Upon completion of your probationary/trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest. This position is managed by the Air Force Civil Engineer Career Program. Employee must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance. Qualifications In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions . SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-14, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes knowledge of analytical and evaluative methods plus a thorough understanding of how regulatory or enforcement programs are administered to select and apply appropriate program evaluation and measurement techniques in determining the extent of compliance with rules and regulations issued by the agency, or in measuring and evaluating program accomplishments involving congressional liaison and public communications activities. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-14 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-15 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Comprehensive knowledge of installations issues; strategic basing of weapon systems; encroachment; military construction; housing and housing privatization; design, construction and maintenance and repair of facilities and infrastructure, the acquisition and disposal of real property/real estate, operations of utility systems, environmental cleanup, compliance, and pollution prevention, operational and facility energy, Base Realignment and Closure, and logistics issues including weapon systems sustainment, life cycle management of weapons systems, and product support. 2. Knowledge of L&PC principles, methods, practices, techniques, governing L&PC operations/public law, policies, governing directives/precedents and execution experience in all facets of integrated L&PC strategies, plans, programs, processes, activities, product development.3. Knowledge of AF/DoD missions, roles, functions, org structures/relationships, operational planning objectives. 4. Knowledge of PPBES and its linkages to Congressional budget cycle. Skill in methods/techniques to develop/evaluate written materials; research/analyze concepts; ID problems & recognize solutions; prepare, approve L&PC materials for audiences with various levels of understanding/interest. 5. Skill in communicating effectively with tact/diplomacy, orally and in writing, to effectively explain programs, functions, activities and gain understanding of organization's efforts by concerned public; to negotiate complex issues, programs, functions with people having varying levels of understanding of Air Force program 6. Ability to evaluate/assess program effectiveness, prepares reports on accomplishment, lead detailed integration effort, and develop recommendations while representing wide variety of viewpoints. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Education IF USING EDUCATION TO QUALIFY: If position has a positive degree requirement or education forms the basis for qualifications, you MUST submit transcriptswith the application. Official transcripts are not required at the time of application; however, if position has a positive degree requirement, qualifying based on education alone or in combination with experience, transcripts must be verified prior to appointment. An accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education must accredit education. Click here to check accreditation. FOREIGN EDUCATION: Education completed in foreign colleges or universities may be used to meet the requirements. You must show proof the education credentials have been deemed to be at least equivalent to that gained in conventional U.S. education program. It is your responsibility to provide such evidence when applying. Additional information Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP): For information on how to apply as an ICTAP eligible click here . To be well-qualified and exercise selection priority for this vacancy, displaced Federal employees must be rated well qualified or above for this position. You must submit a copy of the agency notice, your most recent performance rating, and your most recent SF-50 noting position, grade level, and duty location. Employed Annuitants (Reemployed Annuitants): Applicants in receipt of an annuity based on civilian employment in the Federal Service are subject to the DoD Policy on The Employment of Annuitants. Click here for more information. 120-Day Register: This announcement may result in a 120-day register that may be used to fill like vacancies for 120 days after the closing date. Applicants may be referred for consideration as vacancies occur. Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible: MSP applicants, if determined best qualified, must be selected and placed at the highest grade for which they applied. You must include a completed copy of the DD Form 3145-4, Military Spouse PPP Self-Certification Checklist dated within 30 days along with the documents identified on the checklist to verify your eligibility for MSP. Click here to obtain/download a copy of the DD Form 3145-4, Military Spouse PPP Self-Certification Checklist. Priority Placement Program (PPP) Applicant Eligible: PPP Applicants, if determined well qualified and selected, will be placed at the at the full performance level. You must include the applicable completed copy of the PPP Self-Certification Checklist dated within 30 days along with the documents identified on the checklist to verify your eligibility as a PPP Applicant. Click here to obtain/download a copy of the applicable PPP Self-Certification Checklist (DD3145-1 through DD3145-4, select the appropriate checklist for your claimed preference). To determine the applicable PPP Self-Certification Checklist required to substantiate the eligibilities you are claiming, refer to the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide located in the Required Documents section of this vacancy announcement. Direct Deposit: All federal employees are required to have direct deposit. Disabled veteran leave is available to a Federal employee hired on/after 5 Nov 2016, who is

item.title: Director Government Relations Public Policy
item.description: At Battelle, we are more than just a leading research organization—we are a catalyst for positive change, driving innovation that makes the world safer, healthier, and more sustainable. Joining our team isn't just about taking a job; it's about embracing a mission to develop groundbreaking solutions with real-world impact. Here, your expertise will help shape the future of applied technology and science, supported by a culture that values integrity, collaboration, and pioneering thinking. As part of our nonprofit philanthropic mission, we are also committed to educating the next generation of STEM professionals, ensuring a continuous flow of talent and innovation that will shape the future. At Battelle, you don't just build a career—you build a better tomorrow. Job Summary The Director, Government Relations & Public Policy supports the development and execution of Battelle's federal government relations and public policy strategies. Reporting to the Vice President, Government Affairs, the Director advances Battelle priorities through engagement with Congress, federal agencies, coalitions, and other stakeholders. The role provides policy analysis, supports legislative and appropriations strategies, and coordinates advocacy efforts across Battelle business sectors and affiliated organizations. Responsibilities Support development and implementation of federal government relations and public policy strategies aligned with Battelle priorities. Manage relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, committee staff, federal agencies, and external stakeholders. Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative, regulatory, authorization, and appropriations developments affecting Battelle programs and growth opportunities. Provide policy analysis and recommendations to the Vice President, Government Affairs and business leaders. Develop briefing materials, talking points, congressional engagement plans, stakeholder analyses, and policy memoranda. Support appropriations and authorization strategies for assigned business sectors and affiliates. Coordinate advocacy activities across Battelle sectors and functions to ensure consistent messaging and engagement. Represent Battelle in meetings, conferences, coalitions, and public policy organizations as assigned. Support engagement with federal agencies regarding budget priorities, research initiatives, and strategic programs. Maintain awareness of emerging federal policy issues and identify opportunities and risks impacting Battelle. Key Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred. 8-12+ years of experience in government relations, congressional affairs, public policy, federal agencies, or related fields. Strong knowledge of the federal legislative process, appropriations, authorizations, and policymaking. Demonstrated experience engaging congressional offices, committees, federal agencies, and external stakeholders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to synthesize complex policy issues and translate them into actionable recommendations. Ability to work collaboratively across diverse business and technical organizations. Experience supporting defense, intelligence, homeland security, or other national security-related research and development programs is desirable, but not required. Eligibility to obtain and maintain any required security clearance. Compensation Data Battelle is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The anticipated base salary range for this role is $125,000 - $175,000 per year, in addition to our comprehensive benefits package. A candidate's salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to education, relevant work experience, skills, and certifications. Salary ranges may vary based on experience, geographic location, and market conditions. Benefits: Live an Extraordinary Life We care about your well-being, not just on the job. Battelle offers comprehensive and competitive benefits to help you live your best life. Balance life through a compressed work schedule : Most of our team follows a flexible, compressed work schedule that allows for every other Friday off—giving you a dedicated day to accomplish things in your personal life without using vacation time. Enjoy enhanced work flexibility, including a hybrid arrangement: You have options for where and when you work. Our Together with Flexibility model allows you to work 60% in-office and 40% remote, with Monday and Tuesday as common in-office days, dependent on team and position needs . Take time to recharge : You get paid time off to support work-life balance and keep motivated. Prioritize wellness : Stay healthy with medical, dental, and vision coverage with wellness incentives and benefits plus a variety of optional supplemental benefits. Better together : Coverage for partners, gender-affirming care and health support, and family formation support. Build your financial future : Build financial stability with an industry-leading 401(k) retirement savings plan. For most employees, we put in 5 percent whether you contribute or not, and match your contributions on top of that. Advance your education : Tuition assistance is available to pursue higher education. A Work Environment Where You Succeed For brilliant minds in science, technology, engineering and business operations, Battelle is the place to do the greatest good by solving humanity’s most pressing challenges and creating a safer, healthier and more secure world. You will have the opportunity to thrive in a culture that inspires you to: Apply your talent to challenging and meaningful projects Receive select funding to pursue ideas in scientific and technological discovery Partner with world-class experts in a collaborative environment Nurture and develop the next generation of scientific leaders Give back to and improve our communities Vaccinations & Safety Protocols Battelle may require employees, based on job duties, work location, and/or its clients’ requirements to follow certain safety protocols and to be vaccinated against a variety of viruses, bacteria, and diseases as a condition of employment and continued employment and to provide documentation that they are fully vaccinated. If applicable, Battelle will provide reasonable accommodations based on a qualified disability or medical condition through the Americans with Disabilities Act or the Rehabilitation Act or for a sincerely held religious belief under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (and related state laws). Battelle is an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment and opportunities for advancement, compensation, training, and growth according to individual merit, without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, age, genetic information, disability, veteran-status veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable Federal, state, or local law. Our goal is for each staff member to have the opportunity to grow to the limits of their abilities and to achieve personal and organizational objectives. We will support positive programs for equal treatment of all staff and full utilization of all qualified employees at all levels within Battelle. The above statements are intended to describe the nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, activities and skills required of staff members. No statement herein is intended to imply any authorities to commit Battelle unless special written permission is granted by Battelle's Legal Department. For more information about our other openings, please visit www.battelle.org/careers

item.title: Senior Congressional Analyst
item.description: Senior Congressional Analyst Job ID: 2618935 Location: Arlington, VA, United States Date Posted: Nov 10, 2026 Category: Communications Subcategory: Communications Schedule: Full-Time Shift: Day Job Travel: Yes - 10% of the time Minimum Clearance Required: TS/SCI Clearance Level Must Be Able to Obtain: None Potential for Remote Work: On-Site Benefits: Click here Share: Job Description Description SAIC is searching for a dynamic Congressional Affairs Analyst to join our team, dedicated to the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)). This pivotal role is at the heart of an organization spearheading the development of groundbreaking capabilities for the Department of War (DOW), driving innovation, and securing our nation's technological edge. This role offers a unique opportunity to support an organization and mission that is defining the future of DOW technology. Your work will ensure that OUSW(R&E) remains at the forefront of innovation, all while navigating the intricate landscape of congressional interactions with professionalism and strategic insight. The position will be located at the Pentagon in Arlington, VA. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES: Manage congressional workflow and tasking systems: Congressional Hearings and Reporting Requirements Tracking System (CHARRTS), Office of Legislative Counsel (OLC) Web, DOW Congressional Tracking System, and CATMS database. Provide multifunctional administrative support, including analysis, filing, support activities, task management, briefing management, and managing special congressional workflows. Coordinating legislative activities within OUSW(R&E), ensuring alignment across the enterprise. Handling congressional reporting for OUSW(R&E). analyzing legislative material, coordinating tasking and workflow, arbitrating disputes, and working with OSW(LA) and BAA. Creating and maintaining workflow, reporting, and analysis documents, tracking deadlines, and issuing guidance. Managing special inter-Department projects, coordinating with OSD(LA), OGC, and OLC on task groups and processes. Collating and refining OUSW(R&E) reports, managing groups, and strategizing to meet congressional requirements. Analyzing inquiries and responses, managing correspondence, tracking follow-up actions, and providing document retrieval services. Assembling information, maintaining files, and coordinating responses to congressional and DoW staff inquiries. General administrative duties: coordinating security clearances, processing badge requests, tracking FOIA requests, assisting with Pentagon parking for congressional visitors. Responding to congressional inquiries, coordinating responses, maintaining a database of inquiries and responses. Documenting congressional reports and analysis, summarizing official program information as per DoW or federal directives. Qualifications Required Qualifications: Bachelors and 10 years or more of related experience; OR Masters and 8 years or more experience ; OR PhD or JD and 5 years or more experience. Must have at least 2 years of legislative systems management experience in the DOW. Strong problem identification and resolution skills, flexibility, initiative, and a proven ability to work with Senior Executives efficiently and effectively. TS/SCI clearance required to maintain employment. Desired Qualifications: Experience in congressional briefing management and direct congressional staff interaction and support as a DOW representative. Prior experience supporting an OSW principal (USW, ASW, PDASW). Target salary range: $120,001 - $160,000. The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position based on experience and other factors. Overview SAIC accepts applications on an ongoing basis and there is no deadline. SAIC® is a premier mission integrator focused on advancing the power of technology and innovation to serve and protect our world. Our robust portfolio of offerings across the defense, space, intelligence, and civilian markets includes secure high-end solutions in mission IT, enterprise IT, engineering services, and professional services. We integrate emerging technology, rapidly and securely, into mission critical operations that modernize and enable critical national imperatives. We are approximately 23,000 strong; driven by mission, united by purpose, and inspired by opportunities. SAIC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC has annual revenues of approximately $7.3 billion. For more information, visit saic.com . For ongoing news, please visit our newsroom . Share:

item.title: Legislative Affairs Analyst Arlington Va
item.description: ATTENTION MILITARY AFFILIATED JOB SEEKERS - Our organization works with partner companies to source qualified talent for their open roles. The following position is available to Veterans , Transitioning Military, National Guard and Reserve Members, Military Spouses, Wounded Warriors, and their Caregivers . If you have the required skill set, education requirements, and experience, please click the submit button and follow the next steps. Unless specifically stated otherwise, this role is "On-Site" Legislative Affairs Analyst Location: Herbert R. Temple Army National Guard Readiness Center, Arlington, VA (some work at the Pentagon) Start date: ASAP Salary Range: $95,000 to $105,000 Travel: Occasional CONUS travel may be required in support of congressional or public affairs events Why Vectrona: Vectrona is a mission-driven systems, technology, and operational solutions company built for people who want their work to matter. As proud Americans, we support national security missions that strengthen our institutions and help safeguard our nation’s security and prosperity. We challenge assumptions, seek out hard problems, and bring together people, processes, software, technology, training, and operational expertise to create solutions that simplify the complex and help others succeed. Our culture values integrity, ownership, personal leadership, sound judgment, teamwork, curiosity, and the willingness to step up when something important needs to get done. Why This Work Matters: The Legislative Affairs Analyst helps ensure the National Guard communicates clearly, accurately, and effectively with Congress and other key stakeholders on issues that directly affect the mission. This position sits at the intersection of legislative engagement, strategic communication, stakeholder coordination, and senior leader priorities. By turning complex information into clear, polished products and coordinating input across the organization, the Legislative Affairs Analyst helps ensure NGB leaders are prepared to respond to congressional requirements and communicate the Guard’s priorities with consistency and credibility. This work helps strengthen understanding of the National Guard’s mission while supporting the relationships and decisions that shape its ability to serve the nation. Day-to-Day Responsibilities: -Support development of CNGB strategic communications and legislative deliverables, including responses to congressional taskings -Coordinate with NGB divisions and external stakeholders to gather required data and comments -Manage a Comment Resolution Matrix (CRM) to adjudicate input and track revisions across stakeholders -Draft and edit information papers, reports, and communication products for congressional and public audiences -Assist in the design and implementation of surveys or reporting tools to collect stakeholder input -Provide final formatting, version control, and submission of approved deliverables in compliance with NGB protocols -Maintain awareness of ongoing congressional engagements, hearings, or inquiries affecting the National Guard -Ensure messaging aligns with CNGB guidance and NGB Joint Staff priorities

item.title: Sr Analyst Public Policy Hybrid Arlington
item.description: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you. About the Role: CrowdStrike is looking for a highly motivated Sr. Analyst, Public Policy to join our global Public Policy team. This role will support the team’s work across a range of cybersecurity, technology, and digital policy issues, with a particular focus on U.S. public policy and policy partnerships. The Sr. Analyst will play an important role in the day-to-day operations of the Public Policy team, including monitoring policy developments, conducting research, preparing written materials, coordinating meetings and events, assisting with policy partnerships, and maintaining the internal processes and resources that help the team operate effectively. This is an opportunity for an early-career policy professional to build substantive expertise at the intersection of cybersecurity, business, and government while developing the research, writing, project management, and stakeholder engagement skills necessary for a career in public policy. The role will approximately require 50% of time spent on policy-related work, 25% on internal-facing compliance, and 25% on administrative and organizational support for the public policy team. There is a strong preference for a candidate based in DC/MD/VA. We anticipate office time and in-person meetings multiple days per week, as well as occasional travel. We will also consider exceptional candidates based in major U.S. cities such as San Francisco, Austin, or NYC. What You’ll Do: Prepare regular internal policy updates, news summaries, legislative and regulatory trackers, meeting readouts, and other materials that keep the Public Policy team and key internal stakeholders informed of relevant developments. Support internal Public Policy compliance. Conduct research and support the preparation of memos, backgrounders, talking points, briefing materials, presentations, and other written products for members of the Public Policy team and other CrowdStrike leaders. Maintain organizational tools to manage the team’s policy partnerships and external engagements, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) tools where appropriate. Support the team’s day-to-day meeting and engagement workflow, including scheduling and coordinating meetings, preparing agendas and background materials, managing logistics, taking notes, and tracking follow-up items. Assist with the preparation and coordination of policy events, conferences, roundtables, and other external engagements. Assist with additional administrative, operational, and substantive projects that support the effectiveness of the global Public Policy team. Complete other tasks and duties as assigned. What You’ll Need: 5 years of relevant professional experience in public policy, government affairs, cybersecurity or technology policy, national security, or a related field. A bachelor’s degree in a relevant topic including in public policy, international relations, national security, security studies, cybersecurity, political science, or a related discipline. Demonstrated interest in cybersecurity, AI, and technology policy. Excellent research, analytical, and writing skills, with an ability to quickly understand complex issues and communicate them clearly and concisely. Strong judgment and attention to detail. Ability to synthesize legislative, regulatory, technical, and other complex material for audiences with varying levels of subject-matter expertise. Strong organizational, project-management, and administrative skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and reliably execute both short-turnaround and longer-term assignments. Ability to work collaboratively across teams, cultures, and time zones in a fast-paced environment. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a highly collaborative team. Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes. Bonus Points: Advanced degree in a relevant topic including in public policy, international relations, law, national security, security studies, cybersecurity, political science, or a related discipline. Experience working in or with the U.S. federal government, Congress, a state government, policy research organization, trade association, or technology company. #LI-NA1 Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike: Market leader in compensation and equity awards Comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs Competitive vacation and holidays for recharge Paid parental and adoption leaves Professional development opportunities for all employees regardless of level or role Employee Networks, geographic neighborhood groups, and volunteer opportunities to build connections Vibrant office culture with world class amenities Great Place to Work Certified™ across the globe CrowdStrike is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. item.title: Director Of Legislative Affairs Office Of Equity Policy And Engagement Legislative Affairs Unit
item.description: Director of Legislative Affairs, Office of Equity, Policy, and Engagement, Legislative Affairs Unit Division/Unit : Legislative Affairs Unit Location : 200 St. Paul Place, Baltimore, MD 21202 Closing Date : 12/07/2026 Salary Range : $120,722 - $190,376 / Annually Employee Type : Regular Time Type : Full-Time Share: Save Job Saved Description The Attorney General is the chief legal officer of the State of Maryland. The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) has the general charge, supervision, and direction of the State’s legal business, acting as legal advisors and representatives of the major agencies, various boards, commissions, officials, and institutions of State Government. The OAG also protects the public by civil enforcement of antitrust, civil rights, consumer protection, and securities laws and regulations and by the prosecution of organized crime, Medicaid fraud, environmental crimes, insurance fraud, state tax evasion, and other ​​statutorily assigned matters. As Maryland’s 47th Attorney General, Anthony G. Brown leads the Office with a critical focus on equity, justice, and fairness. The OAG is seeking an accomplished Director of Legislative Affairs to serve as the Attorney General’s primary advocate before the Maryland General Assembly and principal liaison to State agencies, federal elected officials, and community partners. Reporting to the Deputy Attorney General for the Office of Equity, Policy, and Engagement, the Director leads the Legislative Affairs Unit, serves on the Office’s executive team, and coordinates all statewide legislative activity for the OAG. The ideal candidate is an experienced attorney and legislative strategist with strong relationships in Annapolis, sound judgment as a senior advisor, and the ability to lead a team through Maryland’s 90-day legislative session. This is a rare opportunity to shape the laws that protect Marylanders and to advance the Attorney General’s priorities at the center of State policymaking. Key Responsibilities Legislative Leadership and Advocacy Serve as the Attorney General’s chief advocate before the Maryland General Assembly, including oral and written testimony before legislative committees. Develop and execute the OAG’s legislative agenda, including departmental legislation, from concept through enactment. Coordinate statewide legislative activities for the Office, including OAG positions on bills affecting the Office, its divisions, and the State agencies it represents. Lead advocacy for the OAG’s budget priorities throughout the State budget process. Monitor emerging issues and recommend legislative and legal remedies to the Attorney General and senior leadership. Executive Advising and Reporting Advise the Attorney General and executive team on legislative strategy, session developments, and political dynamics. Participate in executive team decision making, including scheduling and priority setting during session. Ensure timely, accurate responses to legislative and constituent inquiries, consistent with law and OAG policy. Relationships and Coordination Build and maintain relationships with legislative leadership, committee chairs, members, legislative staff, and committee counsel. Serve as the OAG’s primary liaison to the Governor’s Legislative Office. Work with Principal Counsels and their client agencies to coordinate legislative positions and testimony. Engage federal elected officials, State and local officials, advocacy organizations, and community groups on the Attorney General’s priorities. Represent the OAG on interagency workgroups, commissions, and special projects assigned by the Attorney General. Unit Management Lead the Legislative Affairs Unit and supervise the Legislative Affairs Manager, including assigning and reviewing work, approving leave, providing training, and conducting performance evaluations. Develop policies and procedures, including session tracking and bill review processes, to ensure efficient operations. Integrate legislative strategy with the broader work of the Office of Equity, Policy, and Engagement. Classification: Designated Admin Mgr Senior III Experience: A bachelor’s degree is required; a JD, MPP, or MPA is strongly preferred. Candidates must have at least 10 years of experience in state government relations, legislative affairs, public policy, or a related field, including experience supervising professional staff. Direct experience working with the Maryland General Assembly is strongly preferred. Experience as General Assembly or Department of Legislative Services staff, in the Governor’s Legislative Office or an agency legislative office, as a registered lobbyist, or in a policy leadership role at an advocacy organization is highly valued. The ideal candidate will demonstrate exceptional writing skills suitable for executive audiences, strong analytical and strategic abilities, and a deep understanding of Maryland’s legislative and budget processes. The role requires a proven record of advancing policy through the full legislative cycle, success in relationship and coalition building, sound judgment and discretion, and the ability to lead under significant time pressure. Candidates must be available for extended evening and weekend hours during the January through April legislative session. Submission: Applicants must submit a resume, cover letter, writing sample (such as legislative testimony, a policy memo, or a bill analysis) and a list of three professional references, including at least one current or former supervisor. Please note that this job posting will come offline at 6:00 p.m. EST on the closing date. Telework: Hybrid Work – Two in-office days weekly outside the legislative session; in person presence in Annapolis is expected during session. Employment Benefits: Working for the Office of the Attorney General offers a competitive benefits package designed to support your health and well‑being. Generous Leave: Annual Leave: 10–25 days per year based on service. Sick Leave: 15 days per year with unlimited carryover. Personal Leave: Up to 6 days per year. Paid Holidays: 12 state holidays. Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans. Retirement Savings: Defined‑benefit pension plan plus 401(k) and 457 supplemental retirement options. Work–Life Balance: Hybrid and flexible work schedules available for many roles. Professional Growth: Ongoing training and development opportunities, including paid MSBA membership. Additional Benefits: Flexible Spending Accounts, free mass transit (eligible areas), Employee Assistance Program, and access to SECU. Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging: The Office of the Attorney General views equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging as the pathway to achieving professional excellence and fostering and maintaining a culture where every employee can thrive. We strive to create a community that draws upon the best pool of talent to unify excellence and diversity while fully embracing individuals from varied backgrounds, cultures, races, identities, life experiences, perspectives, beliefs, and values. We honor, respect, and celebrate all differences, both visible and invisible, and are committed to recruiting, retaining, and promoting individuals who have historically been underrepresented in the practice of law and professional careers. Equal Opportunity Employer: The OAG is an equal opportunity employer that encourages all interested persons to apply regardless of race, color, religion or belief, ancestry, national origin, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, disability, pregnancy, family or parental status, veteran status, genetic information, or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws. item.title: Senior Manager Talent Discovery Selection
item.description: At Insmed, every moment and every patient counts — and so does every person who joins in. As a global biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the lives of patients with serious and rare diseases, you’ll be part of a community that prioritizes the human experience, celebrates curiosity, and values every person’s contributions to meaningful progress. That commitment has earned us recognition as Science magazine’s No. 1 Top Employer for five consecutive years, certification as a Great Place to Work® in the U.S., and a place on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work list in the UK. For patients, for each other, and for the future of science, we’re in. Are you? About the Role: We're looking for a Senior Manager, Talent Discovery & Selection, to help us expand what's possible for patients with serious diseases. Reporting to the Director, Talent Discovery & Selection, the Senior Manager will lead recruiting for assigned functional areas, shaping strategies, processes, and programs that attract and deliver high-quality talent to Insmed. In this hands-on role, you’ll source, screen, and interview candidates while building networks and talent pipelines. You’ll partner closely with business leaders, HR Business Partners (HRBPs), Total Rewards, and Talent Development & Transformation to align hiring priorities and lead an effective, end-to-end recruiting process. What You'll Do: In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to identify, assess, and recommend qualified candidates while serving as a trusted internal talent advisor, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership to hiring managers, business partners, and HRBPs. You'll also: Build relationships across Insmed’s departments and functions to connect teams with internal and external talent. Proactively source candidates for assigned roles through targeted outreach, networking, talent pipelines, employee referrals, internal mobility, and creative sourcing strategies. Apply industry insights and competitive intelligence to inform recruiting strategies. Embed recruiting processes, tools, and systems into the business to improve hiring effectiveness. Drive operational excellence through consistent use of recruiting tools, disciplined processes, and accurate data. Develop and review recruiting metrics and reports to track performance and identify opportunities for improvement. Manage the offer process, including reference checks, background screening, and compensation alignment. Lead intake, alignment, and debrief discussions with hiring managers and interview teams. Who You Are You must have a Bachelor’s degree and at least 6 years of full lifecycle recruiting experience including 3 years in the biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry. Additionally, you have: Strong knowledge of applicant tracking systems, digital sourcing strategies, and behavioral-based interview techniques. AI fluency and a proactive approach to adopting emerging technologies, with the ability to apply AI tools responsibly to streamline workflows, improve productivity, and elevate recruiting effectiveness. Demonstrated proficiency with Talent Acquisition tools and technology including AI-enabled recruiting platforms, sourcing tools, talent CRMs, automation, and workforce analytics. Proficiency with translating workforce data, recruiting analytics, and emerging market trends into actionable talent strategies, new sourcing opportunities, and informed investment decisions. Proven ability to participate in or lead projects while managing day-to-day recruiting priorities. A track record of building trusted business partnerships and communicating clearly and effectively at all organizational levels. Demonstrated success navigating a fast-paced, evolving environment and adapting to shifting priorities. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with a commitment to accuracy, clarity, and follow-through. The ability to collaborate effectively across diverse teams and contribute to a dynamic, inclusive workplace. Nice to Have (but not required): Experience with Workday Recruiting is a plus. Prior experience supporting Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Drug Safety, and/or Regulatory Affairs is strongly preferred. Experience with Beamery and/or Paradox is a plus. Where You’ll Work This is a fully remote role. It can be performed effectively from anywhere while staying connected to your Insmed team and community. Occasional travel for team meetings or events will be expected. Travel Requirements This role requires occasional domestic travel (approximately 10%). #LI-Remote #LI-SK1 Who You Are: Pay Range: $124,000.00-161,000.00 Annual Life at Insmed At Insmed, you’ll find a culture as human as our mission—intentionally designed for the people behind it. You deserve a workplace that reflects the same care you bring to your work each day, with support for how you work, how you grow, and how you show up for patients, your team, and yourself. Highlights of our U.S. offerings include: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage and mental health support, annual wellbeing reimbursement, and access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Generous paid time off policies, fertility and family-forming benefits, caregiver support, and flexible work schedules with purposeful in-person collaboration 401(k) plan with a competitive company match, annual equity awards, and participation in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), and company-paid life and disability insurance Company Learning Institute providing access to LinkedIn Learning, skill building workshops, leadership programs, mentorship connections, and networking opportunities Employee resource groups, service and recognition programs, and meaningful opportunities to connect, volunteer, and give back Eligibility for specific programs may vary and is subject to the terms and conditions of each plan. Current Insmed Employees: Please apply via the Jobs Hub in Workday. Insmed Incorporated is an Equal Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. For more information, please refer to our Equal Employment Opportunity and Non-Discrimination Statement on our Careers site. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. Unsolicited resumes from agencies should not be forwarded to Insmed. Insmed will not be responsible for any fees arising from the use of resumes through this source. Insmed will only pay a fee to agencies if a formal agreement between Insmed and the agency has been established. The Human Resources department is responsible for all recruitment activities; please contact us directly to be considered for a formal agreement. Insmed is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact us by email at TotalRewards@insmed.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.
