item.title: Sr Director Of Legislative Campaigns
item.description: Description Unite America seeks a full-time Sr. Director of Legislative Campaigns to join our Campaigns team. Reporting to one of our two Vice Presidents of Campaigns, this individual will oversee the due diligence, investment recommendations, and execution of a portfolio of legislative campaigns across Unite America’s priority issue areas. Within a growing organization, this role requires hands-on project management and execution (“no task too small”) alongside longer-term strategic development of our campaign work. To be successful in this role, a candidate should have a strong understanding of the legislative process and feel comfortable working in a fast-paced political environment. In addition, you are a diligent, dynamic self-starter who can proactively identify and address challenges and opportunities, and you are excited about contributing to team culture and leadership. Unite America strongly encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply. The position will be based at Unite America’s headquarters in Denver, CO, or remote. Unite America offers a stipend for new hires willing to relocate. This position may be expected to travel 2-4 times per month for both campaign efforts and broader organizational needs (team meetings, retreats, etc). OUR ORGANIZATION Unite America is a non-partisan, philanthropic venture fund that invests in candidates, campaigns, and organizations in order to advance nonpartisan election reforms that will foster a more representative and functional government capable of solving America’s most pressing challenges. Founded in 2014, Unite America and its 35+ person team has grown to be a leader in the democracy reform movement. The organization has existed in its current form, and with its current primary focus, since 2019; in that time, we have successfully mobilized tens of millions of dollars from scores of philanthropists to candidates and reform campaigns across the country. At Unite America, we are working to build a more representative and functional government that puts voters first and reflects the diversity of our country, and an inclusive democracy in which leaders embrace problem-solving over fueling divisiveness. Likewise, we have a vision of building an organization that reflects diverse identities, experiences, and perspectives, a culture of working across differences toward common goals, and a workplace where everyone feels included, respected, and heard. To that end, Unite America is proud to have made diversifying our team, ensuring more equitable opportunity, and fostering a culture of belonging a priority. Our organizational values reinforce this commitment as we work to model the leadership we seek, solve problems together, and take care of one another, to name a few. Requirements RESPONSIBILITIES Legislative Strategy & Oversight Translate political intelligence, legislative developments, and organizational priorities into clear campaign plans, tactics, timelines, and decision points. Oversee a portfolio of proactive and defensive legislative campaigns across multiple states, adjusting strategies as political conditions, leadership dynamics, and legislative pathways evolve. Serve as the primary point of contact for state lobbyists and campaign partners, leading priority-setting discussions and maintaining clear expectations and accountability. Build and maintain strong relationships with legislative leaders, elected officials, lobbyists, coalition partners, grantees, and other influential stakeholders. Coordinate legislative, political, communications, legal, coalition, grassroots, and research strategies to support campaign objectives. Ensure responsible stewardship of resources, effective budget management, and compliance with applicable fiscal, legal, lobbying, and organizational policies. Investment Making & Management Analyze political intelligence, legislative activity, campaign data, and partner performance to inform investment decisions and longer-term state strategy. Serve as program officer for a portfolio of legislative grants and contracts, including due diligence, investment recommendations, proposals, agreements, ongoing management and impact evaluation. Evaluate when Unite America should fund existing in-state partners, retain lobbyists or consultants, help build new organizations, or operate components of a campaign directly. Monitor lobbyist, consultant, campaign, and grantee performance to ensure accountability, timely deliverables, effective coordination, and measurable progress. Legislative Execution & Project Leadership Project-manage multiple concurrent state legislative strategies, ensuring that deadlines, budgets, deliverables, and decision points remain on track and developing remediation plans when they do not. Anticipate legislative, political, legal, operational, and reputational risks and adjust campaign plans accordingly. Establish and improve systems for legislative planning, intelligence sharing, partner coordination, risk management, budget oversight, and performance tracking. Convene and facilitate campaign teams, establish clear ownership, and maintain proactive communication among internal and external stakeholders. Organizational Leadership & Collaboration Provide senior leaders with clear, timely assessments of legislative developments, strategic options, investment needs, and recommended next steps. Collaborate across teams to evaluate new opportunities, assess risks, and advise on strategies beyond campaigns. Model organizational values and contribute to a positive, mission-driven team culture. You have a strong desire to fix a broken political system and a passion for Unite America’s primary reform.You have at least eight years of experience leading state legislative campaigns, government affairs initiatives, public affairs efforts, or related political programs, with a demonstrated record of success in complex political environments. You have experience developing legislative strategy and executing sophisticated advocacy campaigns at the state or multi-state level. Strong understanding of legislative procedure, committee dynamics, political incentives, and the roles of legislative leadership, governors, and other statewide officials. Experience managing contract lobbyists, government affairs teams, consultants, coalitions, or other in-state partners. Ability to translate political intelligence, policy developments, and campaign data into clear strategic recommendations. Experience developing and managing campaign plans, budgets, timelines, and performance measures. Demonstrated ability to allocate resources effectively, anticipate risks, and adjust strategy as political conditions change. Experience coordinating legislative, political, communications, legal, and grassroots strategies. QUALIFICATIONS You possess exceptional conflict resolution skills, promoting a positive and productive team environment You are a skilled relationship builder who can quickly establish trust and credibility with legislators, legislative staff, grantees, lobbyists, coalition partners, colleagues, and other stakeholders across the political and ideological spectrum. You have excellent written and verbal communication skills and can represent Unite America credibly with elected officials, donors, partners, national organizations, and other external audiences. You have familiarity with grantmaking and philanthropic strategy and processes is preferred, not required You are an entrepreneurial, self-starter with strong critical thinking skills and proven ability to effectively manage details, recognize trends, analyze data, and make strategic recommendations You have excellent project-management skills and can manage multiple legislative priorities, shifting timelines, and competing demands while maintaining a consistently high level of execution. Benefits Competitive Compensation ($165k-$190k) 401(k) Plan (with up to a 3% employer contribution match) Health Care Plan (medical, dental, and vision) Unlimited Paid Time Off (vacation, sick days, public holidays, and team-wide wellness days) Family Leave (maternity, paternity, and adoption) Paid sabbatical after 4 years on staff Training & Professional Development Wellness Resources Opportunity to join an inclusive, vibrant, and diverse team

item.title: 2027 Open Enrollment Benefit Options And Elections
item.description: 2027 ESF&R Annual Benefits Open Enrollment - Options and Elections November 1st - December 7th The Eastside Fire & Rescue Annual Benefits Open Enrollment season is under way. Below is an outline of each benefit plan, and options to consider for the upcoming 2027 Plan Year. Changes elected during Open Enrollment take effect on January 1, 2027. Take time to review all benefit plan options outlined below before proceeding. Members who do not wish to make any plan changes in 2027 do not need to continue or take any action. When you are ready to make a change, click the APPLY Button to the right of this form to proceed to the Election Page. On the Election Page - enter your name, phone number and department email address. On the page you will find a list of benefit plan options to choose from. Click YES to the elections you wish to make for 2027. (Or click No.) When finished making elections, click SUBMIT. Once the elections are submitted, Human Resources will review all changes and send forms or paperwork to members through BAMBOO to initiate their change. Medical, Dental, BPAS VEBA Plan Options: Eastside Fire will continue to provide employee and dependent coverage through the LEOFF Trust Medical Plan B and Delta Dental Plan. HRA Annual Deposits continue as $2,000 for Single Enrollees and $4,000 for Employees with Dependents. The new 2027 allotment of VEBA funds will be deposited into member Accounts by January 15, 2027. 1) During Open Enrollment, members may ADD or DELETE eligible dependents who may have been missed before, without needing a qualifying event. 2) Eligible Union Members may choose to OPT OUT of the Medical Plan and receive half of their monthly premium deposited to t heir BPAS VEBA Account. Proof of other medical coverage is required to OPT Out. 3) Eligible Union Members who currently OPT OUT of Medical and receive a VEBA contribution, may choose to re-enroll into the Medical Plan in 2027. Flexible Spending Account (FSA) Dependent Care Account (DCA) Options: 1) Members may set up a Pre-TAX FSA or DCA account to pay for planned out of pocket medical and dependent care expenses. The current annual IRS Maximum for an FSA is $3,400, and $5,000 per year for a DCA. These amounts are projected to increase in 2027. Additional details will be shared when the IRS confirms the increase. 2) For members currently enrolled in a 2026 FSA or DCA, their election and payroll deductions will cease at the end of the year. A NEW election for 2027 will need to be requested for another FSA/DCA account to be set up in 2027. Medical Expense Reimbursement Plan (MERP) and Optional VEBA Deposit: 1) For Eligible Union Members - The Employer contributes $250 per month to each member's MERP Plan. During Open Enrollment, members may opt to have $175 of their MERP proceeds deposited into their VEBA Plan - (Resulting in a $250 split of $75-MERP, $175-VEBA). 2) Members currently set up with $175 going to their VEBA account, who wish to stay with VEBA in 2027, do not need to take any action. 3) Members currently set up with $175 going to their VEBA account, who want to change and direct it towards their MERP plan, need to request the change through Open Enrollment. Deferred Compensation 457b and 401a Options: 1) COLA Increases in 2027 will increase every member's Employer Contribution towards their Randall Hurley or DRS VOYA DCP Accounts. *** It is each employee's responsibility to contact their DCP Plan Agent and UPDATE their DCP Plans with new 2027 deferral elections.... by no later than December 15, 2026. 2) Members must also provide PAYROLL with a copy of their new 2027 DCP Plan choices and deferral elections.... by no later than December 15, 2026. 3) Payroll cannot set up new benefit elections in 2027 without confirmation of each member's chosen DCP Plans and salary deferrals for 2027. DCP Plan Agent contact information will be provided with Open Enrollment materials. If you are ready to elect changes described on this page, click the APPLY button and follow the prompts. When through making elections, click the "Submit Application: button at the lower right side of the page.

item.title: Research Finance Operations Coordinator Mccourt School Of Public Policy Georgetown University
item.description: Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world. Requirements Job Overview The Research Finance & Operations Coordinator provides essential administrative, financial and human capital management (HCM) execution for the McCourt School of Public Policy's Research Enterprise. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Research Finance, this position serves as a core operational bridge for a growing portfolio of research centers, faculty and research teams spread across campus locations. Working alongside Research Administration Managers (RAMs) and the broader School finance team, the Research Finance & Operations Coordinator handles frontline operations, initiates research personnel and student hiring workflows, executes transactional financial processes, and maintains efficient day-to-day financial operations. This role offers high visibility into the full life cycle of sponsored research and center management within a high-volume and dynamic research environment. Key Duties & Responsibilities HR Administration & Research Personnel Personnel Workflows: Initiate and track HCM processing, E-requests, appointment letters, and onboarding workflows for all research personnel types—including research faculty, staff, post-doctoral fellows, temporary employees, visiting scholars, research fellows, and research affiliates. Student Employment: Coordinate the recruitment, hiring, onboarding, and hourly timekeeping processing for grant-supported student workers across McCourt research centers. Administrative Liaison: Serve as the primary operational liaison with central administrative offices—including the Dean’s Office, Provost Office HCM team, Office of Faculty Affairs, Student Employment Office and Office for Global Services—to resolve visa, payroll, and other HCM paperwork. Research Financial & Operational Transactions Financial Processing: Execute day-to-day transactional financial workflows across 145+ active grant accounts, contracts, and center funds, including purchase orders, procurement contracts, miscellaneous payment requests, expense reimbursements (employee and procard) and GU Travel processing, subaward support documents, ACH forms, etc. Financial Monitoring: Support the Senior Director and RAMs in routine financial monitoring of internal and external funds by compiling expenditure data, tracking payments, preparing journals, and assisting with monthly ledger reconciliations of suspense accounts and institutional accounts. Student Financial Operations: Assist with student financial processing where applicable, including tracking grant-funded tuition merit aid, work study credits, research stipends and costing allocations. Research Operations & General Administration Office & Tech Operations: Maintain day-to-day office operations for the McCourt Research Enterprise including facilities, supplies, and technology service requests (e.g., cell phone management and computer orders). Constituent Contact: Act as a professional primary point of contact for internal and external constituents, answering faculty and student inquiries with high-quality, customer-service-oriented communication. Process Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline internal administrative procedures, operational protocols, and office workflows across the research centers.Work Interactions Direct Team: Reports directly to the Senior Director of Research Finance and works in daily partnership with Research Administration Managers (RAMs), Grants and Contracts Accountant, and the McCourt Finance team. Internal Stakeholders: Interacts regularly with McCourt center directors, PIs, research faculty and staff across all locations. External/University Support Units: Liaises frequently with the Office of Faculty Affairs (OFA), Provost HCM, Facilities, Procurement, Joint Office for Research Administration (JORA), Sponsored Projects Financial Operations (SPFO) and Student Employment (SEO). Requirements and Qualifications Minimum Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree required. Experience: Minimum 2 years of administrative and operational experience in a professional office environment, preferably within higher education, a research enterprise, or a non-profit setting. Technical Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint) with intermediate-to-advanced Excel skills (basic formulas, spreadsheet management). Preferred Qualifications Direct experience handling personnel hiring workflows, student employment processing, or basic accounts payable/procurement transactions. Familiarity with university enterprise systems (e.g., Workday/GMS, Cognos) and general higher education administrative policies. Basic understanding of sponsored research environments. Exceptional organizational skills, high attention to detail, strong problem-solving abilities, and a service-oriented approach to collaborating with faculty and senior administrators. item.title: Community Canvasser Final Days Before Election 22 24 Hr
item.description: Community Canvassers and Team Leaders Hiring Immediately - $22-24/hr + bonuses Full-time & Part-time Help us turn out voters in North Carolina to get out the vote and win! Grassroots efforts are ramping up and we are looking for a team of canvassers to help us reach voters who deserve a voice in this election. From now through Election Day, our team is connecting directly with voters on the ground through door-to-door outreach. We will be supporting candidates who champion progressive values and our shared vision for the future, encouraging people to get out and vote for progressive leaders down the ticket. This role is a great opportunity to gain experience in the following areas: Leadership, Communication & Advocacy, Community Outreach & Engagement, Campaign Work, Public Policy, and Social Enterprise. Get paid well! Canvassing positions start at $22/hour. Team Lead positions start at $24/hour. We offer overtime pay, shift bonuses, paid training, sick pay, and bonuses for friend referrals. Apply here: https://www.theoutreachteam.net/interest-form-tot Locations : Granville County & Wilson County, NC We are hiring immediately, all positions run through November 3rd, with possibilities for advancement afterwards. Shifts run from 11:30 pm - 7:30 pm, Tuesday - Sunday with the possibility to work part-time or full-time. Canvasser Responsibilities ($22/hr): Engage with the public in a friendly and respectful manner Deliver a compelling campaign message, and collect complete survey answers from voters Participate in staff training to improve outreach skills Follow the campaign's safety protocols Team Leader Responsibilities ($24/hr): The Canvasser Responsibilities plus: Manage a small group of canvassers out in the field by checking in with them periodically throughout the day, and debriefing with them at the end of the day Ensure each canvasser has all of the materials they need to be successful Assist directors with canvasser training and administrative work The ideal candidate: Passionate about progressive politics and fostering democracy Strong communication skills; you should enjoy working with other people and be willing and excited to speak with everyone Hard worker who will stay motivated to engage as many people as possible Open to new challenges and are interested in building their campaign skills Culturally competent and able to respectfully engage with teammates and the community Prior canvassing experience is preferred, but not required. We are committed to equity, inclusion, and anti-racism. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. Note: Employees must be eligible to work in the US. Upon hire, everyone will be required to present original, and unexpired documents from the Lists of Acceptable Documents to complete the I-9 form verification.

item.title: Election Systems Specialist
item.description: Summary Provides technical support for the Election’s systems. Maintains inventory tracking programs. Maintain security/auditing procedures and the elections software library. Provide Applications/Database support for elections. Assist users with hardware and software problems. Essential Duties Oversee, prepare, document the creation of each election using elections system software and hardware. Prepare and oversee the programming, testing, documentation, and logic and accuracy procedures for elections system software and hardware. Prepare and test electronic voting equipment; voter qualifying computers and printers; and tabulation equipment in accordance with manufacturer and statutory requirements. Use election system software to prepare ballots, including entry of candidate and propositions according to state regulations. Verify and validate through external means, the accuracy of each ballot style and all district assignments. Train and support staff, including election workers, on the operation of all electronic voting equipment and computers used for qualifying voters. Supervise troubleshooting during elections process. Assist in the multi-media training programs and visual aids for election workers. Provide support, including on-site and telephone support of election systems. Operate Election Night Tabulation reporting software. Generate election system reports for Elections Administrator and others as required. Use software applications, such as Microsoft Office, to create and edit spreadsheets and documents as required. Use and maintain Voter Registration and Election system software programs. Prepare and post all required Notices of Election for posting and canvas reports. Maintain Lubbock County Elections’ website, ensuring all required postings and updates are available for the public. Prepare and transmit reports electronically to various government entities. Act as liaison between Elections, vendors and ITS Department regarding election systems. Assist with warehouse duties before, during and after each election, travel to election sites to deliver equipment/or supplies, test and troubleshoot equipment as required. Recommend departmental expenditures for election systems. Cross train with other employees on all elections systems. Public speaking at community events or in educational venues. Other duties as assigned Position Requirements High School Diploma or GED equivalent; 1-2 years of technical school or specialized training in software applications. Completion of current Elections systems training within 6 months of date of hire. Current Texas driver’s license and current liability insurance required. Associate or bachelor’s degree preferred. Supplemental Information KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES : Strong computer software and technical expertise; working knowledge of spreadsheets, word processing, and some experience with database reporting software; excellent verbal and written communication skills, strong interpersonal skills and ability to deal effectively with others; organizational skills and ability to complete assigned tasks within deadlines; prioritize work; and work independently in the absence of specific instructions. Possess the ability to learn and adapt. Retain composure under pressure. Maintain departmental confidentiality. PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS: Maintain the ability to frequently stand, walk, kneel, and bend during the shift; Reach, grip and use fine dexterity; Push and pull objects; Flex upper trunk forward at the waist and fully at the knees multiple times a day; Lift and carry up to 30 pounds multiple times a day; Frequently rotate upper trunk to the left or right while sitting or standing; place arms above, at or below shoulder height; Use of vision and depth perception; Talking and hearing ; verbal and written communication. Must possess the mental and physical capacity to effectively perform the essential functions and meet the requirements of the position. DISCLAIMER: The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the standard functions of this position and should not be constructed as a thorough description of all work requirements. The characteristics of the work environment described are representative of those that an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Equal Employment Employer: Lubbock County will not discriminate in our employment practices based on an applicant’s race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information or status as a protected veteran.

item.title: Washington Legislative Director
item.description: Position: Washington Legislative Director Location: Seattle, WA (hybrid) Reporting To: Washington State Director Compensation : $115,000 - $140,000, plus benefits Start Date: January 2027 About Climate Solutions: For nearly three decades, Climate Solutions has worked to accelerate clean energy solutions to the climate crisis and build a thriving, equitable Northwest powered by clean energy. Across Washington and the broader Northwest, Climate Solutions champions transformational climate and clean energy policies, builds powerful partnerships and coalitions, and helps turn ambitious solutions into action. With groundbreaking policies now in place across the region, the work ahead is both to protect and implement that progress and to keep pushing for solutions that cut climate pollution at the speed and scale required while delivering tangible benefits for people and communities. About the Opportunity: Reporting to the Washington State Director, the Washington Legislative Director will lead Climate Solutions’ Washington legislative strategy to turn ambitious climate and clean energy priorities into political action, building the relationships, collective power, and team capacity needed to win meaningful and lasting policy change. KEY PRIORITIES DURING YOUR FIRST YEAR What You’ll Achieve: ​ Lead Washington Legislative Strategy & Advocacy Champion Climate Solutions’ legislative agenda , navigating a changing political climate to pass, defend, strengthen, and support implementation of state-level climate and clean energy policies, while connecting legislative strategy to real-world impact. Shape near-, medium-, and long-term legislative priorities and strategy in partnership with the Washington State Director, Policy Directors, and contract lobbyists, translating political dynamics into strategic guidance and recommending when and how to adapt. Conduct legislative and political research and analysis to inform advocacy strategy and translate complex policy information into compelling testimony, talking points, briefings, and other materials. ​ Build Legislative Influence & Collective Power Cultivate and steward strategic partnerships across Washington, including with policymakers, government officials, organizations, coalitions, and tribal nations, understanding when Climate Solutions should lead, convene, support, or step back to strengthen collective power and advance collaborative policy action. Build momentum and win campaigns around Climate Solutions’ policy priorities, mobilizing allies across labor, communities of color, environmental coalitions, consumer protection advocates and institutions, and other aligned groups. Build collective power and elevate community voic e, partnering with environmental justice and community organizations to ensure communities most impacted by climate and policy decisions, particularly those historically excluded from policymaking, meaningfully shape advocacy strategies and policy solutions. ​ Strengthen & Integrate Legislative Strategy Across the Team Strengthen prioritization and coordination across Climate Solutions’ legislative strategy, bringing together expertise from across the team, contract lobbyists, and other partners around shared priorities and focusing time and influence where they can have the greatest legislative impact. Expand the team’s capacity for legislative advocacy, drawing on expertise from across the team to engage policymakers, testify, and advocate for Climate Solutions’ priorities. Who You Are: You are Mission & Values Aligned. You bring a deep commitment to accelerating clean energy solutions to the climate crisis and advancing a thriving, equitable Northwest, grounded in justice, integrity, collaboration, respect, and perseverance. You are a Bold & Strategic Advocate. You advocate with conviction, see the bigger picture while staying grounded in how decisions affect people and communities, and make thoughtful choices about when to push, pivot, prioritize, or pause. You Bridge Policy & Political Practicality. You read the political landscape and the room, understand power, stakeholder interests, and competing priorities, and know when to push, pivot, build support, or change tactics to move Climate Solutions’ policy priorities forward. You Bring Deep Legislative Expertise. You understand the rules, timelines, procedures, and decision points that shape how legislation and state budgets move, and know how to use the right levers at the right moments to advance priorities. You are a Persuasive & Adaptive Communicator. You can translate complex policy and technical information into compelling testimony, talking points, briefings, and other advocacy materials, adapting your message and approach for different audiences and settings. You Build Trust-Based Relationships. You build and sustain relationships grounded in trust, work effectively across different personalities and perspectives, navigate disagreement with care, and bring people together around shared goals. You value and draw on others’ professional and lived expertise, while supporting others to build their skills, contribute, and lead. You Bring Climate & Clean Energy Policy Familiarity. You bring familiarity with one or more climate and clean energy policy areas, such as transportation decarbonization, clean buildings, electrification, and/or clean electricity, or demonstrate the ability to build the knowledge needed to advocate across Climate Solutions’ priorities. You are an Effective Planner & Project Manager. You can translate strategy into clear plans, manage multiple priorities and stakeholders, track progress and follow-through, anticipate challenges, and create structure in complex and fast-moving environments. TRAVEL: This is a hybrid role based in Washington that requires significant in-state travel, including to the capitol, attending coalition and partnership meetings, and internal staff meetings. There is flexibility in how you structure your travel and days. BENEFITS: Climate Solutions provides 100% employee premiums for medical, dental, and vision, 6 weeks of PTO and 14 flexible holidays, and access to an Employment Assistance Program (EAP), health care flexible spending and dependent care spending accounts, and voluntary life insurance. In addition, Climate Solutions covers 100% of eligible employees' short- and long term disabilities as well as life. About Our Selection Process: Before you decide to apply, please review our Frequently Asked Questions ( here ) . Our process includes three rounds, each offering opportunities for us to get to know one another: Round 1: Application submission ( here ) and a one-way video interview ( take your interview ) due by November 6 (EOD). This stage includes four interview questions ( here ), which candidates complete on their own time. Round 2: A live, 60-minute interview via Zoom with the hiring committee. Round 3: Final interviews with the two finalists, scheduled for December 10 & 11 in Seattle, WA. _______________________ Don’t meet every single requirement? Apply anyway. We know that people from historically marginalized and excluded communities are often less likely to apply for roles unless they meet every single qualification. We believe lived experience, transferable skills, and community knowledge are valuable forms of expertise. If you’re excited about this role and Climate Solution’s mission, but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with everything listed above, we strongly encourage you to apply. You may be exactly the leader Climate Solutions needs for its next chapter.

item.title: U S Healthcare Professionals Medication Selection Interview
item.description: U.S. Healthcare Professionals – Medication Selection Interview $175 one-time | Remote | Voice Interview | Independent Contractor About the Opportunity We’re seeking U.S.-based healthcare professionals with direct experience in medication selection, prescribing, and clinical treatment decisions to participate in a focused paid interview. The conversation will explore how healthcare professionals evaluate medication options, balance clinical and patient-specific considerations, and make treatment recommendations in real-world care settings. What You’ll Discuss Your current approach to evaluating and selecting medications for patients The clinical and patient-specific factors that influence treatment recommendations How you assess different medication options within your clinical workflow Hypothetical patient scenarios and the reasoning behind your treatment choices Challenges you encounter when prescribing or ordering therapies Practical considerations that can affect medication selection and treatment pathways Who Should Apply This opportunity is intended for U.S.-based healthcare professionals with active prescribing authority and direct involvement in patient treatment decisions. Relevant professionals may include: Physicians and attending physicians Nurse practitioners Physician assistants Clinical specialists with prescribing authority Other healthcare professionals who regularly make medication or treatment recommendations Requirements Currently practicing in the United States as a physician or qualified healthcare professional Active prescribing authority Direct involvement in patient care and treatment decisions Experience evaluating medication or therapy options Comfortable discussing clinical workflows and treatment decision-making in a remote voice interview Able to clearly explain the factors and reasoning behind clinical recommendations Engagement Details Fully remote Independent contractor engagement Participation can be completed on your own schedule Engagements may be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on project needs and performance Participation must not involve confidential or proprietary information belonging to an employer, client, or institution H-1B and STEM OPT candidates are not supported for this opportunity Why Participate? Share your firsthand expertise in medication selection, prescribing workflows, and clinical decision-making while contributing practical insight into how treatment choices are made in real-world healthcare settings. Apply if you’re a U.S.-based healthcare professional with active prescribing authority and meaningful experience making medication and treatment decisions. Skills Medication evaluation Clinical decision-making Treatment planning Patient care Remote communication

item.title: Senior Director Federal Government Affairs
item.description: Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries. JOB DESCRIPTION: The Opportunity The Senior Director, Federal Government Affairs will advance and protect Abbott’s interests with Congress, federal agencies, and key trade and business associations. This leader will drive public policy strategy across all Abbott businesses, analyzing legislative and regulatory developments and shaping the company’s positions on critical issues. The role is responsible for developing and executing advocacy strategies to influence federal policies, legislation, and regulations, with a particular focus on healthcare policy and the evolving role of technology in healthcare delivery and innovation. The successful candidate will proactively monitor emerging policy trends, assess potential business impacts, and develop strategic plans that effectively address issues affecting Abbott’s diverse portfolio. This individual will serve as a trusted advisor, helping to shape policy outcomes that support innovation, patient access, and business objectives. Location: Washington, D.C. item.title: Legislative Legal Services Intern
item.description: Department Information Are you interested in an internship where you don't just interpret or apply the law, but actually help make it? Consider interning with the Office of Legislative Legal Services, the nonpartisan in-house counsel for the Colorado General Assembly. We offer an exciting and varied internship experience to motivated law students with an interest in the legislative process and state policy. About the Office of Legislative Legal Services The office facilitates and supports the legislative work of the General Assembly and protects the General Assembly's organizational interests without participating in its politics. We draft legislation for all 100 state legislators, and we conduct research for and provide legal advice to the legislators and their staff. We also serve the people of Colorado directly by publishing and annotating the Colorado Revised Statutes, reviewing and commenting on potential new laws proposed by citizens exercising their initiative rights, and providing to the public information related to the work of the General Assembly. Description of Job About the Internship Program The Office of Legislative Legal Services internship program invites you to apply your research, writing, interpersonal, and analytical skills to help address Colorado's most pressing public policy problems. Interns receive extensive mentoring and engage with a range of substantive issues through work with each of the subject matter teams. Please find each team’s subject matter expertise listed here: https://content.leg.colorado.gov/agencies/office-legislative-legal-services/team-subject-matters Interns can expect a variety of unique and rewarding experiences including: Legislative bill drafting; Conducting legal research and reviewing other states' laws; Meeting with legislators and lobbyists; Staffing legislative committee hearings; Attending floor debates; and Preparing official annotations to Colorado appellate opinions. The internship program is a strictly "for-credit" opportunity, offered during the legislative session ( mid-January through early May) . Interns are not paid for their experience at the office. The position is part-time, with the actual number of hours to be negotiated between the intern and the mentoring attorney. A minimum commitment of twelve hours per week is required, and three days a week is preferred to ensure a meaningful experience. The internship requires in-person work at the State Capitol complex. Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights Candidate Qualifications The Office of Legislative Legal Services seeks a flexible, enthusiastic, and motivated 2L or 3L student who possesses strong writing skills and excellent people skills. Bring your sound professional judgment, your ability to set aside your own biases, and, perhaps most of all, your intellectual curiosity. Having taken a legislative drafting course or a legislative process course is a plus, but is not required. Supplemental Information Application Materials Please upload your resume, a writing sample, and a brief cover letter that highlights the reasons for your interest and any relevant experience. Interviewing for the 2028 legislative session will begin in August 2027 , and applications for the 2028 session must be submitted no later than August 20, 2027. The office is no longer accepting applications for the 2027 session. The Office of Legislative Legal Services is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, genetic information, or any other status protected by law. All qualified applicants are given equal opportunity, and employment decisions are based exclusively on job-related factors.

item.title: Legislative Regulatory Advocate
item.description: Reports To: Missy Johnson, Senior Director of Government Affairs Employment Type: Full-Time, Exempt About the Firm Nielsen Merksamer is one of the nation's preeminent political law, government law, and lobbying firms, serving a national clientele on campaign, lobbying, and ethics compliance; legislative and administrative advocacy; election law; and high-stakes political and constitutional litigation. The firm is the go-to choice in California for navigating state and local government, and nationally for guidance on the complex laws governing political participation. Position Summary The Legislative & Regulatory Advocate supports the firm's lobbying and government affairs practice by monitoring legislative and regulatory activity, conducting policy research and analysis, tracking legislation and rulemaking, and helping prepare clients for engagement with lawmakers and agencies. This role is well-suited for a detail-oriented policy professional who thrives in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and wants hands-on exposure to the legislative and rulemaking process. Key Responsibilities Legislative & Regulatory Monitoring Track pending federal and/or state legislation, committee hearings, markups, and floor activity relevant to client interests Track and analyze legislative and executive branch hearings, identifying key takeaways and implications for clients Monitor agency rulemakings, notices of proposed rulemaking (NPRMs), public comment periods, and guidance documents Maintain and update legislative and regulatory tracking systems/databases for multiple clients Research & Analysis Draft bill summaries, regulatory analyses, hearing memos, and issue briefs Analyze and report on the potential impact of proposed legislation or regulations on client industries Research legislator background, voting records, committee jurisdiction and policy positions Draft legislation and prepare legal analysis, as requested by clients Client & Lobbyist Support Meet with clients to provide legislative and regulatory briefings and updates Meet with legislators, legislative staff and administration officials on behalf of clients Prepare briefing materials, talking points, and leave-behinds for client meetings and capital/agency visits Develop relationships with key coalition members, identify opportunities for collaboration and synergy in client policy priorities Draft comment letters, testimony, and correspondence to legislators and regulators Testify before legislative committees or regulatory bodies on behalf of clients, as needed Assist in developing advocacy strategies and coalition-building materials Draft client reports summarizing key issues, progress, and other relevant priorities. Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree in political science, Public Policy, Government, Law, Communications, or related field Five years of experience in a legislative office, executive/regulatory agency, trade association, advocacy organization, or lobbying/government affairs or law firm. Strong understanding of the federal and/or state legislative and regulatory process Excellent research and analytical skills Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting to clients and speaking in formal settings (e.g., hearings, briefings) Ability to synthesize complex policy issues into clear, concise materials Attention to detail and strong organizational/project management skills Ability to manage multiple clients’ matters and deadlines simultaneously Preferred Familiarity with state lobbying disclosure requirements Experience with legislative tracking platforms Existing relationships or familiarity with relevant committees, agencies, or policy areas J.D. or graduate degree in public policy is a plus but not required Skills & Attributes Discretion and sound judgment in handling sensitive and confidential client and political information Strong interpersonal skills and professional presence with government officials and clients Adaptability in a fast-moving, deadline-intensive environment Nonpartisan, client-service orientation Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort learning specialized policy-tracking and customer relationship management tools Compensation & Benefits Salary range: $100,000–$250,000, commensurate with experience Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) with firm match Paid time off and firm holidays Professional development and bar/license reimbursement (if applicable) Discretionary bonus. To Apply Please submit a resume and cover letter. Nielsen Merksamer is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, religion, creed, ethnic or national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran or military status, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, domestic partner status, and other categories protected by applicable laws, or in retaliation for opposition to any practices forbidden under this policy.

item.title: U S Congressional Liaison Officer
item.description: U.S. Congressional Liaison Officer Location: Washington, D.C. Work Arrangement: Full-time, on-site Clearance: ACTIVE SECRET CLEARANCE FROM U.S. OR NATO MEMBER NATION REQUIRED Travel: Up to 30 days annually The Opportunity Ironclad Defense Works is seeking a U.S. Congressional Liaison Officer to support NATO Allied Command Transformation in Washington, D.C. This position will serve as ACT’s forward presence on Capitol Hill, helping NATO monitor U.S. legislative developments, build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress and congressional staff, and anticipate political, strategic, and budgetary developments that could affect NATO transformation priorities. This role requires a professional who will combine congressional affairs, government relations, defense policy, and international security expertise with the ability to independently represent NATO ACT across the U.S. legislative and policy community. The candidate must understand the congressional authorization and appropriations process, synthesize complex defense and foreign-policy developments into actionable advice, and establish trusted relationships with senior policymakers and external stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Monitor and analyze the U.S. defense budget process and identify implications for NATO. Track congressional defense reforms and assess their potential impact on NATO transformation. Monitor congressional debates and decisions concerning Ukraine and broader Euro-Atlantic security. Analyze issues related to U.S. force posture in Europe and burden-sharing. Assess political dynamics surrounding defense legislation, including key congressional influencers, priorities, and agendas. Monitor hearings, committee activity, legislation, and other congressional developments relevant to NATO. Develop and maintain professional relationships with Members of Congress and congressional staff. Provide tailored briefings on NATO ACT priorities to legislators, policymakers, and other stakeholders. Plan and conduct informal congressional engagements, meetings, and other relationship-building activities. Coordinate messaging and engagement with U.S. executive agencies, NATO missions, Allied embassies, and other stakeholders. Produce regular reports for SACT and the Political Advisor on congressional trends, risks, and opportunities. Support ACT delegations, SACT visits, Flag Officer engagements, and congressional interactions. Support NATO engagement with Washington-area think tanks, academia, and policy communities. Facilitate ACT participation in hearings, conferences, policy events, and professional networks. Support NATO political-military engagement as directed by the POLAD. Required Qualifications At least two years of experience working with or within the U.S. Congress, particularly on defense, appropriations, or foreign-policy issues. Demonstrated success in a government-relations role, including management of a legislative portfolio and navigation of the congressional process. Strong knowledge of the U.S. congressional authorization and appropriations cycles. Strong expertise in defense policy, international security, and political-military affairs. Demonstrated ability to monitor and interpret complex political, legislative, and budgetary developments and convert them into actionable recommendations. Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with elected officials, policymakers, congressional staff, federal officials, and senior leaders. Experience representing organizational policy positions to Congress, the Executive Branch, think tanks, or comparable external stakeholders. Ability to develop and execute short- and long-term engagement plans supporting organizational priorities. Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain professional relationships across congressional and federal agencies. Ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment while contributing effectively within a broader team. U.S. citizenship and English proficiency. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree or higher in Political Science, International Relations, Economics, Law, or a related discipline. Undergraduate degree combined with substantial congressional staff experience. Familiarity with NATO structures, priorities, capability development, and the Alliance transformation agenda. Previous congressional liaison, legislative affairs, advisory, or diplomatic experience. Previous experience with the U.S. Department of Defense or Department of State. Experience supporting congressional defense committees or appropriations committees. Knowledge of the National Defense Authorization Act, defense appropriations process, and related congressional oversight mechanisms. Existing professional relationships within the congressional defense and foreign-policy community. Experience supporting senior military or diplomatic leaders during congressional engagements. Clearance This position requires an active National SECRET (or higher) security clearance from the U.S. or a NATO member nation. Applicants who do not possess the clearance specified above cannot be considered at this time. Compensation Compensation for this position ranges from $150,000 - $170,000 annually. Final salary will be based on factors such as experience, education, skills, qualifications, location, contract requirements, and overall affordability. Eligible full-time employees may also receive a comprehensive benefits package, including medical and dental insurance, retirement benefits, paid leave, and professional development opportunities. How to Apply Email your resume to [email protected] with the subject line: “U.S. Congressional Liaison Officer – (Your Name) Application” or respond to this job posting via the included web application. Ironclad Defense Works is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

item.title: Campaign Organizer Elect Dan Osborn Flip The Senate
item.description: Campaign Organizer- Nebraska Location and Timeline: We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to begin now and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about Dan Osborn’s run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. Requirements: Valid driver's license and Insurance as well as a verifiable record of safe driving. Must be over 21 (in order to drive the rental car if needed) Must be available full-time. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather thousands of support cards from Dan Osborn supporters. Recruit and train volunteers to talk to voters. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Knock on thousands of doors to educate voters about Dan Osborn and his platform. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training, and developing volunteer leaders in your community to talk to their neighbors and community members about Dan Osborn. Completing your own shifts knocking doors to recruit volunteers and have in depth conversations about Dan Osborn for Senate. Engaging and expanding our support network through developing relationships with community leaders. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Administrative Assistant Center For Faith And Justice Mccourt School Of Public Policy Georgetown University
item.description: Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world. Requirements Job Overview The Administrative Assistant for the Center on Faith and Justice, McCourt School of Public Policy, Georgetown University, will provide high-level administrative support to the Director of the Center on Faith and Justice and assist with the daily operations of the Center. The ideal candidate will be organized, proactive, and skilled in managing logistics, scheduling, and communications. This role is essential to ensuring the smooth functioning of the Center’s activities and the Director’s commitments. The Administrative Assistant provides executive, administrative, and analytical support to the Director in a wide variety of areas including: special projects, teaching and course administration, correspondence, maintenance of the Director’s calendar; planning, coordinating, and executing high-profile events on behalf of the Director; developing, supporting, and maintaining administrative support processes; working closely with, and providing support for, other Center staff; and problem solving for the day-to-day operations of the Center on Faith and Justice. The Administrative Assistant will coordinate activities on behalf of the Director, serve as liaison to senior management across campus, assume primary responsibility for administrative support for the Center, identify issues or problems, prioritize tasks effectively, and work independently with a high level of confidentiality. The Administrative Assistant will also be responsible for assisting with event planning and logistics—both on content as well as administratively. Additional duties include, but are not limited to: Maintain and manage the Director’s calendar, including meetings, speaking engagements and travel arrangements. Draft, review and manage emails, letters and other communication on behalf of the Director. Assist in preparing materials and logistics for speaking events, interviews and other public appearances. Oversee the day-to-day administrative operations, including ordering supplies, managing mail and maintaining office systems. Provide administrative assistance to other staff members as required and coordinate office supply and facilities requests. Handle reimbursements for the Center. Act as the primary point of contact for inquiries directed to the Director and the Center. Assist in updating and maintaining the Center’s digital platform with relevant content. Work Interactions This position reports to the Executive Director of the Center on Faith and Justice, and serves as liaison with University administration, University Deans, senior management, faculty, staff, students, alumni, industry partners and others in the Georgetown community. The position works closely with, and provides support for other staff at the Center on Faith and Justice. The position will oversee the revenue and expenses related to certain projects and events that are funded through RGAs. This position will oversee 1-2 student workers. Requirements and Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in a related field. 0-2 years proven experience in administrative roles, preferably in nonprofit or mission-driven organizations or equivalent combination of education and work experience. Exceptional organizational and multitasking abilities with a keen attention to detail. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency in office software (Google Workspace) and scheduling tools. Experience in event planning and logistics coordination is a plus. Discretion and professionalism in handling confidential information. Interest in or commitment to the mission of the Center on Faith and Justice. Proactive and self-motivated with a problem-solving mindset. Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Strong interpersonal skills with a positive and flexible attitude. A passion for social justice, faith-based initiatives, and the public discourse surrounding these issues is desirable. Experience with social media is preferred. Familiarity with issues at the intersection of faith, justice, religion, politics, and policy. Work Mode Designation This position has been designated as Hybrid. item.title: New York Director Government Affairs
item.description: Overview NRDC (the Natural Resources Defense Council) works to safeguard the Earth, its people, its plants and animals, and the natural systems on which all life depends. NRDC combines the power of more than 3 million members and online activists with the expertise of some 800 policy advocates, lawyers, scientists, and communication experts to confront the climate crisis, protect nature, ensure the rights of all people to clean air, clean water, and healthy communities. As an international nonprofit environmental organization, NRDC is working to address the world’s most urgent environmental challenges, and advance innovative, science-based, and enforceable solutions. Since our founding in 1970, NRDC has helped craft and deliver many of America’s foundational environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act. Today, we continue to lead in advancing and defending strong environmental protections at the local, state, federal and international levels, as well as through the marketplace. Our team works across the United States and around the world, from offices in Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., as well as in Beijing, London, and New Delhi (a subsidiary of NRDC India Pvt. Ltd.). Supported by our members and online activists, NRDC is driving impactful solutions that confront the climate crisis, defend nature and safeguard public health across Asia, Africa, and the Americas. At NRDC, we believe lasting change happens when people bring their talent, passion, and expertise together for a common purpose: to build a cleaner, healthier, and more resilient world. Learn more at nrdc.org NRDC is seeking a New York Director of Government Affairs to work with the Center for Campaigns and Advocacy team in Albany. Position Summary The New York Director of Government Affairs serves as the primary point of contact within NRDC for all state legislative and regulatory work in the state. This position requires collegial work with NRDC staff and collaboration with other organizations to develop and lead coherent strategic advocacy by the New York environmental community. Under guidance from the Eastern Regional Government Affairs Director, the New York Director of Government Affairs leads NRDC’s Albany engagement and coordinates NRDC’s in-state federal advocacy portfolio. The position you are applying for is part of the bargaining unit represented by The Washington Baltimore News Guild (WBNG / The Newsguild-CWA Local 32035 ). Responsibilities To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable a ccommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions : Design and execute proactive and defensive legislative plans, engage on existing or emerging legislation, and lobby relevant state decisionmakers to advance NRDC’s policy objectives . Develop and maintain relationships with elected officials and staff on Committees of Jurisdiction and legislative leadership. Build and maintain relationships with policymakers, regulators, elected officials, and decisionmakers in Albany. Advise on legislative and state budget strategy in consultation with NRDC policy and public affairs staff . Execute and occasionally lead environmental coalitions advocating in Albany. Craft effective messages, prepare coalition letters, and help determine priorities for broader environmental community. Track bills and legislative processes including hearings for all priority legislation across the institution. Attend hearings, provide testimony and integrate relevant NRDC policy experts within NRDC as needed to advance policies throughout legislative and regulatory processes. Provide strategic direction to colleagues across the institution on short-, medium-, and long-term objectives needed to advance NRDC’s institutional goals. Draft and review external communications explaining NRDC’s annual legislative agenda and regulatory priorities. Prepare background briefings and staff trainings regarding New York legislative and regulatory processes, and development of effective advocacy strategies. Hold relationships with New York federal delegation offices and engage with the Regional and Federal Affairs teams within NRDC on federal policy objectives . Collaborate on occasional NRDC engagement on state and local ballot measure campaigns. Coordinate and execute projects as needed with NRDC Action Fund. The above list of duties is not comprehensive but generally demonstrates the types of matters under this position’s responsibility . Other duties may be assigned . Qualifications Requirements Minimum 10 years’ directly related experience, including a minimum of five years leading legislative and/or regulatory work in Albany. Bachelor’s degree in public policy, political science, or relevant field. And/or equivalent education or experience. Skills , Abilities , Competencies Proven track record of moving legislation from policy concept through all stages of the legislative process in Albany. Fluent understanding of how to navigate the legislative and executive branches of New York Government. Government Affairs experience with New York City government is preferred, but not . Extensive network of high-level relationships in New York’s government, political, NGO, and philanthropy landscape. Comfort with and willingness to self-motivate and challenge oneself in a hybrid or remote work environment. Willingness to work strange hours – including nights and weekends – during key junctures in the legislative session. M ust be in Albany 3-4 days a week during the legislative session. Possess the ability to prioritize and respond timely to legislators and their staff, administration officials, donors, affiliates, coalition partners, NRDC staff and the public. Familiarity with managing budgets, including prioritizing and reallocating funds to make the best use of limited resources for strategic purposes. Experience with public speaking on technical and non-technical topics. Proven success in building strong partnerships with national leaders and organizations . Experience in and deep commitment to incorporating and growing the use of justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion principles and practices in strategic goals, work plans, team culture, and operations. Familiarity with and understanding of State and Federal electoral and PAC laws preferred. Experience drafting questionnaires and working candidates through endorsement processes preferred. Experience managing external lobby consultants preferred. Ability to travel to NRDC U.S. based offices, approximately 10-15 % annually Commitment to NRDC’s mission , values , and DEI principles PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position within the described work environment. Frequently : P erform desk-based computer tasks Frequently : A bility to interact and communicate with employees and others as necessary Frequently : Attend planned meetings and collaborate with management and coworkers Occasionally : A bility to attend events and activities in the office or offsite Work is sometimes performed primarily in office . The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in office settings and moderate in other situations . Hours of employment may sometimes require working flexible and/or longer hours, including nights and weekends, when necessitated by projects. The job includes work-related situations such as those involving challenging, important, urgent, time-sensitive, or multiple matters. NRDC is committed to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion, both in our work and in our workplace. We believe that celebrating and actively welcoming diverse voices and perspectives is essential to solving the planet's most pressing environmental problems, and we encourage applications from candidates whose identities have been historically under-represented in the environmental movement. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits , and a supportive working environment. Salary is based on a nonprofit scale and is commensurate with skills and experience. Internal equity will be reviewed and considered to determine a final offer . For this position, the salary range is $150,000 to $180,000 . NRDC operates under a hybrid work model. Employees are required to come to the office 8 days per month. As a science-based organization, NRDC aims to do our part to help contain the COVID-19 public health crisis. For the sake of health, safety, and equity, we ask that people be vaccinated unless they have an approved medical or religious accommodation or other exemption in accordance with state and local law. We consider a person to be vaccinated two weeks after receiving one full course of a CDC-approved vaccine. In accordance with state or local law, new hires will be asked to attest to vaccination, those wishing to do so may request medical or religious accommodations or other exemptions via NRDC Employee Relations. NRDC treats all vaccine-related data
